000ae273-4aa2-5253-90d0-658d62298316.description: Talat Harb founds Bank Misr, an all-Egyptian Bank which finances new industries, Egyptian commercial firms and various projects.

001c8856-52f3-584e-ae67-7431d385a9b0.name: Greece wins Ottoman Empire and Bulgaria
001c8856-52f3-584e-ae67-7431d385a9b0.description: Under the leadership of King Constantine I and Prime Minister Eleftherios Venizelos, Greece defeats the Ottoman Empire and Bulgaria during the Balkan Wars.

0022f256-658f-51eb-901c-eedca76d2b42.description: The Crusaders conquer Palestine with a huge massacre in Jerusalem; the estimated number of the victims is ca 70,000. Major parts of the cities are destroyed. Godfrey de Bouillon is elected as the leader of the Latin Kingdom.

007d5a6b-6ab8-5ca9-a62c-9d6eaf447206.description: The Marinid sultan Abu Inan extends his authority over Constantine, Béjaia and Tunis.

009b8cc1-047c-576e-94f1-54b802648adb.name: Cavour prime minister of the Kingdom of Sardinia
009b8cc1-047c-576e-94f1-54b802648adb.description: Cavour (Camillo Benso, Count of Cavour, 1810–61), the architect of the diplomatic strategies that allowed Italian unification, becomes prime minister of the Kingdom of Sardinia (he will remain prime minister until his death).

00b2b358-d30d-5ce6-a0c9-1a8a80c98be6.name: Wiener Kongress
00b2b358-d30d-5ce6-a0c9-1a8a80c98be6.description: The Wiener Kongress (Congress of Vienna) saw the restoration of the political state (the 1792 Ancien Régime), realignment of the borders, and creation of a loosely arranged German Bund (Federation).

00d80670-8f46-5197-b1d8-ac61843bc10c.description: A severe earthquake damages parts of the Aqsa Mosque and the Holy Sepulchre Church, as well as Umayyad palaces and public buildings all over Palestine.

00f26137-b599-503d-96b8-cc9b88a52cfe.description: Death of Miklós Zrínyi, great Hungarian commander in the Turkish wars. Turks defeated in the Battle of Szentgotthárd but the Habsburgs’ deplorable Peace of Vasvár causes Hungarian revolt.

0122123e-63bc-54b7-b032-d30da0fb5de7.description: The foundation of the Ottoman Empire.

01372f83-ca10-5ef4-866f-abb829d2045a.description: Italy’s first parliament is inaugurated in Turin. Victor Emanuel II, King of Sardinia (1849–61), becomes the first king of Italy (1861–78).

0150d888-aaf3-5a0d-8e08-1bc069c2d2cb.name: The Italian army captures Rome
0150d888-aaf3-5a0d-8e08-1bc069c2d2cb.description: In 1870, taking advantage of French defeat at the hands of Prussia, the Italian army captures Rome, which becomes the capital of Italy. The Pope considers Italian rule on Rome to be illegitimate and bans Catholics from participating in Italian political life. In the following decades the ban is progressively lifted to counter socialist growth.

0195a905-bb4f-5e13-b237-f98ad8774abe.description: Victory of Selim I the Grim over Shah Ismail at the Battle of Çaldıran.

01abf43a-c670-559b-8424-96f9384c2c44.description: Edward the Elder, King of England, wins a decisive victory against the Danes at Tettenhall in Staffordshire and extends his kingdom north to the Humber estuary.

01b6aded-ecb9-54cd-9373-b8298b8164cb.description: The Abbasid Caliph Abu Ja’far al-Mansur (r. 754–75) visits Palestine, stays in Jerusalem and orders a renovation project in the Haram al-Sharif and elsewhere, damaged as a result of the earthquake

01b860d5-66df-5df2-847b-12a9e31906c3.description: Death of Katip Çelebi (1609–57), famous Turkish geographer, historian and bibliographer.

01c4ef6b-4b90-50a4-8386-a6c9459347cd.description: Berber insurrections threaten the Byzantine army, which suffered repeated setbacks.

01ca3cd0-5cf6-5255-80ea-9d687b6979f7.description: Hungarian King Ladislaus Pohrobek takes the Czech throne. Order to evict Jews from royal towns. George of Poděbrady elected Czech king (1485). Attempt to create union of European rulers aiming to avert Turkish expansion, restrict Catholic church hegemony and secure peace.

0200499f-0355-5d46-95d6-be6a10389569.description: Giordano Bruno, philosopher and theologian, is burned at the stake in Rome, condemned by the Church for heresy. His death marks one of the darkest and tragic moments of the Counter-Reformation.

02290e31-334b-5a29-8261-9812e231a56e.description:
Start of the Bourbon dynasty with the coronation of Phillip V.  
Start of the Spanish War of Succession.

024386ec-a697-54b8-a7b3-67bdec18a6ca.description: The Marinid Sultan Abu Yusuf takes Algeciras, Tarifa and Ronda and founds the town of Fez al-Jdid, al-Madina al-Bayda, in Fez.

0280f139-a2db-51a2-ac6e-991e8017c515.description: Mulay Isma‘ïl makes Meknes the capital of the kingdom and starts work on his royal fortress complete with palaces, granaries, lakes and stables. It is reminiscent of the Topkapi Sarayi Citadel in Istanbul.

03283052-9368-563f-8de6-2f6862950274.description: Abbasid revolt in Beja, which quickly spreads to all of al-Gharb.

039f8476-dc69-5a48-9254-5588439d72eb.description: Abu Imran al-Fassi, originally from Fez and celebrated faqih from Ifriqya (Tunisia), where he settled to teach, dies in Kairouan.

03aad4a5-0099-5ec4-a225-d2945a5c6341.description: Karlóca Peace Treaty between the Holy Alliance and the Turks. The Sultan promises not to support Hungarian anti-Habsburg revolts (such as that of Imre Thököly who had earlier lost his freedom fight).

03b3d925-8697-539f-88e3-e3490f56c9f4.name: Istanbul and Izmir occupied
03b3d925-8697-539f-88e3-e3490f56c9f4.description: Allied forces occupy İstanbul (16 March); Greece occupies İzmir (15 May).

03ee068c-399d-542b-a408-f4cf12aab879.description: The Arab conquest of Sicily is complete with the fall of Rometta, the last Byzantine stronghold.

03f89fe3-cf01-58e1-8991-f61209f7a89c.description: Konradin, son of King Konrad IV of the Hohenstaufen Dynasty, is beheaded. This ends the German emperorship in Italy.

03fd0a03-9cc4-529c-98c3-2d1af35bd794.description: Kılıç Arslan moves the capital of the Anatolian Seljuqs to Konya after being defeated by the Crusaders.

0416c65f-724c-5f08-935b-358a5277b79e.description: New Capitulations negotiated by the Marquis of Villeneuve. Rapid expansion of trade with the Ports of the Levant and North Africa.

04182081-b9f4-5a2d-8b3a-b4014646701f.description: Sijilmasa taken by the Rustamids. A century of peace follows in Central Maghreb under the rule of the Kharijites.

04542783-0f79-581a-afc4-9ffd350ba514.name: British Occupation of Egypt
04542783-0f79-581a-afc4-9ffd350ba514.description: Britain also acquires indirect control over Egypt, with an occupying army and control over Egyptian finances and administration. Egyptian tourism flourishes and with it a superficial economic development – an affluent class, construction of railways and building projects. However, European cultural influences in Egypt are mostly French.

0458a9da-8b4d-5ff0-87e0-da901e4ea1ac.description: Wenceslas II crowned King of Bohemia. Minting of Prague kreuzers, the most sought-after European silver currency. Wenceslas crowned King of Poland 1300, of Hungary 1301. The murder of Wenceslas III (1306) ended male line of Przemyslid dynasty.

0468c614-d990-5735-a18a-d05014130495.description: Bilad al-Sham (Syria, Jordan, Palestine) comes under the rule of the Tulunid dynasty; Ahmad ibn Tulun is the founder of this dynasty in Egypt.

058cb8aa-8241-51a9-a850-bd9f4460b50f.description: Fraternal Union. The origination of an independent church picking up the threads of Hussite ideology. War in Moravia. Matthias Corvinus against George of Poděbrady.

05f2113f-d487-5b04-8dac-309357a3c344.description: Svenska Akademien (the Swedish Academy) is founded by King Gustavus III in order to advance the Swedish language and literature. The Academy has also awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature since 1901.

0612710a-5768-5a65-b244-cced6749bea0.description: The Seljuqs take Baghdad and northern Syria. The beginning of the Seljuq sultanate and the revival of Islamic military and urban development along Sunni doctrines.

066dc71a-dabf-545c-a60b-833d19fe67b2.description: Charles I is tried and executed; the Commonwealth, in which England is governed as a republic, is established and lasts until 1660 (it exists in name alone through Cromwell’s Protectorate of 1653–9).

0671960e-152c-59b9-8ba9-e7dc3a5cb490.description: Sulayman Ibn ‘Abd al-Malik, the governor of Palestine, begins to build the city of Ramla as a new administrative centre.

0675ca02-0688-5b4b-9b3e-c117c2452fbe.description: ‘Abdallah the Shi’ite reaches the Kutama tribe.

0711ca7c-865a-5e43-8ffe-55ad0482435e.name: Qawasim lands are divided among his four sons
0711ca7c-865a-5e43-8ffe-55ad0482435e.description: Qawasim lands are divided among the four sons of Sheikh Sultan bin Saqr following his death. The number of Trucial States rises from five to nine.

0724d833-b987-53e8-a245-cc4d0169410e.description: The rise of Zahir ‘Umar in northern Palestine establishes a semi-independent state. During his rule several palaces and castles are established in Galilee. Palestine begins to export cotton in commercial quantities to France.

07364618-fce2-5c2d-97d1-521d4ca75aa3.description: Byzantium puts down the Berber revolt that flared up after local chieftains are murdered by Sergius, Byzantine Governor of Tripoli.

074e50d0-7ea9-595b-942b-0501dcf146f5.description: To support his ailing regime, Charles X prepares an military expedition for the conquest of Algiers, establishing a colony that would eventually encompass all of Algeria.

0790de8f-c0ae-57c1-a116-a3ab57fba788.description: The Government of Ireland Act 1920 (also known as the Fourth Home Rule Bill) partitions Ireland into the independent south and the six counties of the North, which remain part of the United Kingdom.

087950f1-7aba-598e-9cbb-48c720664666.name: Reign of Mulay al-Hasan I
087950f1-7aba-598e-9cbb-48c720664666.description: Reign of Mulay al-Hasan I: Mulay al-Hasan I maintains the political independence of the country. He attempted to adapt the country to its new circumstances and employed a policy of reforms, affecting all areas of political and economic life, to improve the management of public affairs.

088df141-881f-5650-8509-1dde7af54b03.name: Promulgation of the Fundamental Pact
088df141-881f-5650-8509-1dde7af54b03.description: Promulgation of the Fundamental Pact by Muhammad Pasha Bey: a “Declaration of Rights” in 11 points. The pact guarantees Tunisians and also foreigners their civil and political rights, security of persons and properties, equality before the law, etc.

08bdd8d5-6c10-5db7-842c-d43cd59bc83f.description: Crowning of the first Croatian king, Stjepan Držislav (969–97), a member of the Trpimirović Dynasty. The Byzantine Emperor Basil II gave him symbols of royal power.

08c5f629-81da-5c98-a249-ee3df8c2508e.name: Cabralismo - an authoritarian regime ruled by conservative Bernardo Costa Cabral who rehabilitated the 1826 Constitutional Chart.
08c5f629-81da-5c98-a249-ee3df8c2508e.description: The period of Cabralismo, an authoritarian regime ruled by conservative Bernardo Costa Cabral who rehabilitates the 1826 Constitutional Charter but promoting the public infrastructures and fiscal code revision. Upper middle class and aristocracy regain state control and former privileges. Popular rebellions lead to the fall of his government.

08d3b28a-cbe0-5448-a40c-0fc8b05d11d9.description: The Swedish general Königsmarck sacks the city of Prague and carries off a substantial booty to Sweden. In the same year the Peace of Westphalia finally puts an end to the Thirty Years War.

0938b094-9d19-5539-847a-deaa3b19396c.description: Military disaster at Annual in northeastern Morocco during the African conflict.

093ad85b-36a2-56f3-9f2f-c1793233d4d6.description: The Ayyubid army leader Usama bin Mungidh erects Ajlun castle to counter the Crusader castle of Belvoir (Kawkab al-Hawa) to the west. In August of this year the Ayyubids besiege Karak Castle under the leadership of Salah al-Din (Saladin) the dynasty’s founder.

0948125d-276f-50a5-87be-a47f18ec6b58.description: The Commune of Rome is born, an expression of the nascent communal civility that will have a profound effect on Italian cultural identity.

096b59db-802d-5555-9934-ec8f40f20346.description: Henry V invades France as part of the Hundred Years’ War (1337–1453) and defeats the French at Agincourt despite being considerably outnumbered.

097de22b-b2d5-5fc3-9e50-26f26064e7d6.description: Sultan Abu Yusuf orders the construction of a new town at Algeciras.

09a9fe71-8e43-5d8f-bcc0-689b8ac5f38e.description: On 25 April, at San Remo the United Nations imposes a British mandate on Jordan, Palestine and Iraq.

0a80a03a-bbeb-5b69-b56e-02c5135daf25.name: Abolition and extermination of the Janissary Corps
0a80a03a-bbeb-5b69-b56e-02c5135daf25.description: 15–17 June: The abolition and extermination of the Janissary corps (the so-called Auspicious Incident) in İstanbul by troops loyal to Sultan Mahmud II. This act provides the conditions for institutional modernisation.

0ac12064-9012-5038-b235-781a1675ef56.description: In Torgau in Saxonia the first German opera ‘Dafne’ composed by Heinrich Schütz (1595–1672) is first performed.

0b9d66a6-fdc2-5392-96bc-5d5194ccdb77.description: Prophet Muhammad sends a letter to Cyrus, the Byzantine Patriarch of Alexandria and ruler of Egypt, inviting him to accept Islam. Cyrus sends gifts to the Prophet in answer, together with two sisters from Upper Egypt. The Prophet married one of them, called Maria the Copt. She bore him his only son, who died in boyhood.

0bbef6a5-14bb-5277-b059-3fb2f1d42cd7.description: The naturalist Charles Darwin publishes The Origin of Species, setting out his evidence for the development of new creatures through the process of natural selection.

0c142f63-19e1-586e-bd42-9a313543f63f.description: King John Balliol of Scotland establishes a mutual defence treaty, the ‘Auld Alliance’, between Scotland and France, directed against the English.

0c16ddc8-4b72-5640-a182-52ff75fa9b1e.description: The Hungarian Diet accepts the Habsburgs’ female succession. Introduction of a Newcomen-type steam machine, the first in continental Europe, in Újbánya (Königsberg; today: Nová Baňa, Slovakia).

0c9c6a2c-5309-550f-9f89-8d04b23940b9.description: Arwad Island is the last Crusader position in Syria to be repossessed by the Muslims.

0cd237fb-4c85-53e3-9a45-33476737ed30.description: The Mamluk Sultan al-Zahir Baybars captures Karak castle from the Ayyubids, putting an end to Ayyubid rule there; he rebuilt some of its towers and transferred his wealth to it.

0d1945ac-4fcc-5486-b818-17a76986f59d.name: Rebel clans allied to Sharif Hussein attacked Jiddah
0d1945ac-4fcc-5486-b818-17a76986f59d.description: Rebel clans allied to Sharif Husayn attack Jeddah (Jidda) and other seaports along the Arabian coast of the Red Sea.

0d316bf4-dace-54b4-b01c-4ebad06ad7a4.description: First regular Ottoman ambassador in Europe (London).

0d4c6b81-0ba3-581a-ba40-c51acba9672b.description: The Danube’s great flood destroys a huge part of Pest. Contract signed to build the first permanent bridge (today: Széchenyi Lánchíd) between Buda and Pest initiated by Count István Széchenyi.

0db574bc-e7a4-5ec9-a8f0-13f291ea264f.description: The Battle of Kösedağ and the invasion of Anatolia by the Mongols.

0dbef608-f76a-5bbf-b4a4-4896564ff2b0.description: First war of independence: Charles Albert of Savoy, King of Sardinia (1831–49) leads a coalition of Italian states to drive the Austrians from the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia.

0dc18487-63ca-5bca-833e-1deec0c2fc99.name: Contesting the union of Transilvania with Hungary
0dc18487-63ca-5bca-833e-1deec0c2fc99.description: In 1892 a delegation of 237 Romanians sends Emperor Franz Joseph a Memorandum protesting against the discriminatory effects of the union of Transylvania with Hungary (1867). In 1893 the signatories of the petition are sent for trial at the end of which, in May 1894, they are sentenced to prison. However, in 1895 the Emperor amnesties them.

0dd31216-4bae-5058-8390-89942d202c20.description: The Nibelungenlied is written down. During the Age of Chivalry numerous texts, ballads and songs were written by Minnesänger singers such as medieval lyricist Walter von der Vogelweide (c.1170–c.1230).

0e46db9d-a4fd-5082-8c26-25d11901cbed.description: The Crusaders occupy Jordan and Palestine during their first campaign to the area until 1187.

0e492afd-a496-5214-be48-1845eee3182d.description: The French occupy the lands of the Papal States and proclaim the Roman Republic.

0e79de47-da1b-53f9-8eac-fd97e6187a3e.description: The Fatimids conquer Palestine, annexing it to Egypt.

0e8b123d-17ff-56ae-bf1b-5eb48430f904.name: Romania declares war on Austria
0e8b123d-17ff-56ae-bf1b-5eb48430f904.description: Romania declares war on the Central Powers: Germany, Austria and Bulgaria.

0e9b8eb8-e957-5457-940d-eed66f32c54c.description: The Convention Parliament restores Charles II to the English throne; the Indemnity Act pardons all except those who had signed Charles I’s death warrant, and they are hung, drawn and quartered.

0ea127ca-a246-5a36-85a6-91f3c218daf8.description: Ragusa falls into the hands of Lajos (Louis) I (the Great). During Medieval times Hungary was its most extensive under his rule. Compilation of a Hungarian chronicle, the Képes Krónika (Illustrated Chronicle).

0ea6dfd1-d6f1-5b9a-83da-258f2b054093.description: Stockholm, Sweden’s capital today is founded by Birger Jarl.

0ebf0190-8081-5d56-b08d-e6f6303dbcbe.description: Uppsala University is founded. It is the oldest university in Scandinavia and still one of Sweden’s most renowned universities. Uppsala is located about 80 km north of the capital Stockholm.

0ef544c2-60c5-52ba-856a-222b4ea68b58.description: Birth in Mecca of Prophet Muhammad from the tribe of Quraysh.

0f0e330c-ea2b-5d7f-a70b-7cb63b7218ff.description: The Almoravid amir Yusuf ibn Tashufin wins the Battle of Zallaca near to Badajoz and mints a gold coin, known as the maravedis in the Christian West.

0f13e13f-532c-5c56-a15a-0f0dc5ac7378.description: The Crusaders take Antioch in June after a nine-month siege, founding the first Crusader state in the Levant.

0f189c19-8d0e-5f2c-af07-5db542c81285.description: The conquest of Constantinople (Istanbul) by Mehmed II which brings the Eastern Roman Empire (Byzantine Empire) to an end.

0f51abf5-c8b2-569d-b23d-afe714bff765.description: Hus burned at the stake at the assembly of the Council of Constance. Struggles between Catholics and Utraquists (“heretics”). Crusades, plundering of monasteries and churches, iconoclasm.

0f5acb2c-7e7f-51ea-8a8b-9e0b1503a5d8.description: The first diplomatic agreement of the Croats with the Holy See. They made an agreement with Pope Agaton by which they agreed not to start wars against neighbouring Christian states.

0f5da38b-dc05-5751-b40d-56d8ee6e5800.description: End of the First Empire. Violence of the White Terror (massacre of Mamluks in Marseille who had come from Egypt with Bonaparte). Acceptance of a constitutional charter by the instigators of the Restoration.

0f64fc28-ee1c-568d-a632-f5f818f7810b.description: Lorenzo de’Medici the Magnificent (1469–92) rules Florence. Under his control, Florence becomes the driving force behind Italian art.

0f7bab5a-5886-5e48-9639-4d8ef95478b5.name: Treaty of Maritime Peace in Perpetuity
0f7bab5a-5886-5e48-9639-4d8ef95478b5.description: A Treaty of Maritime Peace in Perpetuity is concluded between Britain and the Trucial Coast rulers. Britain assumes the right to police maritime peace and commits to protecting the sheikhdoms from external interference and attack.

0fb14610-e011-5b64-9a22-ae3cdae6a774.description: Al-Ashraf Khalil defeats the Crusaders who retreat to Cyprus. He annexes the city of Acre in Palestine.

0fdd53a2-dd15-5287-9b24-e77691cfea02.description: Estates defeated at Battle of White Mountain resulting in mass punishment and persecution. Uprising of the Wallachians (Carpathian pastoral culture). Charles University made over to the Jesuits.

103bfb7f-3909-5a55-9170-c2bc8871d5a9.description: Golden Bull of Sicily: Roman King Friedrich II defines the relationship between Czech kings and the Holy Roman Empire. The Czech king becomes one of seven electors privileged to elect the Roman king.

10b1382a-ff42-52fc-9d16-2a0842cd92b3.description: Black Death (the plague) spreads throughout the British Isles from the south coast, killing between one-third and a half of the population.

10bf9640-3d11-572b-9725-3e5d4d8eccb4.name: Mulay Sulayman
10bf9640-3d11-572b-9725-3e5d4d8eccb4.description: At the beginning of his reign, Mulay Sulayman adopts a policy to isolate the country, excluding contact with the European and even Turkish worlds. He leant on the national brotherhoods and maintained mediaeval, feudal ways of life that eschewed Western technical innovations which he deemed to be dangerous. He nonetheless signed agreements with Portugal in 1823, England in 1824 and France in 1825, under pressure to change his position on account of the international situation. During the first third of the 19th century, Morocco was subject to systematic pressure from rapidly expanding European imperialism.

10f7cc32-ef14-59ea-a170-1accfa0ed6a8.name: The Valençay Treaty
10f7cc32-ef14-59ea-a170-1accfa0ed6a8.description: The Valençay Treaty ends the war between Spain and France. Return of King Fernando VII and absolutist restoration.

110abf60-df8a-5021-a435-e437a19eff34.description:
King Faisal enters Damascus, celebrating the first Arab government.  
The French army occupies the Syrian coast (1919).  
King Faisal is expelled by the French, after which he becomes king of Iraq.

1114a73b-48bc-5cec-82c4-a1738c06305b.name: First Constitution of Serbia
1114a73b-48bc-5cec-82c4-a1738c06305b.description: The First Constitution of the Principality of Serbia (the Candlemas Constitution) is prompted by the autocratic rule of Miloš Obrenović, founder of the Obrenović Dynasty and Serbian Prince (1815–39; 1858–60). It is signed in 1835 in the city of Kragujevac, with the intention to limit the absolute power of Miloš, but under pressure from the *Porte* (Turkish Government), Austria and Russia the Constitution is abolished as early as the following year.

11b93b11-084a-5942-9d1d-2aabba0f5a0c.description: The death of Frederick Barbarossa in the river of Calycadmus.

120e2be4-fbf3-5705-ab07-e367fb80ddf4.name: The German National Assembly approves the Constitution of the German Empire
120e2be4-fbf3-5705-ab07-e367fb80ddf4.description: The German National Assembly approves the Constitution of the German Empire.

1233e1c8-d1a4-58d8-8d9f-22763c0fea1e.description: Highlights of the Czech radical baroque: construction of Church of St. Nicholas, Prague, began (architect K. Dienzenhofer). Charles Bridge embellished with statues by M. B. Braun and F. Brokof.

1246abcf-0fc6-580d-9327-0ad802135949.name: Martyrs Square
1246abcf-0fc6-580d-9327-0ad802135949.description: Turkish authorities publicly execute 21 Syrians and Lebanese in Damascus and Beirut, respectively, for alleged anti-Turkish activities; the place of execution in each city will be renamed Martyrs' Square.

125a41da-1f4c-5bb3-9a7b-119a5f7666f4.description: Battle of Ayacucho and definitive loss of the territories in continental America.

128e76da-afcc-5b89-9153-25eec0ade885.description: Duke Branimir becomes Banus of Croatia and breaks up with Constantinople. Pope John VIII gave his blessing to the duke and the whole Croatian people, as he informed Branimir in his letters.

129e1619-237c-5252-9906-6ce2910d2524.description: The Zirid princes share out the kingdom of Ifriqiya and the fortress of the Bani Hammad.

12eddebb-3b1f-53c0-8139-0b4499eeecf0.description: Sulayman the Magnificent dies on his last expedition to the fort of Szigetvar on the Hungarian border and Selim II ascends the throne.

1315fea9-0b32-50d4-8167-65c27887ac55.name: Irish Free State
1315fea9-0b32-50d4-8167-65c27887ac55.description: Of the 32 counties of Ireland, twenty-six southern counties vote to secede from the United Kingdom to become the Irish Free State.

133fe939-8db6-5b41-902c-d3dc5bc831e0.description: Louis IX is captured by the Ayyubid army in Mansourah and later released for a ransom of 100,000 dinars. Al-Salih Ayyub dies and is succeeded by his son Turan Shah who shatters the Crusader army attacking the Delta.

13a93ace-6a19-5374-9786-7b306ea3d7f4.description: The defeat of Napoleon Bonaparte at Waterloo by the United Kingdom, Prussia, Austria and Russia marks the end of the Napoleonic Wars and peace is established in Europe at the Congress of Vienna.

13c15681-862c-52cb-b9a5-7003467a77ae.description: The powers of the Almohads declines.

13dac36b-9fbb-5fa2-8583-815b08f81f34.name: German warships shell Russian ports
13dac36b-9fbb-5fa2-8583-815b08f81f34.description: 29 October: German warships, officially designated as Ottoman vessels, shell Russian Black Sea ports, an action that leads the Ottoman Empire to enter World War I.

13e73776-c4fc-5ef3-a4b7-9cf5eeade4e2.description: On 7 March Amir Faysal, the son of Sharif Husayn, is made king of Greater Syria by the Syrian National Congress. The administrative structure of this kingdom consists of eight provinces, three of them in Jordan.

147cd727-f65b-557a-ba84-e1a5e73b486e.description: Beginning of the Western Schism, which will divide the Christian Church and see two different popes on the papal seat.

14caae37-a082-5320-b2c6-8d3c41706f49.description: Charlemagne (800–14) becomes the Emperor of Rome and the Holy Roman Empire is born.

152c36c0-d0a5-53f3-aaa1-1679e8b8f8d0.description: Mutiny of Aranjuez and abdication of Charles IV in favour of his son Ferdinand VII. Abdications of Bayonne. Joseph Bonaparte becomes King of Spain. Popular uprising in Madrid on 2 May and start of the War of Independence against the French occupiers (1808–13).

153f92ad-21a5-5743-b4bb-1ac74cad8c8a.description: Charles Martel, son of Pippin of Herstal, stops the Muslims of ‘Abd al-Rahman who had raided as far as Poitiers, and subsequently extends his rule over Aquitaine and Provence.

15505c68-ae85-5788-8b44-3a5ad2cc6bcd.description: Ahmad Ibn Tulun rules independently from the Abbasid Caliphate and founds al-Qatai city, the third Islamic capital of Egypt.

156d8464-f294-5c24-bab6-fe3806d2a9d0.description: Frequent incursions by Portuguese, French, Spanish and Italian fleets in the ports of Central Maghreb: Honain, Oran, Algiers and Béjaia.

157c2813-3d90-50aa-a7d3-6fe4e265eb85.description: The Ayyubids capture the Crusader castles of Karak and Shawbak, ending the Crusaders’ rule in Jordan.

158eb698-9413-5fa7-86d3-311318547a6f.description: The warship Wasa sinks in Stockholm on her maiden voyage. The ship was discovered and salvaged in 1956, and is now exhibited in Stockholm.

15ef6e9b-2925-5093-a5e2-9edeabc2b1c4.description: French military victories are marked in particular by Bonaparte’s success in Italy. Under the Directoire, he prepares an expeditionary force for Egypt, which is accompanied by a team of experts intended to bring modern techniques and institutions to the country. The French are stalled in Egypt and leave the country in 1801.

15efcbdb-4dcb-5878-9a4c-13426648045a.description: The Young Turks Revolution overthrows Sultan Abdulhamid II. The Second Constitutional Period begins.

16bfa79f-50f4-5128-90a4-c0f159b646ee.description: Death of Louis IX at the gates of Tunis during the Eighth Crusade following an initial defeat in Egypt (Seventh Crusade). Louis IX will be canonised in 1297.

16d29a40-f9f8-52a9-bdaf-4de60397ce72.description: The second Crusade arrives in Syria, led by Louis VII of France and Conrad III of Germany, besieging Damascus for four days, but failing to conquer it.

16e436e2-76c7-53af-a380-e4ad7f0d6779.name: Louis Philippe becomes king
16e436e2-76c7-53af-a380-e4ad7f0d6779.description: The July Monarchy: Louis-Philippe becomes “Citizen-King”, and economic growth is joined by increased poverty.

175052f1-afe4-51a6-9bfd-e303319a98f9.description: Pippin the Younger, son of Charles Martel, is proclaimed King of the Franks and turns his attention to the south. He leads expeditions against the Lombards, recovers Narbonne from the Muslims and helps to revitalise trade in the Mediterranean.

17e57512-3af9-56ad-bf1e-82fc5f7a325e.description: Economic and religious interaction between Arabia and the Fertile Crescent as Muhammad joins his uncle on mercantile travel to Syria, where he meets the monk Bahira in Bosra.

18637c69-3047-5e90-8cf2-09d7de71678a.description: Beylik of Salah Bey at Constantine. Renovation of the town and construction of el-Kantara bridge.

186ea0b3-28bc-5331-86e0-704c5ef7795b.name: After the defeat of the Al Qawasim by the British
186ea0b3-28bc-5331-86e0-704c5ef7795b.description: After the defeat of the Qawasim by the British, a British Residency is established at Bushire on the Persian littoral to represent Britain’s political, economic and military interests there. Shortly after, a “Native Agent” is based in Sharjah as his representative. Native agents were generally non-Arab but Arabic-speaking Muslims from the Indian subcontinent or the Persian littoral of the Gulf, chosen for their loyalty to Britain and their in-depth local and regional knowledge. Their task was to monitor activities on the Trucial Coast and liaise with local powers on Britain’s behalf.

1884ecf3-5742-5cdc-85e9-3961fdd618ba.description: Scots under Robert Bruce (Robert I) comprehensively defeat the invading English army at the Battle of Bannockburn, re-establishing Scotland’s independence.

18a3d60f-dabd-5abb-9cbc-8f4adfd349e8.description: The British Army suppresses the Easter Rising, a rebellion in Dublin designed to force Ireland’s independence from Great Britain, and its leaders are executed.

18b93719-ae33-55e3-a4bd-640d2059e998.name: Muhammad Sadiq Bey promulgates a constitution
18b93719-ae33-55e3-a4bd-640d2059e998.description: Muhammad Sadiq Bey promulgates a constitution limiting his powers. Tunisia’s first constitution is the culmination of the reformist policies of the 19th-century Husaynid beys.

18d2bdda-f67c-5529-92cd-ed765d901ec3.description: The Hungarian Jacobin Conspiracy’s members are executed or imprisoned. Archduke Josef becomes the new Hungarian Palatine. Pál Kitaibel invents a vacuum-filtering process.

18f48aaf-32b5-5177-bb0d-6bed68c2d15c.description: Largest uprising of the serfs. Patents of King Leopold I include: corvée patent, legalisation of the Evangelical church (1691). The first textile manufactories.

1962e747-521f-5cfa-a679-5538e2d26bce.description: Foundation of the town of Mahdia, capital of the Fatimids.

1986b3e4-b784-5a0c-985e-b3ccf9fe26b3.description: A military expedition to Jordan and Palestine is mounted by Ibrahim Pasha, son of Muhammad ‘Ali Pasha of Egypt, who controlled the whole area for ten years.

198d4297-6a40-5ac7-b16c-f5bc23676c10.description: Emperor Rudolph II transfers his court to Prague, which became a major European centre of politics, science and arts (de Brahe, Kepler). The first public autopsy (Ján Jesenský, 1600).

1a2f1bf5-03f4-5776-b538-6c8a51882add.name: Treaty of Erzurum
1a2f1bf5-03f4-5776-b538-6c8a51882add.description: 28 July: Treaty of Erzurum, which ends the Ottoman–Iranian war and restores the previous border.

1a50617c-4ad6-5dce-adac-8976cf87e0c3.description: Jerusalem is surrendered by the Patriarch Sophronius to ‘Umar Ibn al-Khattab. The Plaza of the Haram al-Sharif is cleaned and prepared for a modest wooden structure. It will take the Muslim armies another ten years to control the rest of Palestine.

1a506441-db7f-5726-acfc-932b10d3a7b1.description: Al-Mahdi's son, Abbasid Caliph Harun al-Rashid, the protagonist of many tales in the ‘1001 nights’, moves his court to al-Raqqa, which becomes the ‘Abbasid capital for the next 12 years.

1a8d42c0-fd99-58bb-a840-10b2be8dc7a9.description: In the Treaty of Verdun the Frankish Empire is divided into three separate parts called West-, Middle- and East Francia. The Germanic Empire is called the Holy Roman Empire of the German Nation.

1ab81572-3f54-5b35-99a1-f877dcff13eb.name: Almost uninterrupted rule by Giovanni Giolitti
1ab81572-3f54-5b35-99a1-f877dcff13eb.description: Almost uninterrupted rule by Giovanni Giolitti, who allows more freedom of action to trade unions, introduces some social reforms and makes some openings for Socialists and Catholics.

1abad8aa-fe77-59c3-8da6-f5cc736a354d.name: First Balkan War
1abad8aa-fe77-59c3-8da6-f5cc736a354d.description: The First Balkan War begins in October 1912 between Serbia, Bulgaria, Greece, Montenegro and the Ottoman Empire; Montenegro is accused of igniting it by attacking Skadar. At the request of Turkey, an armistice is concluded in December 1912. Negotiations in London fail and the war continues into 1913. A Peace Treaty is signed in London in May 1913. Turkey surrenders all territories west of the Enos-Midija. The Serbian Navy withdraws from the sea; in November 1912, Albania is formed due to Austrian pressure.

1adf1060-6f94-584f-acd2-4bbe43e3fbbe.name: The Queen Regent, María Cristina, is forced to reinstate the 1812
1adf1060-6f94-584f-acd2-4bbe43e3fbbe.description: The Queen Regent, María Cristina, is forced to reinstate the 1812 Constitution after a military coup (*pronunciamiento*) in order to get support from the liberals in the First Carlist War. Under the Desamortización de Mendizábal Church properties are disentailed to fund the war. General Espartero takes over the Regency from the Queen in 1841.

1b07e539-903c-5a05-b20b-eb21d9f608de.description: Abu al-Alaa al-Ma'arri, blind Syrian poet, dies. His most famous literary work, Risalat al-Ghufran (Letter of Forgiveness), inspires Dante Alighieri’s Divine Comedy three centuries later.

1c3233e2-5df3-5ec8-9e6f-4f6649c63ddc.description: The assasination of Austria’s crown prince leads to the beginning of the First World War in which Germany fights on the sides of the Central Powers against the Allied Powers.

1c856a62-bfb9-5e4e-920b-d5a36439ae6f.description: Council of Burgos abolishes the Mozarabic rite in favour of the Roman rite.

1ca0bf3c-392f-5a57-b07d-4bb268d08b2c.description: The coronation of the last Hungarian royal couple, Charles IV and Zita. Romania declares war on Hungary and enters Transylvania. The Allies reject the peace note of the Central Powers.

1cb440c0-2d91-5e8e-80da-66e695173cb5.description: The Lombards officially convert to Catholicism, a process that began with the work of Gregory the Great.

1cca0a62-f5d5-504c-aa2a-4dc46801148f.description: The Sassanian invasion of Syria (Bilad al-Sham) begins under the  leadership of Shahrbaraz, causing the destruction of many cities.

1d082139-5292-56e4-aac4-022bb99ea92a.description: The first parliament  (Meclis-i Mebusan) is established.

1d63bf29-4526-5efc-afcd-23dc9e584090.description: Death of the great geographer al-Hassan al-Wazzan (Leo Africanus), whose works, written in Latin, illuminated many aspects of civilisation in the Maghreb.

1db05db3-c34d-56cf-9db2-7bea8b690a56.description: Publication of *Ratio Educationis*, Maria Theresia’s school reform. The Nagyszombat University (Tyrnau; today: Trnava, Slovakia), founded by Bishop Péter Pázmány in 1635, moves to Buda.

1dcea065-7a87-5568-818f-1b90906eb3b2.description: Third war of independence: Italy succeeds in freeing the Veneto region from Austrian control.

1dfb515f-0c54-5471-b716-2910b7723024.description: The crisis that besets all of the countries at war in Russia takes the form of a genuine revolution whose repercussions will be felt far beyond its borders.

1e25c1a1-f5e8-5679-972d-8d4abe2b9708.description: Birth of Johann Sebastian Bach (1685–1750), who is seen as one of the foremost composers of concertos, cantatas and oratorios in the Western tonal tradition.

1eb96ee0-fce4-5fe8-af8b-27bda3c4ebef.description: Coup d’etat by Louis Napoleon, who becomes emperor as Napoleon III. He takes France to war in the Crimea alongside England. The Treaty of Paris establishes the existence of an independent Romanian state.

1ec47d0a-c730-5a8b-9afe-827478896737.description: The first post office is founded in Irbid city during Ottoman rule under Sultan ‘Abd al Hamid II, who wanted to have telegraph offices in the empire.

1efa4fa9-de8d-5c0a-a288-28d272fc6adf.name: Restoration of the monarchy
1efa4fa9-de8d-5c0a-a288-28d272fc6adf.description: Restoration of the monarchy. A military uprising under General Martínez Campos in Sagunto against the Republic returns the throne to the Bourbon Dynasty, with Alfonso XII (son of Isabel II) as King.

1f0e0f75-5d99-5efc-a6ba-2180bdcb726c.name: Madrid Conference
1f0e0f75-5d99-5efc-a6ba-2180bdcb726c.description: The intention of the 1880 Madrid Conference, reflected in the agreements signed by Morocco under the reign of Mulay al-Hasan I and the countries of Europe, is to enhance the benefits of reform in Morocco and to provide a legal and regulatory framework for Mulay al-Hasan I. Following these agreements, the European countries won the right to own land and assets throughout Morocco. The agreements were the result of globalisation of Moroccan business.

1f15d9fb-a195-5f6b-9f40-b3f1c20345ac.description: The naval battle of Preveza off the Adriatic coast. Barbarossa defeats Genoese admiral Andrea Doria.

1faaca18-8185-5001-83b0-eb570c68caa3.description: England’s Parliament issues the Bill of Rights, establishing a constitutional monarchy in England and barring Roman Catholics from the throne.

1fbf7f36-ff20-50d7-9aa7-e8cb6774fb4a.description: V. M. Kramerius publishes the first Czech revival newspaper, the first mass reading material in the Czech language in 170 years.

1ffa7658-10ce-552e-9a0b-b2ba7645c278.description: Revolution against British occupation led by Saad Zaghloul in which all classes of society join.

201c3e10-5a1e-511f-85ce-489ab781703a.description: The Domesday Book is completed. A survey of every English county south of the rivers Ribble and Tees, it was commissioned by William I at Christmas 1085 to enable him to tax his landowning subjects.

20a1d615-9888-5343-8c3e-bf6100e8fdb1.description: Building of St Vitus Cathedral at Prague Castle commenced (master builder: Matthias of Arras, followed by Peter Parler). Foundation of Prague archbishopric.

20ceb169-43cb-54ed-93ea-681457da361b.description: Great victories over Turks in north Croatia. The commanders of the victorious army were Banus Nikola Erdödy, General Leslie and Johann Joseph Herberstein.

20e3f2a9-16c9-5a27-a7ca-79342c290b07.description: War with the USA. Loss of the last overseas territories (Cuba, Puerto Rico and Philippines).

2100c09e-81da-5cf9-9bc3-e90abebe3635.description: Sultan Sidi Muhammad Ibn ‘Abdallah succeeds his father, opens up trading relations with Europe and undertakes a huge programme of construction and fortification of the Atlantic towns.

213a880a-9ea7-5e70-9c3b-bf3fd002c1da.name: The French expedition to Algeria
213a880a-9ea7-5e70-9c3b-bf3fd002c1da.description: The French expedition to Algeria arouses strong emotions in Morocco. It was understood to be a direct threat, in particular following incursions by French troops into eastern Morocco. Mulay ‘Abd al-Rahman accepted the call of the people of Tlemcen and gave his support to the religious and military leader ‘Abd al-Qadir.

21c22d2f-6ed1-5ec0-8eac-e1d12598e587.description: Famous Turkish traveller Evliya Çelebi (1611–82) was born in Istanbul.

21c23f70-444b-57fe-b454-dcb0dce6dd69.description: Establishment of the Egyptian Federation of Industries.Britain grants Egypt autonomous rule. Sultan Fouad takes the title of King.

21cce328-4c0c-54bc-9dba-0ae3df9eb063.description: King Ferdinand I promulgates the Sesmaria law on agriculture.

22648a84-1ebd-59b2-86ca-54573888a8e4.description: Michelangelo finishes the fresco Last Judgement in the Sistine Chapel.

229112dd-6bd9-56e0-926a-cc1c945f41e6.description: Egypt comes under the control of the Abbasid Caliphate and al-Askar, the second Islamic capital of Egypt, is founded. Marwan ibn Muhammad, the last Umayyad Caliph in the East, is murdered in Abu Seir, Fayyum, west of the Delta.

22a3799f-f1a9-5a4c-a5f4-276e3a29522a.description: Discovery of the Cabo Verde archipelago.

22ae8d63-0806-559a-b713-b15cb56423a6.description: King Konrad I (911–18) of the Conradine Dynasty becomes king.

22b37828-9479-5d5b-96eb-d2063238fae1.description: The Hanseatic League, an alliance of trading guilds from the cities of Lübeck, Hamburg, Wismar and Rostock is officially founded.

22b932b5-680c-554f-a87a-6b93adc2a209.name: Treaty of Sèvres and the Arab Revolt
22b932b5-680c-554f-a87a-6b93adc2a209.description: Squabbling among the allies (those that had betrayed the Arab Revolution) delays the signing of the Peace Treaty with the Ottomans, which is being negotiated at Sèvres in France up until 10 August 1920. The Treaty confirmed French and British possession of Syria, Lebanon, Palestine, Jordan and Iraq in the guise of League of Nations mandates. Sharif Husayn ibn ‘Ali is rewarded for his leadership of the Arab Revolt with international recognition of the Hijaz as an independent kingdom.

22c92de3-b426-5587-b678-4e9a4377b322.description: Trianon Peace Treaty: Hungary loses two-thirds of its territory – 190,000 square km – (Transylvania, the Uplands, part of Western, Eastern and Southern Hungary).

2305d7b6-00ab-52e6-8465-2a991867a6f4.name: Abdication of Napoleon I
2305d7b6-00ab-52e6-8465-2a991867a6f4.description: Abdication of Napoleon I on 6 April sees the end of the First French Empire (1804–14).

23415d77-cbe0-5611-9250-b42909c13baf.name: Curzon’s tour of the Gulf
23415d77-cbe0-5611-9250-b42909c13baf.description: The British Viceroy, Lord Curzon, visits the sheikhdoms of the Gulf to confirm treaties of protection that exclude other European powers. Iraq and Arabia fall under a British- Indian sphere of influence with the Indian rupee as the principal currency. Curzon’s policy lasts until 1970.

2356e8e4-2b1f-58d9-aba5-abed93fc65a0.description: The Marinid sultan Abu Ya’qub lays siege to Tlemcen for seven years.

237258a4-99c7-55b3-bbdd-5ba73ea164c3.description: Lisbon earthquake. Reconstruction of the city begins under the auspices of the Prime Minister, the Marquis of Pombal.

239ff1b5-450c-5354-b43c-92df405718b8.description: Napoleon incorporates Dalmatia, Dubrovnik and western Croatia as the French Illyrian Provinces. France stimulated agriculture and commerce in the provinces and fought piracy.

244c912b-9393-598d-b577-23a3ebd86437.description: On 17 June in this year, in the Swedish town of Kalmar, the three Nordic countries Denmark, Norway and Sweden are united under the Danish Monarch, Queen Margarethe. For Sweden this loss of independence and Danish sovereignty will last 125 years.

246fac45-2103-5efc-93ef-b65ee8b5167c.description: Nur al-Din, son of Zangi, takes control of Damascus and establishes it as a capital city. It becomes the new cultural, economic, religious, political and educational hub of the Islamic world at large, attracting many scholars.

2476a503-db5c-5c24-b19c-5d5859b96b05.name: The right to vote is extended
2476a503-db5c-5c24-b19c-5d5859b96b05.description: The right to vote is extended to all men above the age of 30 (or aged 21 if they completed primary school). The Pope allows Catholics to vote.

24ed5e53-2968-5136-bffb-ec109f9d11f7.name: Creation of the first Romanian political parties
24ed5e53-2968-5136-bffb-ec109f9d11f7.description: Creation of the first Romanian political parties: the Liberal Party (1875), the Conservative Party (1880), the Radical-Democratic Party (1888), and the Social-Democratic Party of Romanian Labourers (1893).

24f27e64-f75c-5d52-97a1-b1d4c22c4e5b.description: Ladislas of Naples, Croat king and a claimant to the Hungarian throne as King Ladislav of Anjou, sells Dalmatia to the Venetians for 100,000 ducats. By 1420 Venice controlled all of Dalmatia except for Dubrovnik.

250fca80-30bb-5744-8a3d-b19026ef60d8.description: Egypt, Jerusalem and Damascus come under the rule of the Persian Emperor Xerxes II.

251dbd30-c263-51b4-af91-b2e3e1685fe3.description: Mary, Queen of Scots, abdicates Scotland’s throne and her one-year-old son James VI becomes King of Scotland; Mary is executed in 1587 for plotting to kill Elizabeth I.

256a53ec-978d-5e74-b834-40234b8fa7fe.description: The Swedish East India Company is founded for trading in the Far East.

256e947f-df5e-5b8d-9c3e-9002b6c85a2b.description: On 4 September the Battle of Mu’ta begins between the Muslims and the Byzantines at the site of Mu’ta in southern Jordan. The cause of the battle is the killing of messenger of Prophet Muhammad by the Ghassanids.

258c0bff-a9a9-5e51-af16-8f05e17c4a43.description: The Pragmatic Sanction: Charles VI declared the heritability of the Habsburg crown in the female line in default of a male heir, and the indivisibility of the countries of the House of Habsburg. Plague endemics.

25e6c170-8d7e-521f-8401-3a43c5a6dd70.description: Musa ibn Abi ’l-Afiya, chief of the Miknassa tribe, conquers Fez and takes control of all of Maghreb.

25f8a351-0c67-5511-ae9a-05836ea0c1ed.description: King Gustavus III, through a coup d’état makes himself absolute monarch. Twenty years later, in 1792, he is murdered at a masquerade ball.

2611a998-35c3-5527-a22a-5f62c77511b5.description: Prince Charles Edward Stuart (‘Bonnie Prince Charlie’) lands in Scotland and starts a campaign to restore his father James Francis (the Old Pretender) to the thrones of Britain.

266cc2c7-1e9e-5cf3-992e-efa0cddaa017.description: Sweden enters the Thirty Years’ War under Gustavus Adolphus (Gustav II Adolf). This war involved most European nations.

26a23d8f-c395-5825-94d9-d5f8c8161336.description: Carolina Resolutio: Emperor Karl (Charles) VI (Karl III as king of Hungary) regulates Protestant affairs. England accepts the Pragmatic Sanction in return for economic advantages.

26a2c361-31dc-55a0-87ad-7487948ea18a.description: The wedding of King Lajos II and Mary Habsburg (Mary leaves Hungary after the deaths of Lajos II and as Mary of Hungary later becomes the governor of the Low Countries).

26bcb535-5673-53d3-ad7f-5b58d2f25a57.description: Cultural and economic exchange between the Italian states and Mamluk Syria, exemplified by Andreas Alpagos, physician of the Venetian consulate in Damascus, who translates many Arabic manuscripts.

26cadaf0-aa1b-5dc9-9eec-cfa4060a7250.description:
The first period of Iconoclasm begins when Byzantine Emperor Leo III forbids the worship of religious images.  
Empress Irene, who took power as regent for his son, Constantine VI (780–97), brought this period to an end with a council held in Nicea in 787 in favour of icon worship.

26cc8040-5466-5d1a-9014-b3a494b8aff8.description: The physician Robert Koch (1843–1910) finds the bacillus of the Cholera disease. This is only one of the numerous findings of the pioneer of bacteriology.

26da04ee-7f58-53c5-a266-2422fcc19d78.name: Great peace congress was held in Vienna
26da04ee-7f58-53c5-a266-2422fcc19d78.description: The Great Peace Congress is held in Vienna from 18 September 1814 to 9 June 1815. Clemens Wenzel Duke of Metternich organises the Austrian predominance in Italy. Austria exchanges the Austrian Netherlands for the territory of the Venetian Republic and creates the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia.

273d70c1-c2bb-571c-a79a-844701148f75.description: The most well-known Swedish saint, Saint Birgitta, is born. Her Order, Ordo Sanctissimi Salvatoris (the Order of the Most Holy Saviour), is approved by a Papal Bull in 1370.

27dd0edc-9407-5509-9877-9ef53d79fbca.description: Having already founded the Zagreb bishopric, King (St) László I founds the St Egid Benedictine monastery in Somogyvár (his first burial site before Várad [today: Oradea, Romania]), inviting monks from Saint Gilles.

27f820b6-9acd-56c6-be82-ee4130019591.description: The epic Anglo-Saxon poem Beowulf, consisting of 3,182 lines of Old English, is probably written; the poet is anonymous.

2830c84c-9afc-5074-8669-1ba50eb536d8.description: Michelangelo Buonarroti starts work on David, a masterpiece of the Renaissance. The work, conceived as a symbol of the Florentine Republic, is completed in 1504.

289a7e50-45dd-5fde-bd4a-48a8b218e648.description: The March Revolution tried to introduce a democratic constitution. Marx (1818–83) and Engels (1820–95) publish Das Kommunistische Manifest analysing capitalist methods of production.

28d336d1-ae64-5425-af71-3104c121f1f7.description: Abu Hamid al-Ghazali (d.1111), the great philosopher, visits Palestine and takes refuge for three years in the Haram al-Sharif.

28ecf140-0f7f-5f9d-b485-35516c1bee43.description: The arrival at Ma’an of the Hijazi Railway line from Damascus is celebrated on 1 September, on the anniversary of the accession of Sultan ‘Abd al Hamid II to the throne.

29455b48-5d00-51d8-b4b7-85037c64bd9c.description: Battle of Aljubarrota. Beginning of the Avis Dynasty with John I.

298b33d8-c046-5fc6-a571-f1b4ce604f9c.name: Great Arab Revolt
298b33d8-c046-5fc6-a571-f1b4ce604f9c.description: Supported by the UK, on 10 June 1916 Husayn ibn ‘Ali, the Sharif of Mecca, declares the Great Arab Revolt against the Turks with the aim of establishing an independent Arab state under his leadership in Bilad al-Sham (Greater Syria). Aqaba in Jordan is captured in 1917, becoming the headquarters of the northern army headed by Husayn’s son Prince Faysal, who becomes King of Syria in 1920. British promises to Sharif Husayn have contradicted other secret agreements of the UK with its allies, e.g. Sykes–Picot. These mandates put an end to the Arab Kingdom of Syria under King Faysal on 24 July 1920.

299920bb-2a53-53ee-8813-0d0c51f44bef.description: The Act of Union unites the kingdoms of England and Scotland and transfers the seat of Scottish government to London, creating the Kingdom of Great Britain.

29a0a883-e78d-55c3-b87a-8866ad3d7b70.name: Italy’s first African war
29a0a883-e78d-55c3-b87a-8866ad3d7b70.description: Italy’s first African war: in 1882 Italy starts colonial expansion in the Horn of Africa; in 1890, Eritrea becomes an Italian colony. Afterwards, Italy attempts to penetrate into Ethiopia and suffers a crushing defeat at Adwa (the biggest African victory over a colonial army): Italy loses 4,000 Italian and 2,000 colonial soldiers. The Crispi government resigns.

29dd3711-8399-5487-8219-33352bc528eb.description: Start of the islamicisation of al-Andalus. First incursions in al-Gharb.

2a212264-a53f-550f-852b-e14e9c7fb3d0.description: Murad I captures Edirne (Adrianople). As the third Ottoman capital, Edirne now becomes the headquarters for the further expansion.

2a28984c-7460-524b-babb-a5502f9b5da7.description: The inauguration of the first railway between Jaffa and Jerusalem

2a5051fd-c8ce-5190-9301-2ebfde469594.description: Philip the Fair, surrounded by his ‘jurists’, consolidates the authority of the King of France. Levying taxes on Jews and ‘Lombards’ and confiscating the riches of the Knights Templar, he enters into a conflict with the papacy which is only resolved in 1305 with the election of a French pope.

2a7b6bbe-2029-5fed-ad45-5c1a57ecc81e.name: The Kingdom of Sardinia participates in the Crimean war
2a7b6bbe-2029-5fed-ad45-5c1a57ecc81e.description: The Kingdom of Sardinia participates in the Crimean war as part of the Anglo-French alliance against Russia.

2a878e02-8441-5986-ba7c-d99f0404125b.description: William of Normandy lands at Pevensey, defeats and kills Harold II at the Battle of Hastings and becomes William I, the Conqueror; the first Norman King of England (until 1087).

2a93cf50-6b9a-551f-9371-51b68b37031e.description: On 6 May the Sykes-Picot agreement divides the Arab area into zones of permanent colonial influence between France and Britain; Jordan was allocated to British administration.

2aad596a-7b63-525c-8cce-41debbeaa7a4.description: Al-Afdal Ibn Badr al-Jamali (d.515/1121), the commander-in-chief of the Fatimid armies completes the construction of the huge mosque of ‘Asqalan with its magnificent minbar (pulpit), which is exhibited to this day in the Ibrahimi Mosque in Hebron.

2ab34570-1028-519d-900b-b19f23b80e8a.description: During the rule of the Merovingian Dynasty (558–629), rulers of the Frankish Dynasty gradually gain power over parts of what will later become Germany.

2ab621a1-285d-5faa-b434-1b8228552433.name: Regeneration, led mainly by Minister Fontes Pereira Melo
2ab621a1-285d-5faa-b434-1b8228552433.description: Regeneration, led mainly by Minister Fontes Pereira Melo (who gives the period name – Fontism) is a peaceful political cycle of global innovation started in 1851. The kingdom is tired of political unrest. Conditions are created for the middle classes and foreign investors to support economic expansion, the development of infrastructure and industrialisation.

2abc9658-095d-5a98-a9e3-b1c1ecb1ccd6.description: The Battle of Ankara between Tamerlane and Bayezid and the start of the Interregnum (Fetret) Period.

2b15f4e6-26ad-5dcc-b2c8-592e4c9462c3.description: Start of Portuguese expansion in Morocco with the conquest of Ceuta.

2b2ed3c4-0c02-5af2-9ada-b0bbd50412bf.name: Romania fights in the First World War
2b2ed3c4-0c02-5af2-9ada-b0bbd50412bf.description: After two years of neutrality, Romania fights in the World War I on the side of the Triple Entente. At the end of the war, following the dissolution of the Austro-Hungarian monarchy and of the Russian Empire, the national gatherings of Bessarabia, Transylvania, Banat and Bukovina vote for their union with the Romanian kingdom. Greater Romania is thus created.

2b577c29-5b3f-567d-ab58-550aac88e5ff.name: Lord Curzon visits the Trucial shaikhs
2b577c29-5b3f-567d-ab58-550aac88e5ff.description: British Viceroy and Governor-General of India, Lord Curzon, visits the Trucial sheikhs at Sharjah to reaffirm Britain’s commitment to “guardianship and protection” and the British Government’s position as “your overlords and protectors”. Curzon asserts that continued British control of India depends on maintaining British supremacy in the Gulf.

2b82bc16-0f83-575e-8c9d-1cb88b973f4d.description: Damascus becomes capital of the Umayyad Empire under Mu‘awiya (Caliph 661–81). Assassination of ‘Ali, nephew of the Prophet, by a Kharijite (secessionist).

2b96c252-e950-5517-a8db-89da1a889f25.description: Development of commercial relations with Italian towns.

2b9a07fc-5259-59a3-897b-1f73f087c01e.name: Stimulus by French July Revolution
2b9a07fc-5259-59a3-897b-1f73f087c01e.description: Stimulated by the French July Revolution, the *Vormärz* (pre-March) Revolution refers to the formation of political programmes and factional movements.

2bcdd51c-06b0-57fc-b7f9-744fb2055517.description: The plague of ‘Amwasa, a town located between Jerusalem and Jaffa, in which hundreds of soldiers and officers, including the army commander Abu ‘Ubaida ‘Amir bin al-Jarrah, lose their lives

2c3e0e21-8805-5b99-af1f-0073a37781e3.description: Muhammad ‘Ali, the Pasha of Egypt, sends his army under the command of his son Ibrahim Pasha to conquer Palestine and succeeds in bringing the country under his control.

2cd8dc54-23b9-50ab-b089-94ebbecc93f8.description: Famine due to the low level of the Nile for several consecutive years and an earthquake result in over 240,000 dead.

2ce70c94-398f-5338-904d-87fbc76bbd71.description: Anatolian Seljuq Sultan Alaeddin Keykubad marries the daughter of the Ayyubid Sultan al-Malik Adil.

2ce84b2f-4047-5460-90db-e0c4b7e0a8a5.description: The church of Haghia Sophia in Constantinople is opened on 27 December by Byzantine Emperor Justinian I having been rebuilt after its destruction in Nika Riot (532).

2d1e62e5-c8e3-5d7b-a8ff-2dfa53b6e735.description: Establishment of the Beylik of Constantine.

2d225d93-e88c-5abf-8ce2-adc5e930c715.name: Triple Alliance
2d225d93-e88c-5abf-8ce2-adc5e930c715.description: The Triple Alliance formed (Italy, Germany, Austria-Hungary).

2d302fe6-eab4-5362-83f2-162983ff38de.description: Gaza becomes an independent Mamluk governate (niyaba).

2d5e5adf-59ef-5b7b-8714-644157da49f0.description: The fall of ‘Asqalan, the last Fatimid military base in Palestine.

2d648f71-76bf-5cd6-abf4-4e8acbf9fe43.description: Coronation of King (St) László I who reforms Hungary’s legal codes, administrative and ecclesiastical system and life (1083: canonisation of King István and Prince Imre; 1092: synod of Szabolcs).

2d7d9a59-43ed-5170-a1ad-4e0390ae0f19.name: Italy participates in WWI on the side of Britain, France and Russia
2d7d9a59-43ed-5170-a1ad-4e0390ae0f19.description: Italy participates in World War I on the side of the UK, France and Russia, despite widespread opposition to entering the war. On the Austrian front, Italy suffers a crushing defeat at Caporetto in 1917, but wins in 1918. In Libya, Arab revolt: Italy keeps control only of coastal towns. Casualties are 650,000 military deaths, 950,000 wounded, 600,000 prisoners of war or missing.

2d945522-a203-5f90-9c18-0c592affebc6.description: Peace of Westphalia marks the end of the Thirty Years’ War. Habsburg rule in the Czech lands officially acknowledged. Moravia lost almost half of its population. Inflow of foreign aristocracy. Brno became the capital of Moravia.

2d9a0fd0-882b-5e8b-b439-eaac6a9dbd5b.description: Appearance of the first taifa kingdoms in al-Andalus.

2db35884-0dcb-51af-8feb-97eb2256b41b.description: Peace with Spain, which recognises Portuguese independence.

2df6d6ea-d613-5474-930a-90e8d74c3754.description: Basilica of Euphrasius built in Piorec, one of the most important monuments in Croatia. It was built on the remains of an earlier three-naved basilica.

2dfede66-08ea-5b14-998b-45bb3c2c24ce.description: A moribund Idrisid Morocco vacillates between the Umayyads of al-Andalus and the Fatimids of Ifriqiya for 27 years.

2e049eef-f57d-5de3-8ec0-4c10938509ee.description: Daily life in the regency is marked by civil wars and power struggles, first among the deys and then the beys.

2e10d16d-0c4d-585e-b2b4-02defffc0781.description: Foundation of the abbey at Cluny (near to Mâcon), whose monks followed the Benedictine order. The monks at Cluny travelled throughout Europe and played an important role in 11th-century reform.

2e3ea087-5afe-5338-957a-9a3889459efb.description:
Governor Camilio Gonzaga establishes the city of Split. He proposed to the Venetian Senate to build a bulwark to defend the town.  
The Paulist School of philosophy was established.

2e841549-695a-56ea-97fc-8cd7ad6c5b2a.description: The Almoravids take the town of Sijilmassa.

2f124f94-76c2-57a9-86cc-04e893c85b21.description: Expulsion of the Byzantines and unification of the peninsular lands of the Visigoth Kingdom of Toledo.

2f53789c-449c-5aff-b105-7d621c8784c6.name: Bashir II becomes the leader of Lebanon
2f53789c-449c-5aff-b105-7d621c8784c6.description: Bashir Shihab II, helped by the Ottomans and by Ahmad Pasha al-Jazzar (governor of Acre), defeats his rival in the Battle of Simqanieh. Bashir Jumblatt dies in Acre at the order of al-Jazzar. Bashir II represses the Druze rebellion, particularly in and around Beirut. This makes Bashir II the only leader of Mount Lebanon.

2f8c1e29-2c7a-5d73-9603-1ddb08087165.description: Charles VII is crowned in Reims, having been proclaimed the true king of France by Joan of Arc. A gradual reconquest of the kingdom begins, to be completed towards the end of the 15th century.

2fc2c359-cb5d-59f7-b25c-981347b36b4b.description:
Conquest of Nasrid Granada and expulsion of the last Muslim power in the Peninsula.  
Expulsion of the Jews.  
Discovery of America.

30123690-f935-51d6-b829-15c09c5bf051.name: British occupation of Aden
30123690-f935-51d6-b829-15c09c5bf051.description: British control of India is driven by trade. Steamships require fuelling stations. To this purpose Aden is occupied and controlled imperially from India for a century. Most British control of the Middle East is indirect and informal. Aden becomes a Crown Colony, with partial control of the Hinterland.

3016577c-60dd-55c3-8277-61f4d6fcb408.description: The Mamluk Amir Sarghatmish builds a madrasa in Amman; it became the headquarters of Balqa, to teach Hanafi rites (one of the four Sunni rites in Islam).

303e7baf-ffd4-5875-b983-5d32c0c22c32.description: Friedrich I Barbarossa (1152–90) of the Hohenstaufen Dynasty is crowned emperor. He drowned during the Third Crusade near Konya in Turkey in 1190.

30605f3f-79c6-5430-aaef-b20e16b57357.name: Conflicts between the Druse and the Maronite
30605f3f-79c6-5430-aaef-b20e16b57357.description: Conflicts between the Druze and the Maronite Christians explode. A Maronite revolt against the feudal class erupts, lasting till 1858.

30714b85-a474-5cb0-984e-75bf4c136235.description: Trpimir I issues a charter in Latin in which he names himself the ‘Duke of Croats’ (*Dux Chroatorum iuvatus munere divino*) and his realm as the ‘Realm of the Croats’ (*Regnum Chroatorum*).

31030fb9-1bf2-5270-9f5b-94dad865481d.description: Death of Luís de Camões. Loss of independence: Phillip II of Spain becomes king of Portugal as Phillip I.

31878f86-f9ab-5fff-b351-24d754c1eba7.description: Reconquest of the coast by the Almohads and reunification of Ifriqiya.

31898899-b4ad-5a03-99d9-ef2ffcabf419.description: The Fatimids enter Fustat with little resistance. Jawhar Al-Siqili founds al-Qahira (Cairo) to the north of al-Fustat in anticipation of the arrival of the Fatimid Caliph al-Mu’izz from North Africa to make Cairo his seat of rule.

31bb7f1e-29db-5a59-b2b2-95c8964ab870.description: The Norse (Viking) raids on England and Scotland begin with a raid on the Lindisfarne monastery on the north-east coast of England.

3203faf7-f674-56b8-9ff5-abe8897e67c3.description: King Otto II (r. 973–83) marries the Byzantine princess Theophanu and Byzantine influence enters German art and culture.

328f265b-a477-590d-ae49-14d4e83ef499.description: The Berlin Conference sets out the manner in which colonies are to be acquired, and preludes the division of Africa. France and Jules Ferry establish a protectorate in Tunisia (1881) and Madagascar (1885). ‘French’ territories in West Africa are united in a federation in 1890.

32a440a3-8f52-5588-82d1-6b7f499325f1.description: Unsuccesful peasant revolt led by György Dózsa. The presentation to the Hungarian Parliament of the *Tripartitum*, a collection of Hungarian unwritten laws compiled by jurist István Werbőczy (published Vienna, 1518).

32bb5381-b440-58d3-b4c0-e94e9f40869d.description: After the Plombières meeting between Napoleon III and Cavour, an alliance is signed between France and Piemont. War with Austria results in the Armistice of Villafranca, the first step towards Italian unity (Rome remains under papal control for the time being). Savoy and Nice become part of France following a referendum.

32c40eda-8fa3-56c0-be35-bfebe4210d85.description: The world's first permanent passenger railway service, the Stockton and Darlington Railway, opens in northern England.

32f946ec-2f50-5de0-b6f6-28fcc0e8facb.name: Armistice between Austro-Hungary and the Entente Powers
32f946ec-2f50-5de0-b6f6-28fcc0e8facb.description: Armistice between Austro-Hungary and the Entente Powers (France, Russia and the United Kingdom).

32fcaa4e-3de5-5d1e-bf7d-62fe60a7c94b.name: The Treaty of Sevres
32fcaa4e-3de5-5d1e-bf7d-62fe60a7c94b.description: The Treaty of Sèvres is ratified after the victory of the Balkan Wars and the end of World War I. Consequently, Greece gains administration of the area of Smyrna.

33154f08-3836-548b-bcda-a749c70d2d84.description: The assassination of Henry III ends the reign of the Valois, which was marked by Wars of Religion between Catholics and Protestants. The Catholic League’s recognition of Henry IV, now converted to Catholicism, allows the kingdom to be reunited.

333b762f-21b9-587d-b2b7-a54ceeab8f8a.description: Hammadid kingdom conquered by the Almohads.

334291dc-172a-596a-a24a-379f1e1d9428.description: The Siege of Vienna by the Ottomans ends in the defeat of the Ottomans by a united army. A gradual retreat of the Ottomans begins.

3374a7bb-9d39-587e-aeb9-774f13809a60.name: Repeated skirmishes between British and Qawasimi vessels
3374a7bb-9d39-587e-aeb9-774f13809a60.description: Repeated skirmishes between British and Qawasim vessels are labelled “piracy” by the former and taken as justification to plot the final destruction of the Qawasim by the latter. The British launch naval attacks against the Qawasim strongholds at Ras al-Khaimah along the Gulf and on the Persian littoral. However, the Qawasim succeed in rebuilding their fleet and positions to resume their defensive trade-war against the British and their Omani allies.

3393c160-73b5-5f90-8d3c-916dd33b279a.description: Glorious Revolution and end of the Bourbon dynasty.

33d1073a-c0cd-567b-a9e8-7aaae1de3e6a.name: Crimean War
33d1073a-c0cd-567b-a9e8-7aaae1de3e6a.description: War between Russia and the Ottoman Empire and its allies France, UK and Piedmont-Savoy. The Crimean War is a consequence of rivalry over the Eastern Question and France’s support of Catholic claims and Russia’s support of Orthodox claims to control the holy sites in Jerusalem. Russia seeks to exploit Ottoman political weakness to gain diplomatic rights for Orthodox subjects of the Empire. Peace established by the Treaty of Paris (1856).

33fcc702-ac35-5fa5-b9d0-4731722d1a6b.description: Al-Zahir Baybars captures the city of Antioch, the second Crusader state in the Levant after al-Raha.

34352b64-976c-536f-b35f-5a07f4cceca3.name: First Restoration
34352b64-976c-536f-b35f-5a07f4cceca3.description: First Restoration: the return of the monarchy, referred to as the Bourbon Restoration. Louis XVIII (brother of Louis XVI) facilitated this by accepting a return to the monarchy by means of the Charter of 1814. This Charter combined the more moderate ideas of the Revolution with certain monarchist traditions.

34862ab6-f257-5c9d-8c63-f9c5480fc6d4.name: Opening of the Suez Canal
34862ab6-f257-5c9d-8c63-f9c5480fc6d4.description: Built largely with French expertise and capital, the Suez Canal shortens the journey to India. The British government secures a major financial interest in the Canal in 1876, and its security becomes a major British interest for the following century.

34b05ed8-7b3b-57c5-b08b-b87e6eb4a7f6.name: Emperor Pedro I of Brazil turned Pedro IV of Portugal gave up the throne to his daughter
34b05ed8-7b3b-57c5-b08b-b87e6eb4a7f6.description: With the death of his father, Emperor Pedro I of Brazil becomes Pedro IV of Portugal but gives up the throne to his daughter, future Queen Maria II. The proclamation of a moderate Constitutional Charter does not stop the absolutist movement led by his brother, Prince Miguel (1802–66), who disregards the rights of his niece Princess Maria and Pedro’s decision.

34fcab2b-dc2f-544c-b0e0-dc856d20ac60.name: Aqaba became the new base for Faysal’s army
34fcab2b-dc2f-544c-b0e0-dc856d20ac60.description: In June 1917 the coastal city of Aqaba in Jordan becomes the new base for Faisal’s army, renamed the “Arab Northern Army”. Attacks on the Hijaz Railway continue, extending now as far north as southern Jordan. T. E. Lawrence, “Lawrence of Arabia” himself led reconnaissance parties into Syria and made contact with Arab nationalists in Damascus. The spectacular victory of the Egyptian Expeditionary Force (EEF) at the Third Battle of Gaza (Beersheba) in October 1917, and the subsequent British advance into the Jordan Valley, gave renewed impetus to Faisal’s “railway war” further east. Meanwhile, Amir Faisal, with Lawrence as his adviser, had captured the seaport of Wejh (al-Wagh) on the Red Sea, 150 km north of Yanbu. From there, Faisal’s men spent most of 1917 attacking the Hijaz Railway. Small raiding parties blew up sections of track, destroyed bridges, water towers and even some weakly defended railway stations. The British, planning to invade Palestine, were keen for the Arab rebels to keep the 12,000 Ottoman troops tied down in Medina (Madinah).

3513b9af-0c20-5db1-af3a-945c0057099c.description: Přemysl Otakar II killed at Battle of the Moravian Field. Under his rule, the Czech lands reached to the shores of the Adriatic. Bohemia governed by Otto of Brandenburg, Moravia by Rudolph of Habsburg.

35f32299-83bc-56af-8759-78e7c473b0fa.description: The Umayyad Dynasty starts its caliphate in Syria and Jordan under Mu’awiya ibn Abi Sufyan, who makes Damascus his capital.

368b9b30-fe58-57b6-ac37-4eb8ad940bfd.name: Isabel II becomes Queen of Spain
368b9b30-fe58-57b6-ac37-4eb8ad940bfd.description: Isabel II becomes Queen of Spain. The Salic Law forbidding women to reign had been abolished in 1830 because Fernando VII's only heirs were female. His brother, Carlos de Borbón, asserts his claim to the throne against his niece (first Carlist War, 1836–39); two further Carlist wars will follow (1846–49, 1872–76).

36c600ee-238c-5104-b1d5-181e80447600.description: Ibn Marzuq, celebrated historian of the Marinid Sultan Abu al-Hassan, dies in Fez.

36e1af7c-3bb9-5f93-9462-befff7918c1f.description: Insurrections and popular resistance against the occupation.

37059d81-d5cf-57a4-941c-f419f32cb6e8.description: Yusuf ibn Tashufin annexes Andalusia to the Almoravid empire.

372f2dcd-a881-5181-ae34-488d9d454235.description: John of Luxemburg marries Elizabeth Przemyslid. First Czech-langauge publication *Dalimil Chronicle* (1314); the first guild code in the Czech lands published (1318).

3791815a-9bf9-5eca-a777-ee474a6db196.description: On 25–28 January Emperor Henry IV (1056–1106) of the Salian Dynasty is forced on a walk of penitence to Canossa to beg forgiveness of Pope Gregor VII and to accept him as arbitrator. The Way (or Walk) to Canossa refers to the walk itself and the events surrounding his journey.

379adc29-287b-5b4e-9d83-375ab79250cb.description: The Battle of Nikápoly: Sultan Bayazid I defeats the crusaders of King Sigismund of Luxemburg, sole ruler of Hungary after the death of his first wife, Queen Mary, daughter of Lajos (Louis) I in 1395.

37bc9459-586b-5e66-b94c-492828a4e324.description: Moroccan resistance fighters win the Battle of Annual in the Rif, defeating the Spanish army.

37bf8829-e6ef-54b3-bfd7-6c5dda09e2c6.name: Military Coup
37bf8829-e6ef-54b3-bfd7-6c5dda09e2c6.description: A military coup brings about restitution of the Karađorđević Dynasty.

37daa534-8ff0-5ad7-8825-af2533e9cbbd.description: Election of King Mátyás (Matthias) I Hunyadi (Corvinus) son of János Hunyadi. He made Hungary one of the greatest economical and military powers of Europe and defended Europe from the Turks.

37f173f0-8fb1-58f1-9fcc-5a66edc976d2.description: Amir Ya‘qub al-Mansur win the Battle of Alarcos against the Spanish.

37fa2522-6029-5df2-b76a-817b3740c7e1.description: The Lombards enter Italy. The lands occupied in the Centre and the South become the Duchies of Spoleto and Benevento respectively.

3818d5fd-c5b6-507f-af3e-cc1015160262.description: A time of financial difficulties and European manoeuvring. Tunisia’s state debt results in the establishment of an international financial commission, and a French–English initiative intended to control Tunisian finances.

381bc6c0-47ec-5252-b2e8-8016ecad32e1.description: Battle of Siffin between Mu’awiya, governor of Damascus, and ‘Ali, the fourth caliph and cousin and son-in-law of the Prophet, resulting in a schism in the Muslim community with Kharijites (secessionists) accepting neither.

382e923b-1910-5e0f-ba53-3972d96b8af6.name: Bashir II and Bashir Jumblatt
382e923b-1910-5e0f-ba53-3972d96b8af6.description: Bashir Shihab II, who was elected as amir in 1788 under Ottoman suzerainty, is overthrown when he backs Acre, and flees to Egypt, later to return and form an army. Bashir Jumblatt, the Druze leader, gathers the Druze factions and declares a rebellion that leads to massacres and battles with the Maronites who support Bashir Shihab.

383d1653-79ab-5139-9743-17029b0cafd9.name: Catholic Emancipation
383d1653-79ab-5139-9743-17029b0cafd9.description: Irish lawyer Daniel O’Connell leads the campaign for concession of Catholic Emancipation, which will allow Roman Catholics to sit in the UK Parliament. The campaign is successful, helped along by the death of George III, but O’Connell’s long-term goal is to repeal Ireland’s Act of Union with Great Britain.

388aea07-bde6-5036-8e0e-f684f0ad4ac6.name: Serbo-Turkish War in Bosnia and Herzegovina
388aea07-bde6-5036-8e0e-f684f0ad4ac6.description: During the 1875 Bosnia-Herzegovina rebellion against Ottoman authority, the principalities of Serbia and Montenegro provide the insurgents with moral, material and military support, which leads to the first Serbo-Turkish War in 1876. Having been a long time in preparation, the rebellion is widespread and raises questions not only about Serbia but also about the East, thus becoming an event of European importance. Its outcome is the convocation of the Berlin Congress (1878), at which both Serbia and Montenegro gain independence, and Austria-Hungary takes over Bosnia-Herzegovina.

38957083-5395-5510-a2cc-c5c82063cde9.description: End of the Thirty Years’ War. The Peace of Westphalia is signed in Münster and Osnabrück and results in a territorial agreement for Germany.

38b37486-4ca5-5ea5-a8ad-ff3929a1df98.description: Peace in Srijemski Karlovci. The end of Turkish rule in north Croatia It remained under the rule of Habsburgs while south Croatia, with the exception of Dubrovnik Republic, was dominated by Venice.

391e794a-87d2-5483-baa5-bd477e8e9f79.name: Reforms of Khayr al-Din
391e794a-87d2-5483-baa5-bd477e8e9f79.description: The regency of Khayr al-Din, the Grand Vizier reformer, who reorganises institutions and the economy. His major cultural works are the creation of Sadiki College and major reform of the Zaytuna Mosque.

392bdf81-90a4-59c4-be66-5325b35de674.description: The Anjala league is created. This is a group of Finnish officers voicing their opinion about a free Finland.

39331e52-56f9-57b3-aa21-c246025ffb0f.description: Death of Louis XIV. A long regency period ensues, marked by the financial experience of Law and the colonisation of Louisiana.

393b8cfb-9942-518d-8662-b4c0306464c2.name: Al Qawasim confederation migrates to the Arab Gulf coast
393b8cfb-9942-518d-8662-b4c0306464c2.description: In the early 1700s, the (Al-Qasimi) Qawasim confederation migrates to the coast of the Arab Gulf from the Persian littoral. Here, they establish their main base in Julfar (later Ras al-Khaimah), soon extending their sway all along the lower Gulf, across areas of the east coast and towns on the Persian littoral.

39792b25-cc09-5cf4-b24a-343aa7e4091e.description: The Bloodbath of Stockholm. Danish King Christian II has a large number of the Swedish nobility beheaded.

3987d218-e552-5510-8c0e-a99c8c8a201f.description: Mu’awiya Ibn Abi Sufyan (r. 661–80) declares himself Caliph in Jerusalem, announcing the beginning of the Umayyad dynasty. The caliphs  ‘Abd al-Malik, Sulayman, ‘Umar II and other Umayyad caliphs did the same.

398a51cb-b12c-5007-9180-fe06cc51a912.description: Abu Inan builds the Buinaniya madrasa in Fez, where Marinid decorative arts find their full aesthetic expression.

39e4a69a-c75f-5119-b55e-4bd1464fb8a9.description: The mother of Caliph al-Muqtadir orders several construction works in Palestine including renewal of the gates of the Dome of the Rock.

3a5c7b0e-5525-51cb-9a92-f7c14cf42418.description: Croats establish the principalities of Primorska Hrvatska on the Adriatic Coast and Posavska Hrvatska in north Croatia.

3a97e768-fdfd-5678-82f8-c2c62b2e9f3f.name: The Peace (or Treaty) of Bucharest
3a97e768-fdfd-5678-82f8-c2c62b2e9f3f.description: The Peace (or Treaty) of Bucharest between Romania and Austria.

3ae5c9c0-9320-5c9d-b667-aa81029ad761.description: Hernán Cortés completes the conquest of the Aztec Empire (Mexico).

3af083b2-afbd-5dc1-9307-ac2a302e4b79.description: Bonnie Prince Charlie’s Jacobite army is routed by government troops at the Battle of Culloden; the rebellion collapses and Charles Edward Stewart escapes, dying in Italian exile in 1788.

3b5c2397-2fc8-5cf3-9fef-8fb260ae04db.name: Battle of Jena and Auerstedt
3b5c2397-2fc8-5cf3-9fef-8fb260ae04db.description: The twin battles of Jena and Auerstedt are fought – in the midst of the collapse of the Prussian State and abolition of the Holy Roman Empire by Kaiser Franz II – under pressure from Napoleon Bonaparte.

3b69be10-d58a-52a7-9805-ece6996337cb.description: Roger II, governor of Sicily since 1112, is crowned King of Sicily and reigns until 1154.

3ba4b872-d15e-5f19-9276-3532d502974b.description: The Lancastrian Henry Tudor defeats the Yorkist monarch Richard III at Bosworth Field and claims the throne as Henry VII, marking the end of the Plantagenet dynasty and the ascendancy of the Tudors.

3ba4be7c-9b81-5799-a724-7b204d6a497c.description: The Sassanian (Persian) army conquers Palestine during a campaign of occupation of Great Syria and Egypt. The conquest is very destructive, tens of churches are destroyed, and monasteries are sacked and burned.

3c25f5fb-a621-52df-b837-a0e26676f92a.description: Birth of the Tunisian nationalist movement named the Young Tunisians after the Young Turk movement in Istanbul.

3c91edce-1d52-54ad-82bd-d17232131431.name: Municipal organization for Istanbul
3c91edce-1d52-54ad-82bd-d17232131431.description: The Tanzimat Council appoints a City Ordering Commission (Intizam-ı Şehir Heyeti), comprising Ottoman and foreign residents, charged with developing new regulation to transform the structure of Instanbul into a municipal government. It recommends establishment of a commission to enforce urban regulations and improve the city's physical make-up, financed through a separate tax structure.

3c9d5659-a75b-52ca-945e-3308bac60539.description: Death of the historian Ibn al-Warraq, whose work, dedicated to the towns of Tahert, Oran, Sijilmassa, Nekkour and al-Basra, would later be used by the geographer al-Bakri in his Description of Northern Africa.

3d0779fd-2a97-5ac7-bd15-b1fc7e31bd7f.description: The long reign of Bey Hammuda Pasha enhances the legitimacy of the dynasty and helps to stabilise the country.

3d0f8752-a96c-5c13-a9bf-51021b32acdc.name: The heir apparent of Austria Franz Ferdinand gets killed in Sarajevo by a member of the Serbian intelligence service
3d0f8752-a96c-5c13-a9bf-51021b32acdc.description: The heir apparent of Austria, Franz Ferdinand, is murdered in Sarajevo by a member of the Serbian intelligence service known as the “Black Hand”. As a consequence, the Austrian government issues an ultimatum to Serbia; Germany declares war on the Russian Empire and on France; and Great Britain declares war on the German Empire.

3d728eba-aff4-5a4f-86da-605c78b0b4c9.description: The Capitulations afford French ships and subjects the freedom of the Ottoman Empire. French consuls gain the right to judge their compatriots in criminal and civil courts. Trade is greatly facilitated.

3d9812e4-b8ef-57b6-9ac5-850fc6a37dfc.description: The Suez Canal, build under the direction of Ferdinand de Lesseps and the watchful eyes of Empress Eugenie, is opened.

3dae562a-52d6-5555-a72f-59c79c393258.description: After devastating Baghdad, the Mongols, led by Hulegu, invade Syria and put an end to the Ayyubid dynasty. The Mongols lose Syria when they are defeated by the Mamluks in Ain Jalut.

3db76185-8b18-5ca3-add1-fdcce7e70fbf.description: A severe earthquake causes great damage all over Palestine.

3db937f3-6f2c-555f-87d9-3cd4d5ba7ff3.description: The oldest German code of law (Sachsenspiegel), written by Eike von Repgow (ca.1180–d. after 1233) in Latin and translated to German appears in final form. It becomes a standard for all future codes of law.

3dc5ecf9-642b-52bd-937e-54c6b8c26174.description: Expulsion of the Society of Jesus.
