3e12f5fd-ba5d-52e4-80bb-44e6a023c956.name: Assasination of the first Governor of Greece
3e12f5fd-ba5d-52e4-80bb-44e6a023c956.description: The First Governor of Greece, Conte Ioannis Kapodistrias, is assassinated.

3e3954f1-27ae-55d2-9fb6-0379bad29d5e.description: The Representation of the People Act 1918 allows women over the age of 30 with the minimum property qualifications to vote in the United Kingdom’s elections for the first time.

3e450688-88c2-56bb-bfd7-280b207b6d36.name: The German National Assembly meets in Frankfurt
3e450688-88c2-56bb-bfd7-280b207b6d36.description: The German National Assembly meets in Frankfurt.

3e46dcf2-c671-5ecd-8570-602dcc6b73b7.description: Mulay Isma‘ïl takes the town of Mamora back from the Spanish and it is renamed al-Mahdiya.

3e6e7aa9-2883-5b04-b168-4538152bf867.description: The first academic thesis in Swedish is presented. Up until now all theses had been written in Latin and even after this date Latin remained the academic language.

3e7a6480-896d-5bfb-ad87-fdd66ac7fb34.description: During the conquest of Jordan, a plague called ‘Emwas’ starts in Palestine and spreads all over Jordan. Among the 25,000 people who die are the companions of the Prophet who ruled the Jordan valley.

3ead5f3b-fb93-53a2-9e44-3bc24f19c7b4.description: The Sa‘dids crush the last Wattasids and enter Fez amid much ceremony.

3eb7a9b3-273d-5c01-bed5-6041862fc40b.name: Play arouses patriotic sentiments
3eb7a9b3-273d-5c01-bed5-6041862fc40b.description: 1 April: Namık Kemal’s play *Vatan Yahud Silistre* arouses patriotic sentiments in İstanbul.

3f178cfd-a839-5dff-b912-dc73471fb7ee.description: The invention of the printing machine with movable metal types by Johannes Gutenberg (c. 1398–c. 1468) results in the first printing of the Gutenberg Bible (Biblia Sacra) in 1455.

3f4cb0ce-5c63-5da8-bc07-f731381c9d73.description: Restoration of the Bourbons with Alfonso XII.

3f9af882-80c2-5359-a845-09c7be4e0fd2.description: Circassians, non-Arab Islamic people from the Caucasus region of western Asia, are forced to emigrate from their lands to the south by the Russians. The Ottoman empire helped them to reach Arab countries and settled them there.

3fa14438-b4b6-5f5c-890f-1c3481e4ceda.name: Italo-Turkish war
3fa14438-b4b6-5f5c-890f-1c3481e4ceda.description: Italo-Turkish war: Italy gains possession of Libya and the Dodecanese Islands.

3fd5e0cb-c3b5-56cb-911b-f8250f6e629c.name: Treaty of Lausanne
3fd5e0cb-c3b5-56cb-911b-f8250f6e629c.description: 24 July: Treaty of Lausanne, which officially dissolves the Ottoman Empire.

3ff42eed-9116-5398-8f28-e68deb78aea6.description: Great Seljuk Empire is founded by Tughril Beg.

4042dc9f-88b1-598c-a239-a83682f1058b.description: Saracen raid on the Lerins Islands (the most significant of a series of raids on the Provençal coast). The monks taken are bought back through the Abbey of Saint-Victor.

405ce77a-8dfe-54f7-8fcf-62e914fe9e08.description: The ‘Fundamental law’ for military territory (the so-called ‘Vojna krajina’ of the Varaždin and Karlovac military district) in Croatia is established.

407082c9-f7f9-5726-8678-89804c243ef5.description: Defeat of the Klis, the last southern fortress. Ottomans constitute the Sanđak of Klis.

4081b08b-c5ec-5ae8-a186-1eb79b2a0d5a.description: Badr Al-Jamali, the Fatimid vizier, consolidates Cairo’s walls while extending its perimeter.

4081d6fa-5d80-56a2-9ef3-1bb154005ea3.description: Compromise with the House of Habsburg (activated by Ferenc Deák on the Hungarian side). Emperor Franz Joseph I crowned King of Hungary in Buda. Birth of the Austro-Hungarian Monarchy.

41204c10-4ff6-558d-8cab-bc6fcc7e525a.description: Babylon (the Roman settlement south of present-day Cairo) capitulates to the Muslim armies led by Amr ibn al-'As.The first Islamic capital of Egypt, Fustat, is founded.

415862c6-3b5a-5779-961a-b814e4cf1d07.description:
Moorish rebellion in the Alpujarras.  
Risings in the Netherlands.

4158faf2-bdc2-5dce-b596-c5084591557f.name: First World War
4158faf2-bdc2-5dce-b596-c5084591557f.description: World War I is declared and fought.

41779435-72d2-5d45-8768-1dceddd75d06.description: The Second Crusades arrive in Anatolia on the way to the Holy Lands.

41c83dd7-921e-5b8b-b4a6-27f412fa3e00.description: Chlothar I, son of Clovis, becomes the sole ruler of the Franks, having previously shared his kingdom with his brothers.

4232ff9c-1256-5deb-96fe-5d0ebb21e721.description: Bey Husayn bin ‘Ali founds the dynasty that will run the country until 1881 independently, and then under the French protectorate until 20 March 1956. Eighteen different beys come into power. The word bey refers to a political-military position dating back to the Turkish conquest, like pasha and dey.

426811d5-e488-578e-bf2f-ed6b071df91f.name: First parliament in the German history is being established
426811d5-e488-578e-bf2f-ed6b071df91f.description: Establishment of the first parliament in German history (at the Paulskirche, Frankfurt am Main), and elaboration of the German Imperial Constitution.

426d1d37-8fd0-5398-af00-f51502b04de6.description: During the reign of Abu Hammu Musa I, the Tachfiniya madrasa is built in Tlemcen, the town is fortified and the kingdom is expanded to Constantine and Béjaia.

42bcc0c6-2c2d-56d5-9824-e015cd16a1ca.description: Three years after Scottish victory at Largs, Alexander III of Scotland and Magnus IV of Norway sign the treaty of Perth, handing sovereignty over the Western Isles and the Isle of Man to Scotland.

42cec425-fe67-5db6-9273-f3e6dbac1020.description: Penda establishes his kingdom of Mercia as the pre-eminent Anglo-Saxon realm after defeating and killing Oswald of Northumbria at the Battle of Maserfield.

433360bc-e2c9-5614-a09f-7d06bf6e2a56.name: A series of incidents provoke the intervention of the French army
433360bc-e2c9-5614-a09f-7d06bf6e2a56.description: A series of incidents provoke the intervention of the French army when in August 1907 the French land in Casablanca and occupy Oujda, Casablanca and Fez, despite opposition from Germany.

43a6bdfe-913d-53ed-a7e1-d1f54dbc4dee.description: Aqaba Castle is established on the shore of the Red Sea during the reign of the Mamluk Sultan Qansawh al-Ghawri.

43a82bf6-3fd0-5e78-b728-fb49dce467ea.description: Spanish presence in the coastal towns of Mers el-Kébir (1505), Oran (1509), Algiers (1510) and Béjaia (1510).

43dd3e00-777b-59a8-9acc-29c4ba3e6d59.description: French ships bombard the town of Salé.

43ede450-465f-5c99-852d-554217fca08e.description: The colonial powers sign the Act of Algeciras, proclaiming the independence of the Sultan of Morocco, the integrity of the empire and the economic equality of the colonial powers.

440f98e6-7968-5b4d-9f22-4d30cae32afd.description: Ahmad al-Mansur starts work on the al-Badi Palace (the Incomparable) in Marrakesh and reorganises sugar production in Chichaoua, Darâ and Essaouira regions.

4420ce42-e991-54b0-8b2d-2aabe2e96f6c.description: The villages of Mount Nablus revolt against the Ottoman governor, refusing to pay taxes after a locust attack destroys their harvest.

44829943-397f-50a4-acae-5a65332f8c8c.description: Jesuits build the Church of St Catherine in Zagreb, from its architecture and inventory one of the most outstanding Jesuit churches in Croatia.

448e2952-7f34-5034-9f9b-bf57836f2d10.description: Expulsion of the Jews and the Muslims.

44b77875-cbba-5a35-a2f4-48014c5867ec.description: On the initiative of the Council of Trent the Bishop of Zagreb, Juraj Drašković, establishes the Zagreb Seminary (Seminarium Clericorum) to promote theology.

44eb6702-267e-5192-a6ab-eb4c560ff6a9.description: Juan Sebastián Elcano completes the first circumnavigation of the globe.

44f2f8e6-56eb-50ea-872a-14c2cdb51258.description: King Charles XII (Karl XII) dies and is succeeded by his sister Ulrika Eleonora the Younger. The royal power is restricted, with more power given to council and parliament.

4500cecf-6397-5924-b9df-815925ebb0c8.name: Kinglake’s tour of the Middle East
4500cecf-6397-5924-b9df-815925ebb0c8.description: The development of steam power brings increased trade and travel to the eastern Mediterranean. This leads to the publication of travel literature and an interest in the archaeology of the Bible. A. W. Kinglake’s *Eothen* is the most widely read of the travel books.

4527189c-23d1-5794-9384-5b409f2418f1.description: Conquest of Cairo by Selim I the Grim.

455df1fc-7f8d-5efe-97db-15681e3f982e.name: The Royal and Parliamentary Titles Act
455df1fc-7f8d-5efe-97db-15681e3f982e.description: The Royal and Parliamentary Titles Act renames parliament to reflect the change following secession of Southern Ireland. The state is now known as the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland.

458024a5-91ec-5bdd-8a07-af31da303332.description: Venice conquers Karlobag attacking Novi Vinodolski, the city of the Frankopans. This marks the beginning of the Austro-Venetian war, at this stage known as the Uskok war.

46074fd4-311b-50a6-8e84-ea49fd4d20a3.description: The first Czech periodical newspaper (Prague). Moravian aristocracy in service of the empire. Viennese artists in Moravia. Development of pilgrimages; church celebrations.

46751acf-b479-5590-9e2a-9b5a81257c3b.description: King Boabdil, the last Nasrid king, takes refuge in Oran then Tlemcen.

46b02563-57d3-5b63-b95d-4ca37ce1335a.name: The popular uprising
46b02563-57d3-5b63-b95d-4ca37ce1335a.description: The popular uprising sounds the death knell for reform. The great figure of this insurrection, ‘Ali bin Ghedham, comes from the region of Kasserine.

46c4cfb1-3593-5170-976b-ba0e420253d1.description: Damascus–Beirut railway (and Damascus–Hijaz railway in 1908) built by German workers reflecting economic and industrial ties between the Ottoman Empire and Germany. The German Emperor William II visits Damascus on November 1898.

46f3181d-ae5c-5da3-9130-643d909e0b19.description: Prague described in narration of Jewish-Arabian merchant Ibn Jákúb. Establishment of first (Benedictine) monasteries and Prague bishopric (974). Foundation of the Czech state under the Przemyslid dynasty.

472d3156-e5df-5b37-bd7e-f55225ad1cec.name: Moroccan resistance
472d3156-e5df-5b37-bd7e-f55225ad1cec.description: Moroccan resistance is spirited, and provokes many Berber revolts. Following the surrender of Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Alkrim, who led the peasant revolts in the Rif (1919–26), France launched a campaign of “pacification” that lasted until 1934.

4752ff39-18ff-59d8-96d5-baeeb4555349.description: Second taifas in al-Gharb. Afonso Henriques recognised as king at the Zamora Conference.

47812d73-1765-51c9-a1f7-9106287d7a3c.description: Tunis taken by the Ottoman privateer Barbarossa Khayr al-Din Pasha.

47a1f2b0-9844-5245-b45b-dd2a1c34746e.description: The British and Austrian fleets with the support of the Ottomans attack Palestinian shores, putting an end to Egyptian rule. European influences, including architectural, began to appear in the landscape.

47c305a3-f4e7-5d68-999a-faa2b8aa5b4b.description: Sykes-Picot Agreement between France and Britain divides the eastern Arab countries between both countries; Palestine is allocated to Britain.

47eafb93-3dec-56e8-a95c-532def54b84d.description: The first colonial exhibition opens in Marseille under the auspices of Jules Charles-Roux.

481332a0-4c39-547a-aaf4-d49d9a16b02d.description: The Swedish Missionary Society is founded.

48133435-09eb-53ab-b185-f93d5f3346e1.description: Barbarossa’s fleet comes to the aid of the French in their struggle against Charles V.

49101bbd-fd62-5af9-8332-7152a64fb22f.description: Foundation of the abbey at Alcobaça.

496ad0eb-f1dc-5b9b-8da1-c440a8be3b8c.description: Carthage conquered by the Arabs under the leadership of Hassan ibn Numan.

49b1ea1c-4154-5de9-a06e-f7b48091e1e2.name: Romania becomes part of the Triple Alliance
49b1ea1c-4154-5de9-a06e-f7b48091e1e2.description: 30 October: by signing a treaty with Austro-Hungary, to which Germany adheres the same day and Italy in 1888, Romania becomes part of the Triple Alliance.

49e447ab-f314-5806-b5f5-033f39e6eb13.description: Death of the Berber resistance fighter Kahina.

4a39af34-47d2-5b95-9bc0-e368cab023ca.name: At the congress of Berlin in June 1878
4a39af34-47d2-5b95-9bc0-e368cab023ca.description: In June the signatories at the Congress of Berlin grant Austria the right to occupy and fully administer Bosnia and Herzegovina for an undetermined period.

4b2fe6a5-e85d-5b5d-ad5f-2a2281ac018d.description: Muslim attack on Santarém, resulting in the death of Abu Ya‘qub Yusuf.

4b44c7bc-b668-5732-b7a9-3d74e28a7366.description: Croats settle in the area between the Adriatic Sea and the Sava and Drava rivers.

4b8b1ac1-fdef-5ff1-bd9d-bc3fc36c1e27.description: Badis, son of al-Mansur, leaves Qalaa for the last time and goes to Béjaia.

4bb80339-3cc4-5f43-bb32-146ee218ab19.description: According to the double conquest theory of Gyula László the origin of the first archaeological finds in the Carpathian basin indicate the presence of the first wave of the Hungarian tribes.

4bf552ac-f39d-59d7-b9e6-ec494b60f204.description: Under Duke Henry of Saxony the term ‘Kingdom of the Germans’ (Regnum teutonicum) is used for the first time.

4c20974b-4462-568c-b57b-1f721ff80056.description: Birth of the first organised Tunisian nationalist party named the Destour after the constitutions, suspended since 30 April 1864.

4c2c72ca-f944-55e9-a890-4e06fc17bac5.description: Prolific historiographical and encyclopaedic writing in the Mamluk period. Three authors focused on urban topography of Damascus are Ibn ‘Abd al-Hadi (d. 1503), al-Nu’aymi (d.1520) and Ibn Tulun (d.1546).

4c5520e5-28db-5680-8a1c-cad3e9a665c0.description: Battle of Alcácer Quibir (also known as Battle of the Three Kings) during which King Sebastian dies.

4c7d31a5-4c08-5953-ac0a-9058010e9734.description: The Buda printing house of András Hess publishes his *Chronica Hungarorum*, a chronicle of Hungary. Fruitless negotiations with Emperor Friedrich III lead Mátyás I to occupy Vienna in 1485.

4c9f1e73-78be-543a-ada9-45f90963999e.description: Count Ferenc Széchenyi donates his library and collections to the Hungarian nation. This is the nucleus of the National Museum of Hungary and of the National Széchenyi Library.

4cb7338d-726c-597d-b2b5-2bf4487370c3.description: Dynastic union between Castile and Aragon through Isabel I and Ferdinand II.

4d364b05-cc1a-5137-92cc-adf2648c528e.description: Construction of the Sidi Abdarrahman mausoleum to house his tomb and the necropolis that formed around it.

4d8480d4-69c3-54c8-8ab2-240c5f2784bc.description: Independent emirate with ‘Abd al-Rahman I (Umayyad dynasty).

4d87d64c-3e45-5ad9-b697-61f6ff3f1759.description: Genoa sells Corsica to France one year before the birth of Napoleon Bonaparte.

4d8c1c25-24e2-533a-84ea-3895341682a8.description: Fall of Jerusalem to the Franks.

4daf1c53-294e-5b97-8c94-86a42bc8918a.description: Karak Castle is built by Payen le Boutellier. It is named Crac de Moab or simply le Crac by the Franks. It was a very important castle to Crusaders due to its position as a watch centre of the Islamic army movements.

4dc5a0b8-04a6-512d-ac75-6ef210a6a2cb.name: Creation of the United Principalities of Wallachia and Moldavia
4dc5a0b8-04a6-512d-ac75-6ef210a6a2cb.description: 19 August: the Ottoman Empire, Austria, Russia, Prussia, Piedmont, the UK and France sign the Paris Convention marking the creation of the United Principalities of Wallachia and Moldavia, with separate rulers, legislative and executive powers, and only two institutions in common (Supreme Court of Appeals and central legislative commission). The convention replaces the Organic Regulations, becoming the new constitution of the United Principalities.

4dd015c9-34bf-551c-b584-d072c3d9fc51.name: In 1853 started the War of Krimaia
4dd015c9-34bf-551c-b584-d072c3d9fc51.description: The Crimean War starts in October 1853. On one side is the Russian Empire and on the other the Ottoman Empire, the British Empire, France and the Kingdom of Sardinia. Greece participates with a volunteer corps of 1,000 men as one of Russia’s few allies.

4dd40d00-a8e3-5a70-9a14-9452ce7a029a.description: During the lifetime of Saint Boniface, an English missionary who lived from c. 675 to 754, the tribes in Germany become Christians.

4e2bb256-d175-543c-9a34-3932839a8a99.description: King of Portugal attacks the Algarve region.

4e477f9f-7e9e-5b5f-98d2-f95c52c6274c.name: Development and rearmament
4e477f9f-7e9e-5b5f-98d2-f95c52c6274c.description: Development and rearmament (*Aufrüstung*) of the German Navy.

4e65e772-0a02-5bc0-b0f5-337190cf98d8.description: The Battle of Hattin. The rise of the Ayyubid dynasty as a successful force against the Crusaders, combined with cultural and demographic changes, transforms the face of Palestine after many years of Crusader control.

4e7ceac9-496f-530a-b3a6-6da81ccd6df5.name: Revolution of February
4e7ceac9-496f-530a-b3a6-6da81ccd6df5.description: Revolution of February 1848: Louis-Philippe abdicates and the Republic is proclaimed.

4e93cc09-17e7-5569-bac4-9f0f7b94a32f.name: Mulay Sulayman and trade policy
4e93cc09-17e7-5569-bac4-9f0f7b94a32f.description: In relation to trade policy, Mulay Sulayman opposes the liberalism of his father Muhammad Ibn ‘Abd Allah by passing an edict in 1814 imposing a 50 per cent duty on imports, and takes restrictive measures by banning the export of most Moroccan commodities to Europe, including grain, oil, wool, animal hides and livestock. The years of drought and swarms of locusts that devastated all crops between 1810 and 1816 caused a shortage of basic commodities, price increases and famine, on top of the plague epidemics that swept the country. All of these factors necessarily weakened the country financially and demographically. This could help to explain the inward-looking policies adopted by the sovereign Mulay Sulayman, who—according to some historical sources—claimed that he did not need Europe and hoped that Europe did not need him. A desperate and exhausted Mulay Sulayman resigned and chose his nephew Mulay ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Hisham as his successor.

4ec80c98-e99f-5e84-a520-9924c20c2b97.description: Al-Salih Ayyub builds up an army of Turkish slaves and houses them in his fortress on Roda island in the Nile. They come to be known as the Bahri Mamluks.

4f4821d8-4fc4-5539-9381-abc32c175b40.name: Sykes-Picot Agreements
4f4821d8-4fc4-5539-9381-abc32c175b40.description: British interests in the Middle East are driven partly by the British Indian administration and partly by the strategic alliance with France. Mark Sykes for Britain and George Picot for France come to a diplomatic agreement to divide the Ottoman Levantine possessions for their respective countries. This conflicts with an earlier British promise of independence.

4f5c68b0-eb71-5363-9d15-78b719a872dc.description: Byzantine Emperor Justinian orders the construction of St. Catherine’s Monastery at the foot of Mount Moses in Central Sinai. It became the third pilgrimage site after Jerusalem and Rome.

4fa5b084-ccee-51a0-888e-441a0eadc4e7.name: Second empire becomesmore liberal
4fa5b084-ccee-51a0-888e-441a0eadc4e7.description: After an authoritarian period (1852–60), during which time freedoms are severely restricted and political opponents are forced into exile, the Second Empire is declared and the political climate becomes more liberal and the economy grows.

4fd74db0-e844-5e21-9d9e-dfa3dda881be.description: Dubrovnik recognises the authority of Venice, which will last until 1358. In that period Dubrovnik was obliged to pay Venice annual tribute and to accept Venetians as its dukes and archbishops.

4feb54ce-0f2f-5592-8f51-c16b2b766eea.description: In Ireland, half the potato crop fails followed by almost the entire crop of 1846; around one million people subsequently die in the Irish Famine between 1845 and 1851.

5001b852-cd6c-5311-8e47-c6bc520dca86.description: Almoravid invasion following the Christian conquest of Toledo. Almoravid victory at the Battle of Sagrajas or Zallaqa (Badajoz).

50ac747b-311e-5615-8daf-488a530d5ee7.description: Turks occupy a large part of north Croatia.

511016af-9b07-5c9f-8d6c-a30b2ea930ec.description: The Portuguese take the town of Qsar al-Saghir.

511ce86e-19e7-5ace-969b-b24404fb8218.name: The Ottoman Sultan Abdulhamid built the Hijaz Railway
511ce86e-19e7-5ace-969b-b24404fb8218.description: Under the Ottoman Sultan ‘Abd al-Hamid, the Hijaz Railway is built, running from Istanbul to the Medina (Madinah) province.

52217393-d8ee-5402-bd51-bded5e32a4d9.description:
Petar Zrinski and Fran Krsto Frankopan executed in Wiener Neustadt (Bečko Novo Mjesto).  
Building of Dubrovnik Cathedral after the plan of A. Buffalini from Urbino which displays features of developed Roman Baroque.

523f9595-4283-5b18-9a26-9225bab37429.description: On 4 October a torrential stream destroys the buildings, markets and mosque of Ajlun.

524c3bcc-fc78-5fc9-8cf8-bd35b6f1c912.description: The Ottomans, led by Sinan Pasha, oust the Spanish from Tunis and annex the town to the Ottoman empire.

526938cd-a1ad-5502-b1e0-8baba34b9223.name: Otto von Bismarck becomes Prussian prime minister
526938cd-a1ad-5502-b1e0-8baba34b9223.description: Otto von Bismarck becomes prime minister of Prussia.

52b45bf8-f440-5884-9c8b-7b9eedbddc86.description: Charles IV appointed Margrave of Moravia.

52dd8832-74f2-57f4-bd89-3e527329eb34.description: The Italian Communist Party is formed.

52f62145-5642-55a4-937b-73eed89a215b.description: Olomouc bishopric promoted to archbishopric. Foundation of a bishopric in Brno. Abolition of serfdom. Riots of the Evangelicals in Wallachia.

53111dfb-b9b9-5f55-9240-9b6e026d8d53.description: Galileo is tried by the Inquisition for his scientific theories.

5327b6d4-3a65-5293-a606-ea64db46f1fb.description: The Byzantine Emperor Justinianus (later Justinian) grants the ally of the Byzantines, al-Haritha ibn Jibla, the Arab-Christian ruler of the Ghassan tribe who settled in Syria and Jordan, the title ‘Baselues’ (king).

535178d2-75c5-5c3e-a065-3ec6deee5020.description: Pope Alexander III’s papal bull Manifestis Probatum recognises the king of Portugal.

536db52d-e1ff-5510-aa13-42211a295930.description: Establishment of the Czech Engineering School in Prague. New patent against non-Catholics. Heresy declared a crime against the state, non-Catholics punishable by death.

53b21358-7f48-567e-9c5d-c206eeb896ca.description: Major fire in Umayyad Mosque of Damascus, addressed by a major renovation endeavour by the Ottoman Empire. Thus the current hall is a late-Ottoman renovation with strong Western stylistic influences.

53e04a9b-0217-5a73-929c-4af490d49239.description: Heracles (r. 610–41) reconquers Palestine and the Emperor brings back the Holy Cross to Jerusalem. Restoration projects begin all over Palestine and in Jerusalem in particular.

53ea5d1e-6589-5473-abc2-37eb450a38d0.name: Visit of Ottoman Sultan to France and Britain
53ea5d1e-6589-5473-abc2-37eb450a38d0.description: The 1850s and 1860s sees close political, commercial and cultural relations between the Ottoman Empire and Britain. The zenith of this relationship is the state visit of Ottoman Sultan ‘Abd al-‘Aziz to France and then Britain. The Prince of Wales then reciprocates with a visit to Constantinople, Damascus and Jerusalem in 1869.

54547a63-b6e6-52c9-be7a-11522e48f89e.description: Start of the reign of Louis VI. Establishment and growth of the commune movement in France.

546c0371-e65e-5d2e-9627-942bfe0f2dea.description: The Battle of Mohács: the 75–80 000 Turkish soldiers defeat the Hungarian army of 25,000 men. King Lajos II dies. Both János I (Szapolyai) and Ferdinand I became Hungarian kings.

546f4c69-4e94-55e6-bba7-ca5df34c3ff0.description: Siege of Constantinople by the Muslim Arabs.

547fd8d0-cdb7-50cf-813e-0a6d738ad687.description: A Royal Navy fleet led by Admiral Lord Nelson in HMS Victory destroys the French and Spanish fleets at the Battle of Trafalgar; Nelson is killed in the battle.

5480a2e9-b3cf-5698-8812-798710f49173.name: World War I
5480a2e9-b3cf-5698-8812-798710f49173.description: On 25 July, at the onset of World War I, ‘Abbas Hilmi II is in Constantinople where he suffers wounds to his hands and cheeks during a failed assassination attempt. On 5 November of that same year, when Britain declares war on Turkey, ‘Abbas is accused of deserting his country because he did not return home forthwith. In addition, because the British believe that he has been plotting against their rule, when the Ottoman Empire joins the central powers in the war, Britain declares Egypt an independent Sultanate under British Protectorate on 18 December, and ‘Abbas is deposed.

551ebb0f-8760-5cad-a847-7b8053f88589.description: Ottoman Sultan Sulayman the Magnificent orders the establishment of Ma’an pilgrimage station.

553de630-835e-58f5-9cb8-cf2c1f333d0b.name: Setembrismo - Lower middle classes rebellion and fight against corruption and higher middle class privileges
553de630-835e-58f5-9cb8-cf2c1f333d0b.description: Period of Setembrismo: lower-middle-class rebellion against corruption and upper-middle-class privileges. An industrialisation process takes off to counteract foreign dominance. To overcome the loss of Brazilian revenues the colonisation of African possessions is boosted. The slave trade is prohibited in 1836 by abolitionist Marquis of Sá da Bandeira.

555365e0-aaa3-513b-bd8c-ebedd6fe2db2.description: War with England returns. Establishment of the Continental System and collapse of French trade in the Mediterranean.

55695aa1-b0a9-5f4e-97b5-dea801f7d659.description: Muhammad al-Ikhshid (r. 935–46) conquers Palestine and annexes it to Egypt.

559148d2-07ca-5cb2-a72c-19fa7da07c0e.name: Russian-Ottoman war
559148d2-07ca-5cb2-a72c-19fa7da07c0e.description: After the Russian–Ottoman war of 1806–12 Russia annexes the eastern part of Moldavia (Bessarabia).

559f59cb-5ac1-5e93-9214-b9f88cac905d.description: The Treaty of the Pyrenees ends the Franco-Spanish war and confirms French possession of Roussillon. The union between Louis XIV and Marie-Thérèse lays the foundation for a solid alliance, despite the King of France renouncing his and his successors’ right to the Spanish throne.

55a62e78-aeb7-50e8-85b5-4686d142ee47.description: Victory of Charles Martel (688–741) of the Carolingian Dynasty at the battle of Tours and Poitiers (southern France) over Arab insurgents leads to their retreat to the southern valley of the Rhone.

55b5ac77-fa3e-5cfe-b9a7-1ebaf09d93bb.description: The Abbasid Caliph al-Ma’mun (r. 813–33) orders the restoration of the Dome of the Rock.

5613686d-95e8-539a-9ddd-370f90efee48.description: On 28 May the Transjordan Emirate is established, headed by Prince Abdullah I, son of Sharif Husayn, who later became King Abdullah the founder of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan.

565254cf-3e05-59ae-a148-c24a6942fa18.description: Código de las Siete Partidas, a return to Roman law with the unification of Castilian laws.

5678f5be-3e06-5d07-abad-a8670a5be0f1.description: The German Templars establish their first settlement in Haifa, followed in 1873 in Sarona (near Jaffa) and Jerusalem.

56ad7d25-7c26-56a7-a9a4-c9f725bec018.description: Vandal occupation and the Berber kingdom of the Djeddars.

574c48c1-ec52-5fc7-9120-045bf9d0c20c.description: Proclamation of the ‘Destour’ during the reign of Sadok Bey, the first modern constitution in the Muslim world.

57582bc6-4423-583c-942f-d77effb8e2f4.description: Meeting at Mellalah (Béjaia) between the mahdi Ibn Tumart and ‘Abd al-Mu’min, founders of the Almohad dynasty.

578433d4-58b0-5d8e-a4fd-1cb6e7b3c05c.description: Start of the First Crusade, preached by Pope Urban II at Clermont. The People’s Crusade is mostly annihilated, but the Princes’ Crusade reaches Palestine and takes Jerusalem in 1099, establishing the Frankish Kingdom in the east.

57abb70e-9dc2-5504-be1e-d548144147d9.description: A new national law codex is published. It replaces the earlier medieval laws.

57e52823-8101-54ba-b97f-059ab665773c.description: Foundation of the first German university in Prague by Emperor Charles IV.

58310e59-46aa-5b4e-bc32-362f0b4fed0a.name: Jamal Pasha
58310e59-46aa-5b4e-bc32-362f0b4fed0a.description: Turkish commander Jamal Pasha initiates a blockade of the entire eastern Mediterranean coast. Lebanon witnesses thousands of deaths from widespread famine and plague.

5845f393-ba6d-5c40-9ef1-3e6e4b3364fb.name: British impose a peace treaty
5845f393-ba6d-5c40-9ef1-3e6e4b3364fb.description: The British impose a Peace Treaty on the Qawasim and other sheikhs of the Arab littoral of the Gulf. The signing is preceded by a preliminary agreement forcing the sheikhs to turn over all remaining vessels, fortifications and weapons in exchange for the restoration of their fishing and pearling vessels. The Treaty enjoins all signatories to fly a specific red-and-white flag.

588f15d9-d644-513d-b9bf-aeca23c44bbd.name: Muhammad Ali kills the Mamluks
588f15d9-d644-513d-b9bf-aeca23c44bbd.description: On 1 March, Muhammad ‘Ali invites some 470 Mamluk beys to the Citadel for a feast to celebrate his son’s imminent departure for Mecca. When the feasting is over the Mamluks mount their lavishly decorated horses and are led in procession down the narrow, high-sided defile, below what is now the Police Museum. As they approach Bab al-Azab, the great gates swing closed and gunfire rains down on them from above. After the fusillades, Muhammad ‘Ali’s soldiers wade in with swords and axes to finish the job. Legend relates that only one Mamluk escaped alive, leaping over the wall on his horse.

58905020-ab87-5e94-a3d4-66d653a6cbc1.description: The first mosque in Egypt is built in Bilbis, east of the Delta, to honour the martyrs and 120 companions of the Prophet who died in battle there during the Arab invasion of Egypt. It followed the ground plan of the Prophet's mosque in Medina.

58937cc9-8073-5f41-a01b-586172119fd1.description: Four knights who believe they are working on the implicit orders of King Henry II murder Thomas Becket, the Archbishop of Canterbury, in Canterbury Cathedral.

58e49658-5d56-5cee-a255-546c446b7c9c.description: The discovery of the Cape of Good Hope has an adverse effect on trade in Egypt.

58f04dcc-14c3-570e-91a1-26058adc783d.description: The reign of Henry II (1002–24) sees the establishment of a feudal system, particularly in Northern Italy, which will leave a lasting mark on Italy’s social and economic make-up.

58fd9645-d24f-5ff7-9e13-9e18a9a195d5.description: Reforms under Emperor Joseph II: tolerance patent permitting non-Catholicism (Catholicism remains the official religion). Abolition of serfdom. Closure of monasteries not dedicated to publicly beneficial work.

5902e9f0-1f5e-58a0-a416-f603b26bff55.description: Revolt of the Sicilian Vespers against Sicily’s French Angevin rulers. Aragon emerges victorious in Sicily, which is separated politically from Southern Italy.

592cecff-2d36-5a77-98f1-8da2b13b45fb.description: Birth of the Nasrid Kingdom of Granada.

592e7efc-8d9e-5819-bb5f-31a387a052cb.description: Decisive victory of the Almohads over the nomads at Sétif. Widespread use of Almohad coinage as the industry and commerce of war flourishes. Political unity and religious dogmatism. The apogee of Almohad rule.

592ec00c-9384-51ec-9937-eace81147978.name: Treaty Britain-Morocco
592ec00c-9384-51ec-9937-eace81147978.description: In 1856 a treaty is signed, initiated by Britain in order to strengthen its influence over Morocco and to maintain its naval supremacy in the Mediterranean, which hugely undermines Moroccan sovereignty. This treaty wrested control over the extent of European penetration away from the governing institution of Morocco the Makhzen. The advantages gained by European traders, combined with their superior technique and the quantity of capital behind them, enabled then to monopolise most of the sea trade and to reduce Moroccan players to mere intermediaries.

59535ffd-671f-5e78-8f21-81f325d7570f.name: Serbia became a Kingdom
59535ffd-671f-5e78-8f21-81f325d7570f.description: The first king of Serbia in the modern age is Milan Obrenović, Prince (1822–82) and King (1882–89). From the start of his independent reign, Knez Milan works to build up the military, and sides with Russia in his foreign policy. He declares war on Turkey in 1876, but it ends in Serbia’s defeat due to poorly prepared diplomatic policy. The signing of the Treaty of San Stefano (made between the two countries after the Russo-Turkish War) is followed by an about-face in Knez Milan’s policy as he turns more and more to Austria-Hungary. A decision by the Congress of Berlin in 1878 grants Serbia independence, while the Secret Convention (between Serbia and Austria-Hungary) binds Austria-Hungary into declaring Serbia a kingdom in 1882.

5a1ea0bc-5eaa-51e5-ba81-3c6a7d87d08a.description: Autocracy is introduced under King Charles XI (Karl XI).

5a220c3a-13cf-51aa-aa83-4ae726f3e068.description: The Russian Nestor Chronicle tells of an agreement in this year, stating, among other things, that: If a Rus (Swede) kills a Christian or a Christian a Rus he has to die where he commits this manslaughter. This law is typical for regional Scandinavian jurisdiction. Laws like this were written down in the 13th century, but this is one of very few proofs that they existed much earlier.

5a56a81b-2205-50a5-b646-009dd4131e0f.description: The First World War begins in 1914 in the Balkans before spreading throughout Europe and touching the Mediterranean with the entry of the Ottoman Empire and then Italy (1915) into the war.

5b01dc26-ca6d-5090-9182-1f97b10e501d.name: King Wilhelm
5b01dc26-ca6d-5090-9182-1f97b10e501d.description: King Wilhelm I – later Kaiser (Emperor) of the Second Empire – assumes his regency.

5bce1a44-ff42-5246-adff-a861e0eea35a.description: The end of the Tulunids in Palestine.

5c14846d-9feb-529f-9328-03a7877d33ec.name: Founding of the National Museum
5c14846d-9feb-529f-9328-03a7877d33ec.description: Serbia’s oldest museum, Museum Serbski, now the National Museum in Belgrade, is founded by the Minister of Education Jovan Sterija Popović.

5c561e04-6086-5b89-b5b8-cae35dc41aa8.name: Woodrow Wilson declares his 14 points
5c561e04-6086-5b89-b5b8-cae35dc41aa8.description: Woodrow Wilson declares his “14 points” program in front of Congress.

5c7d87c6-e167-5140-9f9d-ff5c1be46746.description: Napoleon Bonaparte (1804–14) becomes King of Italy.

5cc65d3f-debc-57aa-9b34-78d4fc48acc7.name: The Prussian king Friedrich Wilhelm IV
5cc65d3f-debc-57aa-9b34-78d4fc48acc7.description: The Prussian King Friedrich Wilhelm IV refuses the German Imperial Crown.

5d548ceb-d9a2-52d9-b303-a525b4408e18.description: The war between Germany and France results in a German victory and a proclamation of a German Empire (1871–1918) in Versailles with Wilhelm I of the Hohenzollern Dynasty as German Emperor.

5d82b804-e104-5bff-b26d-3815dc749d68.description: End of the rebellion of Kharijite Abu Yazid (‘the Man of the Donkey’) against the Fatimids.

5dd015f4-0c93-5038-b65a-4c7dcebf0963.description: Sultan Sulayman the Magnificent commissions the huge takiyya in Damascus, a pious and imperial act meant to accommodate and impress pilgrims, under the supervision of famous court architect Sinan.

5dd3075d-46bb-5690-a3eb-2d410fcd6884.name: Commune
5dd3075d-46bb-5690-a3eb-2d410fcd6884.description: When the people of Paris refuse to accept defeat and take up arms the Versailles-based government resist and harshly repress the "Commune".

5e12f1c5-8671-530e-be6f-81f215bfeed4.name: A former Austrian officer
5e12f1c5-8671-530e-be6f-81f215bfeed4.description: Russia recognises Ferdinand of Saxe-Coburg, a former Austrian officer, as the new Prince of Bulgaria.

5e48d6b8-ed2b-53a7-8e62-e7e65d3cb699.description: Al-Mahdi ibn Tumart takes action against the Almoravids to aid the Hargha, Tinmel, Hintata tribes, etc.

5e78536c-7cd6-5345-850f-16b157d05fdc.description: Hildegard von Bingen (1098–1179), a mystic and a composer of hymns who had visions of God, collects her visions in the book Scivias (‘Know the Way’).

5e8d3ab6-e862-58f3-ae9e-1d931d60e54b.description: Sa’id ibn Khalid, a grandson of the third orthodox Caliph ‘Uthman, leads a revolt against the Abbasids at al-Fudayn in Jordan calling for the restitution of the Umayyad caliphate. Abandoned by his companions, his revolt ended.

5e9e3338-513d-5a14-a122-2da2720762e4.description: The composer Richard Wagner (1813–83) writes his opera Tristan and Isolde. This is a new form of musical theatre and musical language which he calls music drama.

5ea85de4-6ad1-5da8-80e7-e340d86d1aab.name: The Republic is proclaimed in Lisbon on 5 October.
5ea85de4-6ad1-5da8-80e7-e340d86d1aab.description: The Republic is proclaimed in Lisbon on 5 October. King Manuel II is forced to exile in England together with his mother Queen Amelia who ends up in her homeland France. A Provisional Government is set up, headed by Teófilo Braga, a well-known respected jurist and writer. The new cabinet ruled until the first republican Constitution was enacted.

5f4ca7bd-5c3d-594c-a744-1806e82465a6.name: Second republic
5f4ca7bd-5c3d-594c-a744-1806e82465a6.description: During the Second Republic a number of social reforms take place, including universal male suffrage and the abolition of slavery. In December 1848 Louis-Napoleon Bonaparte (grand-nephew of Napoleon I) takes over as president of the Republic and reverts to a more conservative political position. He sets up an authoritarian regime by coup d'état (December 1851), and declares himself emperor in 1852.

5f65d4d2-401d-512b-aa01-486fbc8f5134.description: The Slavery Abolition Act makes slavery illegal throughout the British Empire, partly as a result of a ten-year campaign by evangelicals, quakers and methodists.

5f718587-3a77-5868-a61f-c951c2db29c1.description: Deposing of the House of Habsburg. Lajos Kossuth appointed as governor of Hungary. The freedom fight is lost; Hungarian general Görgey capitulates at Világos to the Habsburg’s Russian allies..

5f811e5f-0a1e-5a53-a2b7-09f7dd899f5c.description: Beginning of the Seven Years’ War between Prussia, Austria, Russia and France about the territories of Saxonia and Silesia. Prussia becomes a European power.

5ff73bbd-3cfe-5414-8a1a-e3dc70e1b286.description: Justinian (527–65) becomes the Emperor of Byzantium and sets about reconquering the West, succeeding in destroying the Gothic Kingdom in Italy.

5fffa50a-bb0d-5142-8221-808f5027d8a6.name: Title of khedive for Egyptian governors
5fffa50a-bb0d-5142-8221-808f5027d8a6.description: 8 June: The Egyptian governor receives from the Sublime Porte the title of “khedive,” which provides him legislative independence.

6046c8ef-6db5-5a44-8caf-4c437bee3ef1.description: Diet of Pozsony (Pressburg, today: Bratislava, Slovakia): coronation of Maria Theresia (Theresa), daughter of Karl (Charles) VI, as Queen of Hungary. The diet offers military help for the Habsburgs in the Austrian Succession Wars.

6064a904-43b5-5c03-a1ae-8919ca2276e5.name: Yusuf Bek Butros Karam
6064a904-43b5-5c03-a1ae-8919ca2276e5.description: Yusuf Bek Butros Karam, a Lebanese Maronite born in 1823 fights in the 1860 civil war and leads a rebellion in 1866-67 against the Ottoman Empire’s rule in Mount Lebanon. His proclamations have been interpreted as an early expression of Lebanese nationalism.

60bbb9f9-ccdf-51ef-8ffe-2df92c1028a9.description: French troops besiege Germany. Fighting only ends with the Treaty of the Congress of Vienna (1815). This ultimately results in a reformed Germany.

60d359e4-5723-55aa-a72c-b16e64db0017.description: Al-Azhar mosque becomes a centre for higher religious education under vizier Ya’qub ibn Killis, minister of the Fatimid Caliph al-Aziz Billah.

60d59e9e-7ec2-5d98-9957-b3bac9c7f0f0.description: The town of Béjaia founded by the Hammadid prince al-Nasir. Bab al-Bunud (Gateway of the Standards) and Bab al-Bahr (Gateway of the Sea) erected.

60e0abb3-d972-5461-ab87-276eac092632.description: The inauguration of the Aqsa Mosque by the Umayyad Caliph al-Walid Ibn ‘Abd al-Malik (r. 705–15).

6103a30e-c153-59de-b332-251e72dc1bc4.description: At Nur al-Din's death, his powerful lieutenant Salah al-Din (Saladin) defeats other claimants to the throne, marries Nur al-Din’s wife and is recognised as sultan, becoming founder of the Ayyubid Dynasty.

61264f6f-b22b-5433-93a5-c21f758f3450.description: Phillip III orders the expulsion of Moors from his kingdoms.

618387ff-39ea-513b-be6e-8f87b9c0c023.name: Second Balkan War
618387ff-39ea-513b-be6e-8f87b9c0c023.description: The Second Balkan War begins due to a quarrel between Serbia and Bulgaria over the division of joint conquests. Bulgaria attacks Serbia and Greece in 1923; the Bulgarians are defeated on both fronts. Subsequently, Turkey and Romania declare war on Bulgaria and the Bulgarians soon request an armistice. The war ends with a Peace Treaty signed in Bucharest in August 1913. During the Balkan Wars, Serbia expands its territory by 39,500 square kilometres.

618bca1f-047f-5237-854b-54d69d795327.description: Idris ibn ‘Abdallah (Idris I) takes up residence at Walili, then in the Andalusian Quarter (Adwat al-Andalousiyyin) in Fez, which he founded on the right bank of the Wadi Fez.

61a16d8a-1d45-5af9-977e-81cfe163258c.description: Franz II (1768–1835), Austrian Emperor, lays down the German crown and thus dissolves the Holy Roman Empire of the German Nation.

61a18322-523f-5e0a-b6d7-efae67c4ce92.description: Permanent union of the Christian kingdoms of Castile and Leon.

61bd427f-a05c-527b-9459-8e25e527c4c7.description: Battle of São Mamede. Afonso Henriques takes control of the Portucuese Counties.

61fb2b70-0016-53c5-bc77-fd9ae819195e.description: Kafur al-Ikhshid dies and political and economic strife encourages the Fatimid conquest of Egypt.

6237d70f-6572-5bfd-9e4e-469e0f9fb8c6.description: The erection of al-Mudawara pilgrimage station on the pilgrim route to Mecca, the last station in Jordan before entering Saudi borders.

627c032e-d1d5-5cea-adb2-a0a4eb3e15f3.description: War of Catalonia and Portuguese secession.

629c996b-bda5-57d3-86c9-0704ac1e8c46.description: The peace of Zadar seals the defeat of the Venetian Republic by Louis of Anjou, King of Hungary–Croatia, and marks the reunification of Dalmatia with the Croatian crown within a common kingdom.

62a5e1c8-111e-5e0c-99c1-c922fb7b7bdf.description: James VII (of Scotland) and II (of England) flees to France when William III of Orange, invited by politicians to save England from Roman Catholicism, lands in England.

62df2c36-4d0d-5358-9eec-4a9bd4bbf5cf.description: Ali Bey Al-Kabir revolts against the Ottomans. The revolt is suppressed four years later.

62f41fd3-1860-5be0-9c04-7a6370e10a79.description: Union of the German Reich with the Kingdom of Burgundy under King Konrad II (1024–39) of the Salian Dynasty.

636b3bef-07bf-57f9-843a-faeefcb32adb.description: The battle of ‘Ain Jalut, the first defeat of the Mogul armies and the rise of the Mamluk power in Greater Syria in addition to Egypt.

637a86d3-8ea7-5969-af92-f14ecb20fde8.description: Friedrich II (1215–50), Emperor of the Hohenstaufen Dynasty and King of Sicily, becomes King of Jerusalem during the Fifth Crusade. He was influenced by Islamic traditions.

63b574c5-53e1-5522-85b2-bfade2f695b1.description: Death of Meister Eckhart (1260–1328), a Dominican monk who was a theologian, philosopher and mystic. His writings on metaphysics and mysticism were of importance for the intellectual spirit of the late Middle Ages.

63e6557e-2ecd-5d8c-8936-66e5e1e12bbf.name: The battle of al-Wajba
63e6557e-2ecd-5d8c-8936-66e5e1e12bbf.description: The Battle of al-Wajba is a victory for Sheikh Jassim and Qatar. This represents a decisive moment in the nation's history, asserting Qatar's independence from direct Ottoman interference.

64b55451-65d4-56b5-925b-b3fc5a3df271.description: Travelling artists perform the first opera in Zagreb *I Filosofi imaginari* composed by Giovanni Paisiello, which marks the beginning of the new repertoire including Rossini, Bellini, etc.

64b759a0-0c63-51d3-8f8d-c0ed61c040d0.description: Jesuits build their church in Varaždin dedicated to the Assumption of Virgin. The church is considered to follow the style of the Roman church Il Gesù.

64d43c4e-1e03-5a4e-add5-79bdafe39326.description: Voyage of Bartolomeu Dias around the south of Africa to the Indian Ocean. On his return, he discovers Cape of Storms, renamed the Cape of Good Hope by John II.

6505f97d-840c-59a2-9be7-ed9a0b7af7ed.description: The Church of St Donat in Zadar, first dedicated to Holy Trinity, is built in the 9th century, a great example of Byzantine architecture and the largest circular church of the Carolingian era in Europe.

651725bb-bdea-51a5-a287-08624bc9f901.description: General Sir Edmund Allenby conquers Jerusalem, declaring the end of Ottoman rule over Palestine. The Balfour Declaration (named after the Foreign Minister of England) promises the Zionist movement a homeland in Palestine.

651e94f5-0f70-5505-ba14-e1290675437d.name: The Austrian Government annexes Bosnia and Herzegovina
651e94f5-0f70-5505-ba14-e1290675437d.description: The Austrian Government proclaims the annexation of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the evacuation of Austrian troops from the Sanjak on 6 October. The Austrian annexation then escalates into a major international crisis, which sees Serbia’s future hope to establish a Yugoslav empire shattered.

65271ccb-011c-5700-8dcd-1bda086f845a.description: Arudj defends the town of Jijel.

653e8114-1347-5a8c-8353-1dcadec7cbb6.description: Pippin of Herstal, Mayor of the Palace of Austrasia, reunites the Frankish kingdom, which had disintegrated under the last of the Merovingians.

654a2977-9950-5731-a830-9fab6a5d5cc3.name: War against Greeks in western Anatolia
654a2977-9950-5731-a830-9fab6a5d5cc3.description: 30 August: Final battle in western Anatolia results in the collapse of the Greek army.

6556f937-3643-57de-a5ff-8c093240ecaf.description: Ahmad Ibn Tulun, the Abbasid-appointed governor of Egypt, grows more independent and takes over Syria.

658ef359-7ae8-5fe3-83de-ac691a869bf9.description: As a part of the freedom fight of Prince Ferenc Rákóczi II against the Habsburgs (began in 1703) the Parliament of Ónod declares the Habsburg dynasty deposed in Hungary.

65b4cbb2-b2c4-5110-b66c-5e9731bfc694.description: Selim III, a dedicated reformer, ascends the throne in the same year as the French Revolution.

65e735d6-1884-5c70-8457-64927186fe06.description: Sultan Selim I enters Damascus and builds a shrine over the tomb of Sufi Sheikh Ibn al-Arabi, with a mosque and a takiyya nearby, as the first Ottoman imperial buildings in Damascus.

66283311-38ae-55c1-9fb3-7a442949d310.name: Austria ceded Lombardy but not Venetia to Napoleon III
66283311-38ae-55c1-9fb3-7a442949d310.description: At the Peace of Zürich (10 November) Austria cedes Lombardy, but not Venetia, to Napoleon III; in turn, Napoleon hands the province over to the Kingdom of Sardinia.

6667dec1-e328-5965-82d9-bb3b212c863b.description: Beginning with the Battle of Tertry in 687 the Carolingian Dynasty rules over larger parts of the Germanic tribes.

666de82c-9280-5285-9446-d5a099a8f23e.description: The Great Fire of London destroys more than 13,000 houses and nearly 90 parish churches, as well as St Paul’s Cathedral, the Guildhall and the Royal Exchange.

66844d4f-f8ec-5442-ad5e-74fde0d86bee.description: Provence becomes part of France. The Kings of France inherit the claims of the Angevins. Start of the Italian Wars.

66a8e1ca-4616-5f53-9872-84e0851682cf.description: The Kharijites leave Tahert and take refuge at Sedrata.

66e2c0cc-d8f8-5391-be7d-5738f2dfbd15.description: King Charlemagne (768–814) is crowned as emperor in Rome by Pope Leo III (795–816).

66fc6d34-d859-55c8-9fe1-3ecc6fa4011c.description: Tunis taken by King Charles V of Spain.

67114bbc-bcc1-5ef7-89b5-bdf1410a7e63.description: Foundation letter of the Benedictine abbey in Tihany by King András I (its Latin text contains the first Hungarian text fragment). András was buried in the abbey church in 1060.

671e6324-d0a5-5e33-9558-75f954c4ecfa.description: Birth of the illustrious scholar Ibn Khaldun in Tunis.

672fd0d2-785a-512c-8f61-97375cdda834.name: Peace of Saint-Germain-en-Laye
672fd0d2-785a-512c-8f61-97375cdda834.description: Austria signs the Peace of Saint-Germain-en-Laye with the Entente Powers.

67fc703f-3ef6-570f-8ff8-e3d369080329.description: Olomouc Agreement: Matthias Corvinus rules Moravia, Silesia and Lusatia, Vladislav Jagellon rules Bohemia. After Matthias’s death (1490) Vladislav appointed King of Hungary.

68099065-5a0b-5db3-b89d-67cf2f079a0a.description: Start of the Avignon Papacy: under the direct influence of the King of France, the popes set up the papal residence in Avignon.

6831e6f1-4837-50b1-abf4-e28f9350296d.description: The death of poet Mevlana Rumi (born in Belh, Afghanistan, (1207?).

68514ab3-8233-519f-b8f9-c20abd15aff7.description: At the Peace of Kiel Sweden and Norway are united under one monarch in a personal union.

6868d06f-73a3-5df8-ab72-5906914451c4.description: In the church of Our Lady of Pirates in Komiža on the island of Vis Stjepan Killarevich from Krakow builds one of three preserved 17th-century organs in Croatia.

68cc7749-b76a-5b2a-8e4b-0fbb44ebc5d3.description: The famous French philosopher René Descartes arrives in Sweden, invited by Queen Christina. He dies in Stockholm the following year.

69164915-60ac-5881-b75c-9d3dc8c8e62d.description: Zadar rebels against Venice and allies with Hungary.

6a19443b-3afd-5ccb-88d6-3432a6f11e0e.description: Defeat of the Moroccan army by the occupying French forces in Algeria at the Battle of Isly.

6a1fa53b-578d-5d8e-956d-417412847f45.description: Consecration of the worship of the patron saint of Algiers Alger ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Thaalibi.

6a3d1e30-1204-5b2c-b985-91771bd6d521.description: The Croatian–Hungarian King Bela IV grants the Golden Bull to Gradec, as a token of appreciation for the citizens who provided him shelter during the Tatarian invasion.

6a4fe4b4-097b-5df9-9864-32aebc48c49f.description: The Mirdasid dynasty takes control of Aleppo amidst numerous rivalling emirates, thanks to its skilful diplomacy, particularly with the court of Badr al-Din Lu’lu’ in Mosul.

6a8e5a77-1843-5ea2-9525-f6305af2a714.description: The papal residence moved back to Rome from Avignon during the pontificate of Gregory XI (1370–8).

6aa487ad-149e-585f-9b86-18ae6d154edd.description: On 29 October the Croatian Parliament proclaims Croatia’s administrative relations with Austria and Hungary void. In December the Kingdom of Serbs, Croats and Slovenes is formed.

6abfc0a9-8e84-51e0-90a9-66ba1eba10dc.name: Emperor Wilhelm II visits Tangiers
6abfc0a9-8e84-51e0-90a9-66ba1eba10dc.description: Emperor Wilhelm II visits Tangiers on 3 March 1905, keen to prevent diplomatic isolation of his country and to safeguard Germany’s economic interests.

6ac1e7a4-0763-567a-9aab-392a58ec9f2a.description: Promulgation of a charter during the reign of Muhammad Pasha Bey guaranteeing the rights of his Tunisian subjects and people living in Tunisia.

6b04af09-19b5-5457-868e-6f71c2bce7af.name: Formation of Turkish National Assembly
6b04af09-19b5-5457-868e-6f71c2bce7af.description: 23 April: Formation of Turkish National Assembly in Ankara.

6c13c8ef-71f1-599b-a5c8-987c27675585.description: Construction of the Great Mosque of Kairouan.

6c1930cf-088a-5c20-9e5a-8bbd43461b7e.name: Queen Maria II
6c1930cf-088a-5c20-9e5a-8bbd43461b7e.description: Queen Maria II (1819–53) regains the crown after her father’s death and the liberals’ victory. The Queen has to cope with the transition from absolutism to constitutionalism and disputes between opposing factions, conservatives on one side (Cartismo supporters of the 1826 Charter) and radicals on the other (Vintismo defenders of the Constitution of 1822).

6c2f1fa9-6204-570a-8919-6497aa052e19.description: First maritime conquests of the Muslims, occupying Cyprus.

6c42f919-7aa0-50cf-bc11-abfe289fbdff.description: The town of Sedrata destroyed. Kharijite exodus to Mzab.

6c8c4543-b87f-530b-b89e-d308315a1d76.description: The Abbasid Caliph al-Ma’mun issues a memorial golden coin carrying the name of ‘Jerusalem’.

6c90399e-fd36-52e6-b726-fc34a75f04ca.name: First Napoleonic invasion
6c90399e-fd36-52e6-b726-fc34a75f04ca.description: First Napoleonic invasion. Prince Regent João (1767–1826, crowned in 1816) transfers the court and the seat of political power to Brazil, avoiding being deposed and replaced by a Napoleonic nominee as in other European kingdoms. In Portugal, Beresford, the British governor, intervenes in Portuguese general politics disregarding national needs.

6cca5be6-d210-57c4-8fdc-8943c89de1f8.name: Local governments in Ajlun, Balqa and Kerak
6cca5be6-d210-57c4-8fdc-8943c89de1f8.description: The people of Transjordan, encouraged by the UK, establish local governments in Ajlun, Balqa and Karak. British advisers are assigned to help these governments.

6d0430be-e12b-542b-ba75-56e586778e2e.name: The British government becomes effectively ruler of the Trucial Coast
6d0430be-e12b-542b-ba75-56e586778e2e.description: The British government effectively becomes the ruler of the Trucial Coast when the sheikhs are forced to pledge that neither they nor their descendants will enter agreements with or grant territorial rights to any government or their representatives other than Britain.

6d36b18e-248c-56d7-b27c-f1a061880805.description: Death of Clovis, the Merovingian king who converted to Catholicism, won control of most of the Frankish kingdoms and took Aquitaine from the Visigoths.

6d4f9ede-e846-50b7-b846-12f530be1e23.description: It was around this time that the first Viking expeditions to the East, conducted by people who called themselves Svear (Swedes), are successful enough to bring home the first Arabic silver coins.

6d539e15-d25c-57d0-9714-8ef44ea4c2e8.name: Italy trying to annex Rome
6d539e15-d25c-57d0-9714-8ef44ea4c2e8.description: Uprising in Rome demanding unification with Italy. At the same time, Garibaldi leads an expedition of volunteers that enters the Papal States and tries to seize Rome. Roman rebels are defeated and executed. Garibaldi is defeated by Papal troops backed by a French expeditionary corps (France protects the Papal States).

6daae50a-b99b-511d-afe3-0ac78441af43.name: Second Restoration
6daae50a-b99b-511d-afe3-0ac78441af43.description: Second Restoration: the reign of Louis XVIII and his brother Charles X. France experiences an economic boom (i.e. the development of the railways), but discontent grows over the king’s authoritarian policies.

6dd3eff4-4a18-552a-855d-86149b51f527.description: Building of the Great Umayyad Mosque in Damascus proclaims the imperial status of the new religion and places Islam on an equal footing with the strong Christian heritage of the region.

6dd7704e-28da-54cd-994e-31a3250028c9.description: Declaration of the Papal Bull of the Dissolution of the Jesuit Order. Prince Miklós Esterházy entertains Queen Maria Theresia (Theresa) in Eszterháza with splendid festivities, including Haydn’s music.

6e35aa8a-5ab0-5618-93fc-9b29f41ba4d2.description: The German polymath Johann Wolfgang von Goethe (1749–1832) is born. He became one of the leading figures of German literature during the period of classicism.

6e3698f2-02b9-5756-aa41-c8cf4f9b792e.description: Numerous forts established to hold Kabylie (Dellys, Azzefoun, Béjaia).

6e42aa58-4d87-55a9-b87b-1f075952e460.name: Afonso Costa is appointed Prime Minister
6e42aa58-4d87-55a9-b87b-1f075952e460.description: Afonso Costa is appointed Prime Minister. Republican achievements fall short of people’s expectations, fuelling the resistance of monarchists, capitalists and landlords. Inflation, public debt, trade deficit, strikes, the rise of anarcho-syndicalism, middle-class disillusion, and fear of communism will invite the establishment of the 1915 military dictatorship.

6e4f8911-7f21-5808-b370-e65892592750.description: The recapture of Buda by the allied armies of the Holy Alliance led by Karl von Lothringen (Charles of Lorraine). The last Pasha of Buda dies in the struggle.

6e671705-5538-5973-a1ce-3df4d6aef618.description: Berber insurrections shake the country. Arab pacification puts an end to the insecurity and prompts economic growth.

6e770689-ff4e-520a-a24f-e3cc1bfb4526.description: Josef II dies in February shortly after withdrawning all of his reforms concerning Hungary except for three. The Holy Crown of Hungary is again in Buda. Farkas (Wolfgang) Kempelen builds a speech-imitating machine.

6f214a42-95c6-55f4-8215-4011610d81f1.description: The Mamluks defeat the Crusaders in ‘Akka and the rest of the Palestine and Lebanon coastal cities, putting an end to the Crusader states in Palestine and Syria, which had lasted some two centuries.

6f340f5a-d8bf-599e-8d60-2909d33f5e45.description: The Abbasid family left al-Humayma in Jordan for Kufa in Iraq in order to lead the revolt against the Umayyads. Their plotting reaches a successful conclusion in this year.

6f763c9f-2140-5a30-b6a4-22f4ac5ddf6c.description: The Sa‘dids win the Battle of Oued al-Makhazin (Battle of the Three Kings – resulting in the death of ‘Abd al-Malik, Don Sebastian, King of Portugal and al-Mutawakkil) and the coronation of Ahmad al-Mansur al-Dhahabi (‘the golden’).

6f945400-003a-55f4-b732-d4af19ae593e.name: The Algeciras Conference
6f945400-003a-55f4-b732-d4af19ae593e.description: The Algeciras Conference of 1906 endorses the intervention of Western powers in Morocco, granting special rights to both Spain and France.

6ffc72de-e2ca-54a2-abbf-57ec8f88cc1e.description: Italy enters World War I (1914–18) on the side of France, England and Russia.

70009b19-9e8c-5af5-88a6-11f1459e79c3.description: Annexation of the Kingdom of Portugal.

701b3c4c-459b-54bc-af7e-fd494ad0988b.name: Romania participates in the Second Balkan war
701b3c4c-459b-54bc-af7e-fd494ad0988b.description: In 1913 Romania participates in the Second Balkan War and under the Treaty of Bucharest receives the south of Dobruja from Bulgaria.

7032ab2d-f09f-5f79-a61a-4b59e3c78966.name: The peace treaty of Adrianopole
7032ab2d-f09f-5f79-a61a-4b59e3c78966.description: The peace Treaty of Edirne institutes the Russian protectorate over Moldavia and Wallachia, which lasts until 1856. The Romanian countries remain under Russian occupation until 1834. Under the supervision of the Russian authorities in 1830–31 the Organic Regulations, considered to be the first Romanian constitutions, are drawn up and adopted.

7043adec-94a2-5cef-895e-898d5fc584f6.description: The Abbasid Caliph al-Rashid appoints his brother Ibrahim ibn al-Mahdi governor (wali) of Jordan. It was customary to appoint the brothers and family members of caliphs to administrative positions.

7071890f-2726-5807-ac9f-372a7b4a1491.name: Germany declares war to Portugal
7071890f-2726-5807-ac9f-372a7b4a1491.description: Germany declares war on Portugal. Portugal enters World War I, complying with international commitments in Europe and defending the Portuguese strategic possessions in Africa, mainly Angola and Mozambique. The Portuguese army fought on the western European Front and in the south of Angola (border with Namibia) and the north of Mozambique (Nevala).

70be0e76-4551-58e2-a3cc-a30ce4cf06fe.name: The British destroy Al Qawasim hegemony
70be0e76-4551-58e2-a3cc-a30ce4cf06fe.description: The British put a stop to Qawasim hegemony in the Lower Gulf region by destroying their ports, strongholds, and fleets on both shores of the Arab Gulf.

71974b2e-4adf-51d8-8597-e04be4444a5b.name: The English Admiral Edward Pellow
71974b2e-4adf-51d8-8597-e04be4444a5b.description: The English Admiral Edward Pellow, 1st Viscount Exmouth imposes on the regencies of Algiers, Tunis and Tripoli new recommendations to slow the race at sea. He inaugurates the so-called Gunboat diplomacy, which involves the threat of military force.

71de5983-ed40-5903-a03a-2487540de8d6.description: Emperor Justinian I dies on 13/14 November. He was famous for his successful military campaigns and also for his reform of the legal code. He was also known as ‘the last Roman Emperor’.

71e546a2-7016-560d-ab53-888d66bd85df.description: Great hardship due to a very high flood preventing the sowing of new crops in season; a great rise in prices and the cost of living.

72048ead-8c65-5cac-9ef1-b76901da64ae.name: The Restitution of Obrenovic Dynasty
72048ead-8c65-5cac-9ef1-b76901da64ae.description: The *Hatišerif* (Turkish edict) is issued in 1838, allowing the *Sovjet* (Council) to limit the powers of Prince Miloš Obrenović. Unwilling to accept this however, Miloš abdicates and leaves Serbia in 1839. Prince Mihailo Obrenović reigns for a short time before the Karađorđević Dynasty regains the Serbian throne in 1842. The 1858 *Svetoandrejska skupština* (Assembly convened on St Andrew’s Day) decides on a change of dynasty, overthrowing Prince Aleksandar Karađorđević and reinstating Miloš Obrenović. A 37-strong deputation from the Assembly, with a massive, heavily armed entourage, leaves Belgrade for Bucharest to bring the newly elected prince back to the country, marking the beginning of Miloš’ second, but short-lived reign, which ends when he dies in 1860.

728da759-de05-5c27-bc42-0c6b3447d427.description: Death of Louis IX at the gates of Carthage during the Eighth Crusade against the Kingdom of Tunis.

729ec165-6619-50b1-97b2-215c22bcac7b.description: The Regency of Algiers founded by Khaïr-Eddine. Algiers becomes the first vassal town of the Ottoman Empire in Central Maghreb.

72da6f8a-03d8-51b9-8f7a-1411e201ef2f.description: The Guelphs and Ghibellines, supporters of the Papacy and the Emperor respectively, clash in Florence.

72e976ab-7b9c-57b2-8a32-1cf00bc51a16.description: Ali ibn Abi Talib, the Prophet's cousin and companion, isappointed wali (ruler) of Egypt by ‘Uthman ibn ‘Affan, the third Righteous Caliph.

731d2825-34dc-5c1b-ad80-cce07481cbfe.name: Austria and France concluded the peace of Campo Formio
731d2825-34dc-5c1b-ad80-cce07481cbfe.description: Austria and France conclude the Treaty of Campo Formio on 17 October. Austria then cedes to Belgium and Lombardy. To compensate, it gains the eastern part of the Venetian Republic up to the Adige, including Venice, Istria and Dalmatia.

7328c223-bab3-5b55-b0d2-7c00694cf788.description: The Corpus Iuris Civilis is compiled under Justinian, collecting and organising Roman law. The work remains influential for centuries, becoming the cornerstone of legal studies.

73577528-b383-5d4e-9249-7b67217c0f69.name: Sultan Mehmed V
73577528-b383-5d4e-9249-7b67217c0f69.description: 27 April: Unseating of Sultan Abdülhamid II and accession of Sultan Mehmed V.

735fcfa4-79e8-5584-9768-c75fbe0f8cc5.description: The Turkomans under the command of Utsuz, in the name of the Seljuqs, invade Palestine, defeating and ejecting the Fatimid army. The Fatimids reconquer it 25 years later.

73894d38-608c-52d0-a6b7-048282a78bb2.name: Battle of Isly
73894d38-608c-52d0-a6b7-048282a78bb2.description: The Battle of Isly is fought on 14 August 1844 between the Moroccan army employing an archaic strategy against professional soldiers trained in the Napoleonic campaigns and armed with batteries of light guns. The battle ended with the defeat of the Moroccans. The consequences of this defeat were grave for Morocco. It was the first time the country had lost a battle in more than two centuries, and it showed Mulay ‘Abd al-Rahman just how weak his army was.

73ce346b-a7ba-59c9-9d97-77f864f326b8.description: Charles II lands in Scotland and is proclaimed King of Scotland, but two years later Scotland is occupied by Cromwellian forces, and incorporated into the Commonwealth.

7438e0cd-4c36-53ea-b973-6082a1b99195.description: Muslim counter-revolution is thwarted. The sultan is deposed and constitutional monarchy is declared.

7461a583-5319-5d96-bc8b-835aeefb8505.description: Emperor Wilhelm II (1888–1918) sacks Chancellor Otto von Bismark. The era is called ‘Wilhelminische Ära’ and eventually leads to the First World War.

74a13175-31ff-5506-bdad-c194b76dee86.name: Asia Minor Catastrophe
74a13175-31ff-5506-bdad-c194b76dee86.description: Following the “Asia Minor catastrophe”, almost 1.5 million Greek nationals arrive as refugees at Greece’s coastal regions, for example at Pontus, having been uprooted from their homes in Asia Minor (Anatolia).

750711da-d1fc-5020-88cd-cbf8b44b3bd7.description: The Ayyubid king al-Salih Najm al-Din orders the construction of a congregational mosque at Ajlun; it seems not to have had a minaret.

750f20d5-2095-577c-8bd3-c0bb2460a115.description: Revolt outside Cordova: Muladi protests against taxes put down with large numbers of deportations and executions.

752104ff-ab92-5d24-be3f-a98a9dd4db2d.description: Byzantine Emperor Maurice breaks the peace treaty with the Persians and invades Syria. War continues with both sides growing weak and weary, inadvertently easing the path for the upcoming Muslim conquerers.

75265dcf-e309-5623-bb92-119872b38890.description: Two peace treaties: Vienna ends Hungary’s fight against the Habsburgs led by István Bocskai, Transylvanian prince; Zsitvatorok (part of Dunaradvány, today: Žitava, Slovakia) ends the fight with the Turks. Bocskai dies.

7542ab53-207e-5790-ad12-9d6767a20507.description: Saint Francis of Assisi writes his Rule, inspired by the principles of poverty, errant preaching and Christian charity. Frederick II (1211–50), already King of Sicily, is crowned emperor.

7560c725-f1f9-5ae3-b2fa-1cd004f0e19e.name: Founding of first Serbian journal *Novine serbske*
7560c725-f1f9-5ae3-b2fa-1cd004f0e19e.description: In Vienna in 1813 Dimitrije Davidović, politician, diplomat, author of the Candlemas Constitution and one of the founders of journalism in Serbia, launches *Novine Serbske*, Serbia’s first daily newspaper. The newspapers are printed in Serbia for the first time in 1834.

75ab6cf4-67be-510f-9810-3d8d239173a7.description: Amir Ziri ibn Atiya of the Maghrawa takes Fez.

75ea8147-54e7-5866-ba9e-de354887a88e.name: War declared on Morocco
75ea8147-54e7-5866-ba9e-de354887a88e.description: War declared on Morocco. Battles of Castillejos (Fnidq) and Wad-Ras. A peace agreement is signed with the Moroccan Sultan leaving Tetouan under Spanish rule.

76106077-4fbe-5ac5-831b-fc32a3eed850.description: Napoleon Bonaparte fails to force ‘Akka, under the command of Ahmad Pasha al-Jazzar, to surrender, and retreats to Egypt and France.

7637c289-671a-55af-914e-9e5bde830847.name: Spain focuses on North Africa in the framework of the colonial interests of other European powers
7637c289-671a-55af-914e-9e5bde830847.description: After the loss of its last colonies, Cuba, Puerto Rico and the Philippines, Spain focuses on North Africa in the framework of the colonial interests of other European powers such as France, the UK and Germany. After different international talks and agreements – Spanish–French Agreement (1904), Algeciras Conference (1906), Cartagena Declarations (1907) – Spain and France sign in November 1912 the Treaty establishing the French and Spanish Protectorates in Morocco.

76612ecb-7de2-5f19-898c-9a0345125993.name: San Remo Conference
76612ecb-7de2-5f19-898c-9a0345125993.description: France takes control over Lebanese territory after the San Remo Conference.

767bf16a-6913-5b7b-8d3b-4f238e72b2eb.description: Marco Polo, son of a Venetian merchant, departs for China with his father Nicolò and uncle Matteo. He is one of the first Westerners to reach China.

7688cb66-98d6-589d-bdbd-6120c7e6b1b6.description: The first seigniories are formed, in Milan under Filippo della Torre, in Ferrara with Obizzo d’Este and in Mantova with the Gonzaga family.

76ca0397-5ce3-5704-8d79-9e92e944d2ee.description: Methuen Treaty between Portugal and the United Kingdom.

76cf902a-1193-599d-aede-2794482c58be.name: Edirne retaken
76cf902a-1193-599d-aede-2794482c58be.description: 23 July: Edirne retaken by the Ottoman Army under the command of Enver Paşa.

76e01fa6-f7d0-5253-8859-c7014c752224.name: Resistance to French occupation
76e01fa6-f7d0-5253-8859-c7014c752224.description: Tunisians put up stiff resistance to French occupation without any external support. The Sublime Porte, itself threatened by the Western powers, limits the show of protest against the French occupation.

776b31da-3663-540a-af66-449903290122.description: Al-Zahir Baybars defeats the Tartars in Asia Minor.

7775ae73-0164-5411-84ca-fb0a6ada7c1f.name: Introduction of universal male suffrage and of an electoral system of proportional representation
7775ae73-0164-5411-84ca-fb0a6ada7c1f.description: Introduction of universal male suffrage and of an electoral system of proportional representation. The Popular Party (antecedent to the Christian Democrats) is founded. Mussolini creates the first Fascio di combattimento (embryo of the Fascist Party).

77d1d8d4-47c4-5ddd-bc58-1a459d986cb7.description: Khaïreddine, the prime minister of the bey, instigates a programme of reforms. Foundation of the Collège Sadiki, the first modern secondary school in Tunisia. Foundation of the Sadiki hospital.

77e3d358-67fc-5942-839e-ff23d23e5cfa.description: On 9 July Nikola Tesla is born in Croatia.

784d1ad4-879a-5143-a5ef-97e2854c39cb.description: A Yellow Fever epidemic rages through Egypt.

7866aee2-15a3-5407-a06d-d0b5a4f48d9a.name: Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim Ruler of Qatar
7866aee2-15a3-5407-a06d-d0b5a4f48d9a.description: Treaty with the UK. This recognises Sheikh Abdullah bin Jassim as the ruler of Qatar, and places the sheikhdom under British maritime protection.

788dca06-e404-5193-be41-f794901f648b.description: The land of Thuringia is conquered by rulers of the Merovingian Dynasty with the help of the Saxons.

78b04146-1861-5327-afe3-d91348a8ad18.description: Visigoths defeated by the Franks at the Battle of Vouillé; collapse of the Visigoth Kingdom of Tolosa and withdrawal to the Iberian Peninsula (Kingdom of Toledo).

78dd4d35-d6b9-5942-ab3e-7fd0b98349b5.description: The Ottoman Empire's military strength and imperial patronage of religious and commercial buildings, especially in Damascus, by Lala Mustafa Pasha (1570), Darwish Pasha (1574) and Sinan Pasha (1589).

791d1021-9e23-57b9-a880-2a791e359eed.description: Founding of Olomouc bishopric. Vratislav II made first Czech King (1085). The first Czech chronicle known as the *Chronicle of Cosmas*. Premonstratensian and Cistercian monasteries founded (1140).

792cc7e2-44f5-5a27-9343-72d72bcd1f52.description: The *Law of Vinodol* is composed, one of the first juridical regulations in this part of Europe.

797a2cba-06d1-5dc9-8479-ff5914b1a90b.name: Pedro as Regent returns to Portugal to defend his daughter’s rights
797a2cba-06d1-5dc9-8479-ff5914b1a90b.description: Civil war. Pedro returns to Portugal as Regent to defend his daughter’s rights. He launches military operations from Azores and Porto against the absolutist faction of Prince Miguel favored by the Quadruple Alliance. After the Miguelists’ defeat, peace terms depend on the Évora-Monte Convention and Prince Miguel’s exile.

798257f6-1021-535f-9840-0aae074a5828.description: Assembly of non-Catholic Estates. ’Prague Defenestration’ incident sparked a rising of the Czech Estates against the Habsburgs and the outbreak of the Thirty Years’ War. Czech Estates joined by Moravian and Austrian aristocracy and Frederick, Elector Palatine (Czech king 1619–20).

7986496d-f340-503e-897c-9134459abad3.name: Most parts of Arabia become a part of the new state
7986496d-f340-503e-897c-9134459abad3.description: Most parts of Arabia become part of the new Saudi State. In 1803, The two holy cities of Mecca (Makkah) and Medina (Madinah), along with the rest of the Hijaz region, join the Saudi State.

79a18bd9-ece7-55a7-bf23-5fa46e37f311.description: Creation of the United Kingdom of Portugal and Brazil.

79af730b-ca67-5371-a316-30f78c8396eb.description: Catholicism becomes the official religion of the Visigoth Kingdom of Toledo.

79c792fd-77c1-59f8-a733-cb0125a9752e.description: Northern Morocco is shaken by the Kharijite revolt lead by Maysara al-Matghari.

7a52fcdf-c442-5230-a24b-c51e8d8f749c.description: On 23 August the Ottomans defeat the Mamluks in a decisive battle at Marj Dabiq, marking the end of the Mamluks’ rule in Egypt and Syria.

7a646070-4f51-53ee-a347-81ab80dd7b70.name: Dawud Pasha
7a646070-4f51-53ee-a347-81ab80dd7b70.description: Dawud Pasha (the *mutasarrif* \[governor\] of Lebanon, appointed by the Ottomans) restores to Lebanon a part of its lost territory, establishes for the Druze a school in Abayh that still bears his name and struggles against the feudal lords in the south and the clerical party in the north.

7a6c3010-26aa-5cf1-a20e-8c9f84d04c4d.description: The Croatian People’s Peasants’ Party – from 7 December Republican Peasants’ Party – led by Stjepan Radić refuses to acknowledge the monarchy and leads Croats to ethnic and political emancipation.

7a77081e-dc50-5afc-ae5d-ed507acd1850.name: the young King Alexander of Serbia murdered
7a77081e-dc50-5afc-ae5d-ed507acd1850.description: The young King Alexander of Serbia is brutally murdered in an officers’ conspiracy in June. The replacement of the pro-Austrian Obrenović Dynasty by the pro-Russian House of Karađorđević under Peter I, changes the balance of power in the Balkans.

7a79996f-5777-5cb7-ac04-407bc2249a9e.description: Austria-Hungary reincorporates the military border into Croatia, increasing the number of ethnic Serbs in Croatia to about 25 per cent.

7aeb2f08-5d28-5ee1-a897-67339824e4f1.description: The Porta Pia Breach: on 20 September, the Sardinian army liberates Rome, annexing the city and the Papal States to the Kingdom of Italy. The unification of Italy is complete

7afa4b50-1a4e-5434-8131-18e2304e897c.description: Beginning of a power crisis for the central emirate sparking local rebellions for independence.

7b4b9e1c-fa6a-58c2-89c0-26e0dcea8c29.name: British Ultimatum
7b4b9e1c-fa6a-58c2-89c0-26e0dcea8c29.description: The British Ultimatum (11 January 1890) pressures Portugal to withdraw from southern Africa resulting in popular outrage and unrest. The bankruptcy of 1892, anti-monarchic sentiment against King Carlos I, the cost of living and unfulfilled popular needs are major drivers of the Republican movement.

7b791ac7-d8d3-5d68-ac13-3a180cea05ea.description: Disputes between Rudolph II and his brother Matthias. Moravian Estates led by Karel of Žerotín join the associations of Austrian and Hungarian Estates. Imperial charter issued by Rudolph II confirms religious freedom (1609); however, discord continues.

7b81e809-5ef4-5166-84f8-16d85815854a.description: The Portuguese take the town of Sebta.

7bdc11bd-0506-5fb4-8591-e9c1587220c0.name: Sykes-Picot Treaty
7bdc11bd-0506-5fb4-8591-e9c1587220c0.description: Sykes–Picot Agreement signed by the British, French and Russian governments on 16 May 1916 concerning the division of Ottoman lands in Greater Syria between the two colonial powers, the UK and France. According to this secret treaty southern Syria (Palestine and Jordan) and Iraq are to fall under British mandate and Syria and Lebanon under the French.

7bf6d490-d456-59ff-90b6-cbd66afa2bf1.name: Treaty of the Protectorate
7bf6d490-d456-59ff-90b6-cbd66afa2bf1.description: At the metropolitan palace, Muhammad Sadiq Bey signs the treaty imposed by the French Protectorate known as the Treaty of Bardo (or Treaty of Kasser al-Sa‘id). This is followed by the Convention of Marsa in 1883. The Regency of Tunis passes from Ottoman suzerainty to French domination.

7c09389d-e946-5db3-8b7b-8cbcee844e5b.name: First Serbian railway and railway bridge
7c09389d-e946-5db3-8b7b-8cbcee844e5b.description: The first Serbian railway and railway bridge is built in Belgrade.

7c0b3274-7bcb-5ba7-b3fd-f7e5edd13bab.description: The Ikhshidid dynasty, based in Egypt, extends its rule to Damascus. The Abbasid empire begins to fragment.

7c1ad6bd-1974-576b-9bd8-7735354ba9b3.description: English barons force King John to agree to a statement of their rights and sign the Magna Carta, which limits his power and paves the way towards a constitutional monarchy in England.

7c2ee146-ba53-5964-b2d9-cb23eb7cfdd7.description: Foundation of Cairo (Egypt). The Fatimids leave for Cairo.

7ca9f489-64fb-5adf-a55f-fa9754ac5af6.name: Reign of Muhammad Ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman
7ca9f489-64fb-5adf-a55f-fa9754ac5af6.description: Reign of Muhammad Ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman: with a view to overhauling the machinery of administration, Muhammad IV creates an administrative school, the Madrasa Makhzenia, and proceeds to modernise financial and tax services. He also thought about modernising the army, both in terms of soldier training and equipment. This was eventually achieved by his son Mulay al-Hasan I.

7cbfe03b-c7db-5dae-9833-cb09f7a8e4dc.description: Expounding his economic and social programme (including regulation of the lower Danube) Count István Széchenyi publishes *Hitel* (Credit) the first Hungarian socio-economic reform programme.

7cead247-b0ae-5763-9ebf-59ae5749df87.description: The priest Anders Chydenius from Ostrobothnia (today part of Finland) is elected to parliament, where he actively works for freedom of trade and freedom of print.

7d0cc929-eae7-54e7-8ada-1acf67489c9a.description: Women are given the right to vote in Swedish elections.

7d87484c-d3be-5735-a7da-c7915d51a401.description: The arrival of the Aghlabids triggers the Arab conquest of Sicily.

7d949f6e-348a-5172-87f4-bec6a0a0dea5.description: Capture of Constantinople by the Fourth Crusaders; Nicea becomes the new capital of the Byzantine Empire.

7daf34bc-4ae8-548a-8de3-f30fea7cf443.description: At the Battle of Helge å the Danish King Canute, who has already conquered England, wins a victory and gains control also of Sweden. It does not last, but it is one of the first major battles in what will become seven centuries of war and peace between Denmark and Sweden.

7dc58a1d-8843-5df5-a976-5067e5b3251f.description: The Peace of Augsburg results in recognition of Lutherism and Roman Catholicism. Each ruler now has the right to decide on the religion to be practised in his state.

7dede71a-1484-59fc-923d-a8d3dfd5b786.description: Norman incursions on the coast of Ifriqiya. The Djerba and Kerkennah islands, along with the towns of Gabès, Sfax, Mahdia and Sousse, are occupied by the Normans.

7e0715c0-0290-5b4e-9499-96a9b018b319.description: ‘Abd al-Mu’min starts the construction of the Great Mosque of the Koutoubiya in Marrakesh.

7e173ce2-2de4-553a-a41d-5b61fcf1b23f.description: The establishment of Great Moravia (Moravia, western Slovakia, parts of Hungary, Austria, Bohemia and Poland).

7e4629f7-3d09-583b-a56a-de70f453b63a.description: In October a peace treaty is made between Prophet Muhammad and the Bishop of Ayla, John bin Ru’ba in exchange for the payment of 300 dinars a year as poll tax for protection.

7eb302aa-f081-538b-a781-b0bc915391de.name: Franco prussian war
7eb302aa-f081-538b-a781-b0bc915391de.description: The Franco-Prussian War: France's defeat to Prussia results in the abdication of Napoleon III. Proclamation of the Third Republic.

7eb8ac05-861b-5f54-869d-e7795df9ca02.description: The rule of the Azem family, lasting nearly a century, indicates the rise of local urban notables into the leadership of Syria as Ottoman strength in the Arab provinces begins to weaken.

7f0247de-f0bf-5359-855d-9d7d6cfdb6e5.description: Birth of the illustrious scholar Ibn Arfa.
