7f434184-ddcb-5c28-8d42-ab2dbdfab6d0.description: Issa ibn Yazid al-Assouad founds the town of Sijilmassa at Tafilalet, the great desert port on the gold route.

7fb75a2a-174f-5889-a93a-01a999249076.description: A ruinous earthquake destroys Jerusalem and most of the cities of Jordan at the end of Umayyad rule.

7fc0134c-7298-5017-9f07-a34afb66a915.description: At the Peace Treaty of Fredrikshamn Sweden loses its eastern half (today’s Finland) to Russia.

80f48147-44c1-557b-95d4-cf83058e2aea.description: Publication of the Fuero Juzgo, a summary of Visigothic law.

80f8fda0-8020-5c16-a9df-253be322a36f.description: The Tours Congress sees the rise of revolutionary ideas in France. Nonetheless, France and England seem stronger than ever, and ready to share out the remains of the Ottoman Empire. But they have been severely affected by the war, and nationalist movements are beginning to make themselves heard in Mashriq and Maghreb.

8128be6c-e252-53df-a192-523926903235.description: Establishment of the first public museums (Opava). The first long-distance railway in Europe (České Budějovice–Linz, 1825). J. E. Purkyně introduces cell theory. Disturbances among workers and peasants.

8135c904-16ed-5812-bc23-049b451af18c.name: Temporary peace accord
8135c904-16ed-5812-bc23-049b451af18c.description: A temporary Peace Accord is achieved between the British East India Company, represented by Captain David Seton the Resident at Muscat, and Sheikh Sultan bin Saqr. This comes following several incidents labelled by the British as “piracy”, which the Qawasim argue is crucial defence of their existentially important economic interests in the Gulf region.

816a8455-d337-5d96-9ffb-6bf4ab2ef50c.description: Construction of the Great Mosques of Constantine and Tlemcen.

81caa2dd-140e-52b3-adec-c7b1a4e46a34.description: End of the Christian conquest of the west of the peninsula.

81f0fc36-c1ce-58fa-bce0-101ffd4fe578.description: Bramante begins construction of the new Basilica of Saint Peter.

81f5a073-c56f-5a6e-b163-19b52ff3ef24.description: The Vandals take refuge in Mauritania Tingitana (Northern Morocco in Antiquity).

826c5209-aba9-591c-aefd-1bf8fca1b9e0.name: Estatuto Real
826c5209-aba9-591c-aefd-1bf8fca1b9e0.description: Estatuto Real signed by the Queen Regent, María Cristina de Borbón, as a royal charter similar to the one under the French King Louis XVIII. There is no constitution, but it has two chambers (similar to the British House of Lords and House of Commons) and a government, with a president and ministers.

826f6c8c-327a-5a4d-805b-58a8f47a35e6.description: The policy of Wilhelm II toward the Near East results in his travels to the Ottoman empire (Istanbul, Jerusalem and Damascus).

827243e0-8b70-5c0f-881d-47e68fe1a3ee.description: Atabeg ‘Imad Zangi rules Aleppo, uniting it with Mosul and strengthening the northern frontier against the Crusaders.

82811ab9-6500-5319-8797-83df1e87d7f9.description: The first reform-diet in Pozsony (Pressburg, today: Bratislava, Slovakia) where Count István Széchenyi donates one year’s income from his estates to establish the Hungarian Academy of Sciences.

828da978-e3f1-5465-b4cb-566e2f362687.name: British imposition of treaty to prohibit maritime warfare
828da978-e3f1-5465-b4cb-566e2f362687.description: The British impose a Treaty to prohibit maritime warfare among the Arab littoral sheikhdoms during the pearling season from May to November with Britain as enforcer of the peace. The British now term the lands of the signatory sheikhdoms as “The Trucial Coast” or “Trucial Oman”. The Treaty is renewed regularly until 1853, when a Perpetual Treaty is put into place.

82db517a-d0cf-575c-a7fc-b9d9df7924c6.description: Charlemagne dies in Aachen (Aix-la-Chapelle) on 28 January 814 and is buried in the palatine chapel of Aachen.

83240809-1a96-5e43-8888-b1f6994c8383.description: Start of the Muladi revolts against their Umayyad rulers in the west of the peninsular.

835c65e2-a28f-5ff2-8926-18707e76dd0d.description: Treaty of Tordesillas between the Catholic Kings and John II, dividing the world into two spheres of influence: the Portuguese part and the Spanish part.

843e7b93-9382-5fb6-aa15-d508ca13de58.description: Birth of Leonardo da Vinci, artist, scientist and inventor who will enrich Italian culture with works of great renown, such as the Mona Lisa and Lady with an Ermine.

844ea8e6-3c36-57a2-a6e7-503cea5c081d.description: Prussia, Austria and Russia gain a decisive battle against Napoleon I (1769–1821) near Leipzig. This is seen as the peak of the German freedom movement.

84a32f77-9f95-5c58-8100-9528d44554ec.description: The Ayyubid king al-Nasir Dawud establishes an emirate at Karak; he erects a hospital (bimaristan) to treat the sick and to teach medicine.

84d3dd3f-6827-5068-b1ee-08874ea54a76.name: Inspired by Cadiz Constitution members of Parliament authored the first liberal Constitution
84d3dd3f-6827-5068-b1ee-08874ea54a76.description: 1 October: Inspired by Cadiz Constitution members of Parliament authored the first liberal Constitution. King João VI (1767-1826) promulgated the document on 1 October 1822, in Lisbon. Royal prerogatives and  the nobles and clergy privileges were limited, though with a weak impact.

84f53825-ab39-583f-b00b-4fbdcb2972f8.description:
Charles I of Spain made Holy Roman Emperor (Charles V).  
Revolt in the Germanias.

8512addf-1289-5cb2-8d0f-a4cfab760007.description: Around this time a new and shorter Nordic runic alphabet with 16 runes instead of 24 is introduced. It turns out to be a great success which rapidly spreads literacy in Sweden.

851486b5-b95c-5b54-ad89-2f7a1ad4914c.description: A general strike is called after a period of recession, reduced wages and lockouts.

852b9ffa-33fc-5fd8-b385-8027966f7fda.description: *Pacta conventa* between Hungarian King Koloman and Croatia. Koloman Arpadović crowned as Croatian king in Biograd and the personal union established.

85909fbb-7bcf-5aa6-953e-747d6abe0b07.description: Basil II, also known as Bulgar-Slayer, ascends the throne of the Byzantine Empire.

85bb72ad-6896-53fc-a4fa-1ef72f9b232d.name: Promulgation of the first Ottoman constitution
85bb72ad-6896-53fc-a4fa-1ef72f9b232d.description: 23 December: Promulgation of the first Ottoman constitution.

85c74932-11fc-5818-a400-b53441f61a78.name: Beginning of reforms in the empire
85c74932-11fc-5818-a400-b53441f61a78.description: 3 November: Mustafa Reşid Paşa declares the Imperial Rescript of Gülhane (the beginning of the Tanzimat reforms), granting basic rights to Ottoman subjects and declaring a policy of state reform. These reforms included the "fair and public trial[s] of all accused regardless of religion”, the creation of a system of "separate competences, religious and civil”, and the validity of non-Muslim testimony.

85cf5d5d-54b1-5413-ba10-cbbc7349d7c6.name: the heir apparent Archduke Francis Ferdinand was shot in Sarajevo by a Bosnian youth of Serb origin
85cf5d5d-54b1-5413-ba10-cbbc7349d7c6.description: On 28 June the heir-apparent Archduke Francis Ferdinand is shot in Sarajevo by a Bosnian youth of Serb origin.

85d90573-8eac-5412-b1c7-11162616f0a0.description: Foundation of Budapest with the unification of Buda, Pest and Óbuda. Plans by architect Miklós Ybl for the opera house in Budapest. Celebration of the 50th annniversary of Liszt’s musical career.

85fab7c6-cee6-502d-9260-f863a373d82e.description: Second Arab expedition. Victory at Hadrumetum (Sousse).

86240532-f224-5c3b-b019-d55fbe08f618.description: Birth of Albrecht von Wallenstein (1583–1634), Duke of Friedland, who became the foremost general of emperor Ferdinand II (1619–37) of the Habsburg Dynasty in the Thirty Years’ War.

86e30989-9055-5bf2-8f35-bdbe3e9d818a.description: In Bardo, on 12 May, Sadok Bey is forced to sign the treaty establishing the French protectorate in Tunisia. French colonial occupation begins.

8730568c-7f23-51cb-9249-3768d718584b.name: The mutasarrifiyya
8730568c-7f23-51cb-9249-3768d718584b.description: In the aftermath of the Lebanese civil war in 1860, the Ottoman authorities impose a new system of government for the mountain districts of Lebanon. Formerly, the region had been divided into two districts, one with a Maronite Christian administrator and the other with a Druze. The Ottomans combine them into a single district, known as the *mutasarrifiyya*.

87651cd0-1b60-5e82-8132-362fb7bb320c.name: Austria cooperated in the settlement
87651cd0-1b60-5e82-8132-362fb7bb320c.description: Austria cooperates in a settlement to the Turkish–Egyptian crisis of 1840, sending intervention forces to conquer the Ottoman fortresses of Saida (Sidon) and St Jean d’Acre, and concluding with the Dardanelles Treaty signed at the London Straits Convention of 1841.

877dafd0-9f60-5864-acb2-b560bc71880d.name: Foundation of the NSDAP
877dafd0-9f60-5864-acb2-b560bc71880d.description: Foundation of the National Socialist German Workers Party (NSDAP); the party’s first selection for the German *Reichstag* is on 6 July.

87a43f83-013e-52ab-97a5-e7971a3d8fa8.description: The Peace Treaty of Drinápoly (Adrianapolis). Bálint Bakfark (Valentin Greff Bakfark) whose lute pieces were published in Lyon (1552) lives at the Transylvanian princely court (in 1572 moves to Padua).

87ad1534-a5ce-5b9b-95cd-2736a922d99f.name: Hammuda Pasha Bey
87ad1534-a5ce-5b9b-95cd-2736a922d99f.description: During the reign of Hammuda Pasha Bey, known as the “Founder” of modern Tunisia, the Regency of Tunis enjoys a thriving economy and an overall sense of security.

87c22453-97fc-510d-8609-c93ccb1d12bb.description: The first Normans arrive in Southern Italy.

87f39b39-b595-532d-8cd5-f7ca02ce520c.name: Defensive Treaty of Hunkar Iskelesi
87f39b39-b595-532d-8cd5-f7ca02ce520c.description: 8 July: Defensive Treaty of Hünkar İskelesi with Russia establishes Russian naval superiority in the Black Sea.

884b6c52-4854-57c3-9a84-362a8b9c7571.description: Salah al-Din Ayyub (Saladin) takes control of Egypt.

8891679f-0bca-5f7b-9db7-13f48ca6dba5.name: London Treaty
8891679f-0bca-5f7b-9db7-13f48ca6dba5.description: The London Treaty: England, Russia and France suggest to the Ottoman Sultan that he should recognise Greek independence. This is the first step towards foundation of the Greek State.

8912b1e8-696f-5773-90f9-c9937abd4248.description: The Hungarian King Ladislas establishes the Zagreb Diocese.

891e3bca-a1af-59b5-8bad-f06a6570abb5.description: Sultan Barquq seizes power, establishing the Circassian Mamluk dynasty.Ibn Khaldun arrives in Egypt, where he lectures at al-Azhar and is appointed head of the Hanafite court of justice.

896804f5-0b98-5218-8da0-0a8feeff05d8.description: In the peace treaty of Roskilde Denmark loses most of its territory to Sweden.

8975e916-f26f-5445-af2e-f433857c7b3a.description: Third Arab expedition led by ‘Uqba (Okba) ibn Nafi, who founds the town of Kairouan.

8989e4df-ee57-5979-ade0-7a8544768efb.description: Spanish occupation of the Kingdom of Tunis and fall of the Hafsid princes.

89921c7a-6c88-55fb-8491-e1a4a127f6c8.name: Signing of the Treaty of Versailles
89921c7a-6c88-55fb-8491-e1a4a127f6c8.description: On signature of the Treaty of Versailles, Germany must face up to its responsibility to make reparation payments, abandon territory and let go of its colonies. The League of Nations is founded.

89a5bc65-0567-5c38-865f-1a8185e9a31e.description: After writing the Summa de paenintentia Paulus Hungarus, a canon lawyer, returns from Bologna and organises the Dominican order in Hungary. French architect Villard de Honnecourt visits Hungary.

89b3b259-caa1-5021-80b7-ebc9ba9afb10.name: The Paris Treaty
89b3b259-caa1-5021-80b7-ebc9ba9afb10.description: 30 March: The Paris Treaty marks the end of the Crimean War (1853–56); the Ottoman Empire is admitted into the Concert of Europe.

89db1804-533f-5192-a876-220a9f594541.name: Mohammad bin Saud established the first Saudi state
89db1804-533f-5192-a876-220a9f594541.description: In 1765 Imam Muhammad bin Saud establishes the First Saudi State in Arabia, starting with the Najd region, and making its capital the city of Dir‘iyya.

89f7da91-c373-5f3d-be38-70971584f56f.name: Treaty of Sevres
89f7da91-c373-5f3d-be38-70971584f56f.description: 10 August: Treaty of Sévres, which divides Anatolia between the Allies, Greeks, Armenians and Kurds.

8a0da1ea-cb8c-588f-af93-21ad12e921dd.description: The city of Jerash is discovered by the German explorer Seetzen; Jerash is one of the best preserved Roman cities in the East and was also an Umayyad city minting its own coins.

8a0dbd3b-c7ab-5cb0-9f80-bfd50d6c4a40.description: Birth of the painter, wood carver and engraver Albrecht Dürer (1471–1528). During this period Renaissance art flourished in Germany and Dürer travelled to Italy twice.

8adc9778-a6d1-53d4-b4dc-bdfa8f45a902.name: Imperial Rescript of Reforms
8adc9778-a6d1-53d4-b4dc-bdfa8f45a902.description: 28 February: Under diplomatic pressure, the Sublime Porte is forced to declare the Imperial Rescript of Reforms (Islahat Fermanı), giving the empire admission to the Concert of Europe. The Rescript states the equality of Muslims and non-Muslims before law, the right of non-Muslims to be admitted to government and military service, and abolition of the poll tax and freedom in education for non-Muslims.

8ae3414f-1a18-5e0e-9e99-e6b89b13d3d9.description: The death of Sinan, the master architect of the Ottoman Empire.

8b047a14-4113-55b1-aa73-6fc91cfdba22.description: The first golden coin is minted by Mehmet II.

8b2181da-e6d7-56c0-8fd9-a5101b4879eb.description: Issue of the Charter of Felicianus mentioning the founder of the Diocese, King Ladislas, the first bishop of Zagreb, Bishop Duh, and other clergy.

8b2697d2-dfa5-56b4-bf1b-b92a400f86da.description: The beginning of a long period of cultural revival under Sultan Qaytbay.

8b321ee6-41d9-5afe-ac80-5a5d90a4c313.description: Sack of Rome: the imperial forces of Charles V (1520–56) made up of mercenaries (lanzichenecchi) sack Rome. This event is considered to mark the end of the Renaissance.

8b366f79-f1db-5df1-9d61-2f466087069d.name: Foundation of the secret organisation Filiki Etaireia
8b366f79-f1db-5df1-9d61-2f466087069d.description: Foundation of the secret organisation Filiki Etaireia (Friendly Society) prepares the ground for the Greek Revolution.

8b4c0768-7ef5-5e1c-bc82-4a770beaeecf.description: The Swedish King Olaf establishes a mint in his town Sigtuna, which he probably calls Sigtune Dei (God’s Sigtuna), and strikes his first coins.

8b58cb7e-f6dc-5dda-b4a1-5d3a58fe7482.description: J. Janský publishes his discovery of four blood groups. Introduction of the right to vote. Workers’ strikes. The first permanent cinema.

8ba2e24d-8a08-5ff1-9d43-aaccb9084a29.name: Hambacher Fest
8ba2e24d-8a08-5ff1-9d43-aaccb9084a29.description: From 27 to 30 May an apparently non-political country fair, the “Hambacher Fest”, was held by a German national democratic assembly, demanding freedom, national entity and popular sovereignty.

8bcd27f3-c0ad-5d38-8347-1971bca6fcd5.name: Bankruptcy of Greece
8bcd27f3-c0ad-5d38-8347-1971bca6fcd5.description: Prime Minister Charilaos Trikoupis declares that Greece is bankrupt.

8c073e9f-3803-583b-8313-d568691e42c0.name: Death of Emperor Francis Joseph
8c073e9f-3803-583b-8313-d568691e42c0.description: Death of Emperor Francis Joseph and accession of Emperor Charles I to the Austro-Hungarian throne.

8c0ca8b9-fbea-5d31-a1a5-403cace11fd7.description: Enlightenment leads to the creation, under the Grand Duke of Tuscany Pietro Leopoldo (1765–90), of a new penal code. The death penalty and torture are abolished for the first time in Europe.

8c321b63-6e09-5e87-90a9-24d28ee25683.description: The Aghlabids begin the conquest of Sicily.

8c33a51c-477e-542d-ba24-ba0c468b29fe.description: Peter Forsskål, in his dissertation De libertate civili (On Civil Freedom), advocates for complete freedom of print.

8c86ef04-ea21-5362-a81f-96e5cdc55dca.description: Birth of the ‘Abd al-Wadid Dynasty in Tlemcen and the long reign of Abu Yahya I ibn Zayyan, making Tlemcen an important commercial, cultural and spiritual centre in Central Maghreb.

8daf36ae-da19-51be-8431-78d4430c8364.name: Army mutiny led by Rafael del Riego
8daf36ae-da19-51be-8431-78d4430c8364.description: In 1820, the army mutiny led by Rafael del Riego leads to King Fernando VII accepting the Constitution, in spite of his former opposition to constitutional monarchy, bringing in the Trienio Liberal period of popular rule. The Congress of Verona in 1822 gives France a mandate to restore Fernando as absolute monarch. In 1823 the French army invades Spain to restore absolutism, ending the Trienio Liberal.

8dc1e066-b0ca-50ae-a67d-ad6cb9504c69.name: Prince Pedro, Duke of Braganza and royal heir
8dc1e066-b0ca-50ae-a67d-ad6cb9504c69.description: King João VI asks his heir Prince Pedro, Duke of Braganza (1798–1834) to remain in Brazil. Part of the court decides to stay there. Facing revolt against the anti-Brazilian policy of Portugal, Pedro proclaims the independence of Brazil on 7 September (Grito do Ipiranga). In October he is acclaimed as the first Brazilian Emperor, Pedro I.

8de2de38-0008-5470-854c-c8741ae77ba8.description: Johannes Bureus’ Rvna-ABC is published. It was a reading book with parallel texts in runic and contemporary Swedish writing.

8e713a24-daae-5f44-8cda-86a8f557f7a3.description: On the initiative of Charles VI the Karolina road from Karlovac to Bosilje, Vrbovsko, Mrkopalj, Bakar and Rijeka is built.

8f17df9c-3af3-55db-ba92-cc38b1e7b7c8.description: Mua’yyad Shaykh retakes Syria and rules until his death in 824 / 1421.

8f4bc9d4-1925-5635-bb1e-d9e967d6babb.name: Revolution in Austria
8f4bc9d4-1925-5635-bb1e-d9e967d6babb.description: Revolution in Austria-Hungary and northern Italy.

8f4f638d-7dc8-5b7a-ab9d-c40c130ab513.description: Charles V stops at Algiers, bringing the town great international prestige.

8f8ae31e-110e-547d-b690-cacfe10effcf.description: One of the greatest Sufis of Islam, Ibn al-Arabi (b. 1156), travels all around the Muslim lands and finally settles in Damascus where, under Ayyubid patronage, he composes many works.

8fcec683-d1c6-572d-b49b-de8829a1ce4a.description: The Synod of Whitby establishes the date of Easter in Britain and consequently the supremacy of Roman Christianity over Celtic Christianity.

900be75a-9ad3-5cbe-a28d-b01531cf470d.description: After the defeat of France at the hands of Prussia, the Commune proclaimed in Paris is crushed by the Thiers government sitting in Versailles. The repression is brutal, with thousands deported to join some of the victims of the Kabyle insurrection of the same year.

908a57c7-e383-5113-b9a9-1597ded072c1.description: The declaration of Firman of Islahat (Reform).

90bfa0dd-40ce-568a-9055-6506205b8c6f.description: Ifriqiya is invaded by Hilalian tribes from Egypt. Split into several different kingdoms, Ifriqiya falls to the invaders.

9174a4b4-0d7f-50c2-b352-98b3ff8d8dd5.description: Battle of Sarmada, between the Crusader Principality of Antioch and the Artuqid Atabeg ruler of Aleppo, witnessing the success of the local Muslim forces even without assistance from the Seljuq sultanate.

9196c837-d2b4-55fd-9eef-0cb25ebf46e9.description: Vitterhetsakademien (The Royal Academy of Letters, History and Antiquities) is founded by Lovisa Ulrika, inspired by the Académie Francaise.

91ccf893-db26-5e21-8dd8-2baffc8ff692.description: The War of Independence culminates in the creation of the modern Republic of Turkey in 1923.

9230f9be-daa6-5e9e-a9d7-86214e177c16.description: Mu’awiya Ibn Abi Sufyan, the governor of Greater Syria begins to build the seaport of ‘Akka and to establish the first Islamic shipyard, where the first Muslim fleet is built.

926714b9-3c86-5caf-94f9-53fc3832be91.description: Bede, a priest, monk and the first English historian, publishes the Ecclesiastical History of the English People.

92857bdd-10d7-55e6-b625-792029009380.description: Around 30,000 Croatian soldiers, mainly cavalry, participate in the Thirty Years’ War. Croatian troops fight against Miklós Bethlen (1642–1716) in Bohemia and Hungary.

92bb47f6-e25d-5b2c-8c90-6cce1133f7fd.description: The first Western musical instrument in the Ottoman Palace: .an organ sent by Elizabeth I of England to Mehmet III.

92f84a88-32ed-5c5a-b607-90c4a056aca6.description: Mustafa Kemal Ataturk is born in Salonika.

92f9c3ca-d9e4-5e70-8dcc-3e2214584a58.description: Start of the Catastro de Ensenada, an attempt to organise state taxation.

939fe8a0-ff23-51bf-afdb-adca5baef228.description: Khedive Ismail orders the construction of European-style districts of Cairo in anticipation of the opening of the Suez Canal and builds Abdin Palace to become the new seat of rule.

93d189cb-ae36-5e54-9295-ea87ce356a14.name: Construction of the Tour Eiffel
93d189cb-ae36-5e54-9295-ea87ce356a14.description: The World Fair in Paris showcases the development of the latest industrial processes, and the Eiffel Tower is constructed for it.

93eeb569-6e0c-523e-a5aa-5b5d8226c6c2.description: Beginning of Entente Cordiale between France and England, resulting in the division of the Mediterranean and recognition of England’s influence in Egypt and France’s influence in Morocco. The 1912 Franco-Moroccan Agreement establishes a French protectorate in Morocco.

940a5973-8f4e-5448-b47e-26a4a83bd6c9.description: Battle of Maysalun, on the outskirts of Damascus, between the Syrians and the French. Yusuf Al-Azmeh, leader of the Syrian army, is killed in battle and considered a nationalist hero. Beginning of the French Mandate.

945e7d97-47be-56f7-ad31-1b918b2899d1.name: Shaikh Sultan bin Saqr succeeds his father
945e7d97-47be-56f7-ad31-1b918b2899d1.description: Sheikh Sultan bin Saqr succeeds his father as leader of the Qawasim. He expands the Qawasim Empire to the east to encompass the areas now known as Khor Fakkan and Kalba. He delegates the administration of key strongholds to his brothers and later to his sons. His half-brother Salih bin Saqr rules Sharjah from 1803 to 1838, followed by his son Saqr bin Sultan (until 1846), and then his son Abdallah bin Sultan (until 1855).

94e43014-84ba-5a4e-b222-f019edb670f4.description: The beginning of the Baroque city of Vukovar, building of the city centre, Franciscan monastery, parish church and the Palace of the Counts Eltz.

94efe63f-8d9d-537b-b4d9-8311051449b2.description: Origination of the Moravian Margraviate as part of the Czech state, with main centres Znojmo, Brno and Olomouc.

95007fc3-33aa-5012-b4ec-50e62f916c01.description: Movement of nations – invasions of nomadic tribes, arrival of western Slavs from the Danube and Vistula basins. Agrarian-pastoral culture, cremation burials. The empire of Samo – the first tribal union of the Slavs.

951b13fd-8e49-5fd2-8d19-51539db2f274.description: The Edict of Nantes ends the Wars of Religion, affording protestants considerable rights in the Kingdom of France.

954e1c59-b97f-5337-a0d4-24b34d77b952.description: The Duke of Medina-Sidonia takes the town of Melilla.

95f0662b-6346-53a0-b075-a65fc7dbd1ef.description: A devastating outbreak of the plague compounds the misery of renewed famine and a disastrous war with England.

962f6a76-8ff2-573e-963e-d54a0fb7fe5f.description: Hugh Capet, son of Odo Count of Paris, takes the crown of France and starts a new dynasty.

963e3689-f49e-516d-953b-972e7f9e5da2.description: A professorial chair of Semitic languages is established at Uppsala University. It is the oldest chair of Semitic languages in Sweden.

963e88b5-a317-516e-8a30-94670f4673de.name: Conference of San Remo
963e88b5-a317-516e-8a30-94670f4673de.description: The Conference of San Remo was an international meeting convened to decide which parts of its territories the Ottoman Empire would lose, to become the mandated territory under the League of Nations. For example, France received mandated territory for Syria and Lebanon (and King Faysal of Iraq goes into exile after losing Greater Syria to the French).

963f1a66-1273-5c8e-bb5a-0e563c684af7.description: The Royal Academy at Åbo is founded by Queen Christina. The town Åbo (Turku) is today in Finland. The Academy was moved to the new capital Helsingfors (Helsinki) in the 19th century, and became the Imperial Alexander’s University.

969a9bfc-7bcf-53fd-b3a5-8951c39a7a47.description: Massacre of the Janissaries by Ottoman Sultan Mahmud II.

96e250c2-84c2-5e5b-b6e8-9bff94cc60cd.description: On 13 May Karamanoğlu Mehmed Bey declares that only the Turkish language is to be used for daily and official use.

96e5e4b5-aa64-5511-b1ec-329efd627e19.name: The Ottomans abandon Doha
96e5e4b5-aa64-5511-b1ec-329efd627e19.description: The Ottomans suddenly abandon Doha, leaving behind guns, shells and ammunition.

9710722e-3904-53dd-95fe-25256ccdb433.name: Liberal ideas emergence since 1817
9710722e-3904-53dd-95fe-25256ccdb433.description: The emergence of liberal ideas. In Porto a Provisional Ruling Council is created (1820) and pursues the rebellion against British rule that started in Lisbon. Liberal revolution breaks out in Porto (August 1820), spreads to Lisbon, beginning the radical cycle known as Vintismo. King João VI is forced to return to Portugal from Brazil in 1821.

9712f917-16c8-5108-980f-45c135da3741.description: Having conquered all of North Africa and established Arab rule, ‘Uqba (Okba) ibn Nafi is killed. His mausoleum and mosque are erected near Biskra at Sidi Okba.

973c6b8b-7a18-5ba3-8988-dd148f9de463.description: King James IV of Scotland is killed, along with much of the Scottish aristocracy and thousands of Highlanders and Lowlanders, by the English forces of Henry VIII at Flodden Field in Northumberland.

976ca7cb-265a-5998-8ae5-7250fc2ed750.name: Carlist party rises three times in three dynastic wars against the State
976ca7cb-265a-5998-8ae5-7250fc2ed750.description: As a consequence of political instability and of a woman taking over the rule of Spain, the deeply conservative and ultra-Catholic Carlist party rises three times in three dynastic wars against the State (1836–39, 1846–49 and 1872–76).

977b1c25-67c0-5e7f-88f4-033570cb4b2e.name: Carol de Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen ruler of the United Principalities
977b1c25-67c0-5e7f-88f4-033570cb4b2e.description: 14–20 April: plebiscite leading to German Prince Carol de Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen being elected ruler of the United Principalities and recognised by the Ottoman Empire in October. On 13 July a new constitution is adopted, based on the Belgian one from 1835.

979d710a-1ec4-5981-837d-41ab03d27893.name: Italy annexes Venice
979d710a-1ec4-5981-837d-41ab03d27893.description: Italy participates in the Austro-Prussian War on the side of Prussia and annexes Venice.

97c12ea3-4f56-58fe-b558-e863ea2f0570.name: Alliance of the three Emperors
97c12ea3-4f56-58fe-b558-e863ea2f0570.description: The alliance of the three Emperors of Germany, Russia and Austria recognise the Habsburg Empire’s predominance in the western Balkans. In June, Austria reaches an agreement with King Milan I of Serbia, whereby Austria promises to support an eventual Serbian expansion in the south, while Serbia agrees to exclude any agreement with other powers without Austria’s prior approval.

97ced9b9-f2a0-5c4d-aa0d-9fa4accd95ef.description: The Portuguese found the fortress of Santa Cruz de Aguer near to the village of Founti.

97f3fb7e-3209-5e2c-a5bb-df21a46512a1.description: At the synod (church assembly) at Uppsala this year it is decided to keep Sweden in the Lutheran faith, banning foreign religions in the country.

984730ec-78ba-562d-aaa2-0a7e7716b621.description: Manfred, son of Frederick II, becomes King of Sicily (1258–66).

9859ec0a-bd29-51ca-98b9-98dad01d443d.description: The Ninth Symphony of the composer Ludwig van Beethoven (1770–1827) is seen as the peak of Viennese classical music.

98c09fd6-7c7b-560e-aa74-dda1e43a65d6.description: The poet, historian and philosopher Friedrich Schiller (1759–1805) finishes his drama Die Räuber, a great success in the Sturm und Drang Period.

9906c450-0cbb-5e4d-bc59-287aac1ff9d7.description: Beginning of the reign of Francis I. Continuation of the Italian Wars, marked by victory at Marignano and defeat at Pavia (1526). The King of France effects a reconciliation with the Turks, creating a scandal in the Christian world.

990fa704-5564-53e4-9cd8-586641a9d33a.description: Death of John II and ascension of Manuel I.

9920fb8a-96c7-5363-9af9-de70d2143d3e.name: Formation of Serbian Duchy Vojvodina
9920fb8a-96c7-5363-9af9-de70d2143d3e.description: The Serbian uprising against the Austrian monarchy sees the formation of *Srpsko Vojvodstvo* (the Serbian Duchy). Stevan Knićanin-Vojvoda (military commander) commands Serbian volunteers during the Hungarian Revolution (1848–49).

9954217a-4406-5abd-b1f8-a0d807e80755.description: Ahmad Ibn Tulun (r. 868–84) conquers Palestine and annexes it to Egypt.

999699a8-1c62-57f7-adcb-0797447fb6b5.description: Crac des Chevaliers, a critical Crusader stronghold in the Syrian coastal mountains, falls to the Mamluk Sultan al-Zahir Baybars (r. 1260–77).

99a83377-13c3-5bb1-a766-d812bb727188.name: Karlsbader Beschlüsse
99a83377-13c3-5bb1-a766-d812bb727188.description: The Karlsbader Beschlüsse (Carlsbad Decrees) was intended to suppress liberal and national movements through censorship of the press and political persecution.

99becd50-e409-5a29-94d2-6492740e8dfc.description: An organised National Archive is established, with a Director of Antiquities.

9a3916ce-d256-5c92-a102-e3cc2179fc41.description: Carl von Linné’s Systema naturae, a pioneering work on plant classification, is published.

9a6eeb77-3ff6-50d4-8a8a-9ef27b11a1d9.name: Spain's first Constitution of 1812
9a6eeb77-3ff6-50d4-8a8a-9ef27b11a1d9.description: Spain's first Constitution of 1812, influenced by the French Revolution, is revolutionary because it declares the Spanish American colonies to be provinces and all their inhabitants citizens. The constitution reduces some of the powers and privileges of the monarchy, aristocracy and church and will influence future post-independence South American constitutions. Up to 1876 Spain will change its constitution four times (1837, 1845, 1869, 1876).

9aaaeb56-9081-5d5f-b3f9-350631115f35.description: Christopher Polhem is asked to construct a new kind of steam engine, which is later used successfully in the copper mines at Stora Kopparberg in Sweden.

9b04f760-70ba-559c-9c4c-f93f7ee2e7af.name: Congress of Berlin
9b04f760-70ba-559c-9c4c-f93f7ee2e7af.description: Uprisings in the Balkan Ottoman territories lead to disproportionate reprisals. Popular protests in Britain oppose support for the Ottoman Empire. In contrast to the Crimean War, Britain provides no military aid to the Ottomans in their war with Russia. Diplomatic support is rewarded however, with Britain’s occupation of Cyprus confirmed at the Congress of Berlin.

9b0e0347-84a3-5ad6-90de-36ebb5db81fe.description: The battle of Marj Dabiq, north of Aleppo, between the Ottoman and Mamluk armies, leads to the collapse of the Mamluk empire and the beginning of the Ottomans’ rule in Greater Syria including Palestine.

9b2b1358-8caf-5edd-9920-05860f764130.name: Alexandru Ioan Cuza
9b2b1358-8caf-5edd-9920-05860f764130.description: 14 May: coup d’état of Alexandru Ioan Cuza, who dissolves parliament and proposes a new constitutional project, which is voted the same month and ratified by the Ottoman Empire and the guaranteeing Powers in June 1864. The *Statute Expanding the Paris Convention* assigned greater power to the prince and the government.

9bb23d04-4eb9-5a0b-99fb-b6e49c6ba414.description: Almohad victory over the Christians at the Battle of Alarcos (Ciudad Real).

9c525427-19e0-5584-b3b5-a004e74c6cf3.description: Fatima al-Fihriya, daughter of a Kairouanese man living in Morocco, founds the Qarawiyin Mosque in Fez.

9c72d77d-ee4c-53b9-8f71-7f9d509dbc4f.description: Spread of Christianity, arrival of missionaries Constantine (Cyril) and Methodius; establishment of Old Slavonic language, Glagolitic script. Archbishopric established. Conflicts with Frankish empire, invasions of Hungarian tribes. The foundation of Prague Castle.

9c76674a-4fbb-556b-b357-81a0dc29adaf.description: Albigensian Crusade against Cathars established in southern France triggers the conquest of the Languedoc by barons from the north of France. The Kingdom of France experiences an unprecedented period of economic and cultural expansion.

9c8f81a8-ece3-5b44-97ed-f41a573fec3c.name: Isabel II comes of age in 1843
9c8f81a8-ece3-5b44-97ed-f41a573fec3c.description: Isabel II comes of age in 1843. During her reign the political parties are divided into liberals and conservatives. The Church regains its privileges under the 2nd Concordat signed in 1851. The Queen's rule ends in 1868 with the revolution known as La Gloriosa (the Glorious Revolution).

9ce42dd2-e07d-5c4d-b205-ea3001c4d47d.description: Al-Zahir Baybars defeats the Mongols at Ain Jalut and reinstates the Abbasid caliph in Cairo.

9d0ebea9-7fda-5072-bc7f-ab89cdcadf2c.description: The Battle of Nándorfehérvár (Belgrade): János Hunyadi defeats the attacking Turks led by Sultan Mehmed II. After his victory Hunyadi dies from plague in the military camp.

9d14244d-f574-5f1a-b777-9363a577d9c6.description: The Hammadids and the Zirids reach an agreement to share Central Maghreb.

9d2cc5fc-65e4-5c8d-af9d-46ffb111b571.description: Prussian–Austrian War. Establishment of workers’ associations. J. G. Mendel pioneers genetics. The foundation stone of the National Theatre, Prague laid (1868).

9d566a6f-e45e-5d52-9f49-fc632c7d95bc.description: Italy joins the Triple Alliance with Germany and Austria: Italian colonial policy begins.

9d57cf87-4c8a-51e0-897c-26c2ca365e63.description: Inauguration of the Suez Canal for international shipping in a great celebration hosted by Khedive Ismail.Founding of Dar al-Kuttub, the first public library in Egypt.Opening of the first opera house in the Middle East.

9d779759-50b4-5c34-ab66-dc66330efe01.description: Croatia forms a state union with Austria. By a decision of the Croatian Assembly, the dynasty of Habsburg comes to the Croatian throne.

9d8a7c8f-ad81-5516-b2bb-658af1cfc977.name: September revolution known as La Gloriosa
9d8a7c8f-ad81-5516-b2bb-658af1cfc977.description: Carlist wars, economic crisis (1866–68) and disgruntlement with Queen Isabel II and the government explode in the September revolution known as La Gloriosa. The revolution is followed by six years of democratic government under Amadeo I, from the Italian Saboya family, (1870–73) and then under the first Spanish Republic (1873–74), causing the 3rd Carlist war.

9dbe88be-fa1c-5e79-b79f-e51460222b58.description: The Tulunid dynasty collapses and Egypt reverts to direct Abbasid control.

9df246be-7e24-59fd-98ca-5d56643eb083.description: ‘Abd al-Mu’min conquers Ifriqiya and unifies the three countries of the Maghreb (Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia).

9eae650a-ec2f-593b-8811-0ba66ad6f62a.description: Edward I defeats William Wallace at the Battle of Falkirk and reconquers Scotland. Wallace goes into hiding but is captured in 1305 and executed in London for treason.

9ed781be-d34c-590a-9e80-16be57da95ea.description: Croatian king Stjepan I (1030–58) focused on rebuilding Croatia’s military strength and in 1032 he sent his naval fleet to assist Byzantium in its war against the Arabs.

9f214dfe-dd30-5976-9274-7ea677e01a05.description: Muhammad ibn Tughj, governor of Amman under the Tulunids, defeats the Bedouins and bandits who attack pilgrim caravans; this gives him celebrity in Baghdad.

9f26fc26-dd73-5f23-a28d-5e2b9b09238f.description: Renovation of al Azhar riwaq (portico) screens, restoration of the mosque's ceilings and rationing of a daily meal of lentils for the poor by the wali al-Sharif Muhammad Pasha.

9f2a2dc7-8cb0-5ca4-bfd1-8386e901add6.description: Sultan Abu Inan founds the library of the Qarawiyin Mosque in Fez.

9f56d2ae-5739-575f-afdc-e4ba165c8fc6.description: King Gustav Vasa made Sweden a Protestant country. To complete the change from a Catholic to a Protestant country he had the Bible translated into Swedish, and the first Swedish bible is printed in this year. It is based on Martin Luther’s translation and is the foundation for all Swedish Bible translations up until 1917.

9f93ae4f-7f45-508b-a9d1-aefe15619aba.description: The famous Swedish author August Strindberg is born.

9f967f98-89d9-565b-b3e8-35244a172e12.name: The First World War
9f967f98-89d9-565b-b3e8-35244a172e12.description: The First World War, which left millions dead in France, leaves a lasting impact on society.

9faf7da9-9539-561b-97cd-a5207bb6724f.description: The Council of the Lateran reorganises the Church. The Pope makes Robert Guiscard (1059–85) Duke of Puglia and Calabria. It is the first acknowledgement of Norman domination of Southern Italy.

9fcefd8c-cca1-5f03-adc7-dd277fbc1360.description: In Dubrovnik the Jesuit church of St Ignatius is built according to the plans of Andrea Pozzo.

9fe03546-402e-5ee1-88c0-63096d5187dc.description: Conquest and settlement: the Hungarian tribes spread through the Carpathian basin led by Árpád, the father of the first Hungarian royal dynasty, the Árpáds, whose first king was (St) István (1000–38).

a00416f9-bacd-5434-af4e-2300882d3f35.name: The Constitution of 1876 is restored
a00416f9-bacd-5434-af4e-2300882d3f35.description: 23 July: The Constitution of 1876 is restored and the Committee of the Union and Congress (CUP) takes control over the administration.

a07a35d3-517a-5733-a44e-ab15ff16e00b.name: Romanian independence and Russian-Ottoman war
a07a35d3-517a-5733-a44e-ab15ff16e00b.description: After Parliament declares Romania’s independence (May 1877), Romania participates alongside Russia in the Russian-Ottoman war. The Congress of Berlin (1878) recognises the independence of Romania, which receives the greater part of Dobruja, but cedes the south of Bessarabia to Russia. In March 1881 Romania is proclaimed a kingdom. Prince Carol and his wife Elizabeth are crowned as King and Queen of Romania in May in Bucharest.

a0c5565d-bcb7-5aa2-b36c-ce7301eb22c3.description: Sanctification of Bishop Theodorus as a bishop of Jordan and Palestine by the Empress Theodora according to the request of al-Haritha al-Ghassani.

a142599a-d9ce-5b76-a491-1a81036d9d90.description: Caliph al-Mansur builds a garrison city on the Euphrates next to al-Raqqa, called al-Rafiqa, comissioning his son, al-Mahdi, with its construction. The shape of the city is inspired by the circular plan of Baghdad.

a165c9bb-32b7-5499-9d94-b7888b6bd79d.description: Dagobert I, King of Austrasia, creates a united Frankish kingdom with its capital in Paris. With the help of the future Saint Eligius, his precarious reign lasts for about ten years.

a18cd4ad-e024-5bb4-95c7-1e07a956d5f2.description: Henry IV is forced to abdicate and is followed by King Henry V (1106–25) of the Salian Dynasty.

a1a9d06b-86f3-5944-bedc-2ce44282d5f5.description: The Danelaw – the Viking area in the east and north-east of England with its own legal system – is established after the English king Alfred affirms his authority over the Viking leaders.

a1dd6d65-c01b-57b0-9fbe-2c9333ea9bc0.description: France takes part in a military expedition in support of the Greek insurrection against their Ottoman rulers. The 1829 Treaty of Andrianople recognises Greece’s independence.

a2226042-3ebf-5828-b710-7252e6703035.description: The forestry department is introduced in Ajlun (Orman) to protect the woods from being collected by the inhabitants.

a243ad19-d20c-5f94-b415-81b04e7a6c36.name: Jordan was a part of the Ottoman Syria
a243ad19-d20c-5f94-b415-81b04e7a6c36.description: Jordan is a part of Ottoman Syria. Its importance lies in being a land bridge connecting Anatolia and Syria with north Arabia, Egypt and North Africa and hence the necessity of establishing Ottoman fortresses to guard the Syrian and Egyptian pilgrimage routes.

a24b8786-9796-564e-97e8-9482d8ade191.description: The Sassanian Persian ruler Chosroe I raids Syria as far as Apamea and Antioch.

a2519dc1-25b3-5848-94dc-d4e58e5183cd.description: Death of the scholar Ibn Arfa.

a2617605-242d-588c-96e8-184665651e7f.name: Having ascended to the throne too young, Mulay ‘Abd al ‘Aziz
a2617605-242d-588c-96e8-184665651e7f.description: Having ascended to the throne too young, Mulay ‘Abd al ‘Aziz must act under the regency of his father mulay al-Hasan I’s chamberlain for almost six years. Upon his father death in 1900, Mulay ‘Abd al ‘Aziz took up the reins of power and made clear his desire to restructure the governing institution of Morocco, the *Makhzen*. He worked on the modernisation of the army and stabilisation of the currency. He relaunched the project to ensure universal application of the *tartib* tax, which he wanted to apply to all foreigners and protégés. This project naturally displeased the consular corps.

a2ab2f86-d4d6-5d09-9e9f-dc2197107ed1.description: Muhammad ibn Tughj rules Egypt autonomously under the title of al-Ikhshid given to him by the Abbasid Caliph.

a2c295c4-2f6c-5867-b9b1-9c30ec63bac8.description: Creation of a modern military school and establishment of a programme to translate European manuals into Arabic. Institution of a regular army kitted out like its European counterparts.

a2d5c3bb-ba69-5544-a238-47e55a8cf383.description: Sulayman the Magnificent takes the throne.

a2d7fd9a-de9f-53a2-8ead-7daca1751e64.description: The Almoravid Sanhaja set out the conquer the Maghreb under the leadership of ‘Abdallah ibn Yassine.

a2e6c462-06ac-5f27-823f-2545854c8bd3.description: Germany is proclaimed a Republic and on 11 August the Weimar Constitution comes into effect with Friedrich Ebert as its first president.

a2e963ba-eae3-5033-a6c3-46c4d3cd62d9.description: Foundation of princely town of Sabra-al Mansuriya.

a30b5d58-c0a4-577e-b94e-de7261f9f627.description: Byzantine reconquest of Africa led by the Byzantine general Belisarius. End of the Vandal kingdom.

a31468e6-3353-559a-b94d-cb213463cd1b.description: Approximate date of Cantar de Mio Cid, the principal work of the epic Castilian poem.

a3403bdb-9366-5d70-9205-71af2de3b129.name: Military actions in northern Morocco to prevent attacks by local tribesmen around Melilla
a3403bdb-9366-5d70-9205-71af2de3b129.description: Military actions in northern Morocco to prevent attacks by local tribesmen around Melilla are very unpopular in Spain because of forced levies. The levy decree of 1909 causes uprisings in Barcelona and other Catalonian cities known as Semana Trágica/Setmana Tràgica (Tragic Week). Spain is ultimately successful in the lengthy Rif War (1921–26) in preserving its rule over northern Morocco although in 1921 its army retreats with huge losses.

a34bd331-c80a-5b2d-aa88-167430ae6461.description: Millenium celebrations. Opening of the continent’s first underground railway in Budapest. Alfréd Hajós is the first Olympic swimming champion. István Bugarszky invents the endothermic galvanic cell.

a3abaf9f-7e5f-5f29-be43-6b3655322505.name: Diplomatic missions
a3abaf9f-7e5f-5f29-be43-6b3655322505.description: After his term as governor in Samos, Kostaki Musurus Paşa, a Phanariot Greek becomes the first Ottoman envoy to independent Athens (1840–47) followed by Vienna (1848) and London (1851–55).

a3b52d76-925e-5ce9-a515-99bc63ff43d2.description: The University at Dorpat is founded by Gustavus Adolphus. The town of Dorpat (Tartu) is today in Estonia.

a3b952aa-7896-589e-a630-83dca4c10ec5.name: he Austrian Emperor Franz Josef concluded a secret alliance
a3b952aa-7896-589e-a630-83dca4c10ec5.description: In October, the Austrian Emperor Franz Josef concludes a secret alliance with the Hohenzollern King of Romania, Carol I, against Russia.

a3ee0d33-6ca0-5b47-a931-404128f779be.description: Following the death of Elizabeth I of England, James VI of Scotland becomes James I of England and Ireland, bringing about the ‘Union of the Crowns’.

a40a2962-a846-54e9-a366-75e11eaece36.description: Almohad defeat at Navas de Tolosa, marking the beginning of their decline.

a4481df0-1f77-5e59-9bfe-89ceac191a0c.name: Treaty of Adrianople
a4481df0-1f77-5e59-9bfe-89ceac191a0c.description: 14 September: Treaty of Adrianople (present-day Edirne). This treaty secures Greek independence and strengthens the autonomy of Wallachia, Moldavia (Romania), and Serbia.

a4d54dd8-b667-5fa3-aca7-bc57f43322ab.description: After several attempts to conquer Constantinople, the Umayyads and Byzantines agree to a truce. Frontier warfare continues under the Abbasids but Constaninople is left unconquered until the Ottomans.

a4e05eba-2359-59d5-9a95-f94cff178e1e.description: Jesuits build their church in Rijeka. Dedicated to St Vitus it is the first and the biggest circular Baroque building in Croatia.

a4f0fe71-bf7d-501b-9ad9-2626e2665b64.description: Arrival of the Jesuit order; suppression of non-Catholics. The first independent map of Moravia (1569); the establishment of a university in Olomouc (1573). Fraternal Union published the Kralice Bible (1579); its language became the official norm.

a50dfb42-5caf-54f0-8ae9-204eef7e7ed5.name: Allenby and Faysal I
a50dfb42-5caf-54f0-8ae9-204eef7e7ed5.description: British General Edmund Allenby and Faysal I, son of Sharif Husayn of Mecca, move into Palestine with British and Arab forces, thus opening the way for the occupation of Lebanon.

a5261b45-60e8-5316-9b66-51637ead4c1e.description: ‘Abd al-Rahman III establishes the Caliphate of Córdoba.

a52dcdb9-fca4-5934-aa06-beb9ba79bc0a.description: An earthquake destroys half of Ramla, most of Jericho and Nablus, and causes some damage in Jerusalem. A year later, the Fatimid Caliph al-Zahir (r. 1021–36) orders reconstruction of the Aqsa Mosque and repair of the Dome of the Rock.

a54850a0-2512-5381-82c2-2021586cfa21.description: The first Swedish Court of appeal (Svea Hovrätt) is founded by King Gustavus Adolphus (Gustav II Adolf).

a57c5044-ff50-5ae3-a544-ddf51a5d82c3.description: The first industrial exhibition in Klementinum, Prague. Beginnings of the Czech linguistics. Origins of the nationalist movement. Establishment of the Academy of Fine Arts in Prague (1799).

a5b40142-4553-5368-8f86-cf0fed358889.description: Peace of Westphalia: Holland achieves independence and replaces Spanish hegemony with French.

a5b46708-9432-5415-8f45-474e2c94e280.description: Battle of Lipany, defeat of the Hussites. Sigismund of Luxemburg crowned Czech king (1436). The Basle “Compacts” acknowledging the communion of bread and wine.

a5c04e3e-fa4c-5cad-98a0-dc22ae80fe84.description: Charles IV’s major projects: revival of Slavonic liturgy (1347); foundation of New Town (1348), making Prague the largest European city; establishment of Prague University, the first in Central Europe; provincial statutes in Brno and Olomouc.

a5d988c8-1826-5709-ad6c-746fc2245dc4.name: Mulay ‘Abd al ‘Aziz is deposed and replaced by his brother Mulay ‘Abd al-Hafiz
a5d988c8-1826-5709-ad6c-746fc2245dc4.description: Mulay ‘Abd al ‘Aziz is deposed and replaced by his brother Mulay ‘Abd al-Hafiz (1908–12), who is proclaimed ruler in Marrakesh on 6 August 1907. He was then obliged to sign the treaty establishing the protectorate in Fez on 20 March 1912.

a5f9a990-c7d1-5889-a8ba-99b39c362f02.description: Garibaldi leads the Expedition of the Thousand, and the second war of independence spreads to the South. Thanks to Garibaldi, the Kingdom of Sardinia annexes the Kingdom of the Two Sicilies.

a62f49ef-6034-5dd7-a622-7a71e84aa249.description: In the Treaty of Mersen the Frankish Empire is divided into three separate parts. The empire of King Ludwig II (843–76) of the Carolingian Dynasty is enlargened.

a6530bb8-72a3-535e-b0e0-fddcbbca90ca.description: King Charles XII is defeated at the Battle of Poltava in Ukraine. It is the beginning of the end of Sweden as a Baltic super power.

a6720a51-7bb3-57c6-b899-738da985096f.description: King Otto III (983–1002) is crowned emperor in Rome by Pope Gregory V (996–9).

a6d6c4c5-ee24-52c6-be22-686d1d5b7a88.description: Macbeth, king of Moray, kills Duncan I near Elgin and becomes king of the Scots; his rule ends when he is killed by Duncan’s son Malcolm Canmore in 1057.

a7c94de7-b5cb-5cd4-af7b-9f2d9b779252.description: Baldwin I, the Crusader king of Jerusalem, erects a huge castle at Shawbak on a high mountain in Jordan in order to dominate the area, naming it Le Crac de Montreal.

a7cdba2f-d59d-5f84-a190-fd4ee334011f.description: Sheikh Zahir al-Omar al-Zaidani, ruler of north Jordan abstains from paying taxes to the Ottoman state; he forms an army of mercenaries to protect his land and collect taxes from the inhabitants.

a7d7da5f-d9ca-552b-8ee8-2a0514822156.description: Victory of the Great Seljuqs over the Byzantine army at Manzikert.

a82d8656-48f9-5319-a09b-fd380caeabf2.name: Sympathizers of Tawhidi movement
a82d8656-48f9-5319-a09b-fd380caeabf2.description: The British dismiss a former teacher of al-Taimiyyah School and a *Qadi* in Sharjah for sympathising publicly with the Tawhidi (Wahhabi) movement in Najd.

a85a1a69-0a7d-59be-bfd4-2023ac297f39.description: The Jews thrown out of Spain are under the Ottoman protection.

a88260ac-0d11-50b8-9b3a-2d7220cc6a02.description: On 4 September Prophet Muhammad emigrates with the Muslims to the town of Medina. This event known as Hijra and marks the beginning of the Hijri calendar.

a8b2889d-7ab4-5e6c-a382-56b3681070d0.name: The beginning of the independence process in the Spanish territories in South America and Mexico
a8b2889d-7ab4-5e6c-a382-56b3681070d0.description: The beginning of the independence process in the Spanish territories in South America and Mexico, influenced by the American and French revolutions. The first Declaration of Independence is in Ecuador in 1809 and the American process ends in 1898 with Cuba, followed by the independence of the Philippines and the selling of the Carolinas and the Mariana islands to Germany in 1899.

a91baf1b-b592-53e3-9cd6-8a1ef4b64d6c.description: During the 1870s a series of crop failures lead to starvation and the beginning of large-scale emigration from Sweden to America.

a93e0f2b-c9d0-5eb2-bc7e-9759a4c90308.name: War between Druse and Maronite
a93e0f2b-c9d0-5eb2-bc7e-9759a4c90308.description: A full-scale war erupts between Maronites and Druze. Napoleon III of France sends 7,000 troops to Beirut and helps impose a partition: Druze control of the territory is recognised as the fact on the ground, and the Maronites are forced into an enclave. This is ratified by the Concert of Europe in 1861.

a9417efe-ca91-5283-b61e-32fa5bc518c4.name: Notable increase in the activity of foreign powers
a9417efe-ca91-5283-b61e-32fa5bc518c4.description: There is a notable increase in the activity of foreign powers – especially Ottoman Turkey, France and Russia – in the Gulf region. Germany also makes its first appearance. The main interests for all of them are economic and geostrategic.

a9f8cc0a-2c36-5734-b15f-a19d6ddf08b1.description: On 11 October the governor of Sham, Junbalat, goes to southern Jordan to stop Bani Sakher tribes attacking pilgrim caravans and kills 20 of them.

aa02a42e-9565-58f3-ab44-c827737298ab.description: Gregory the Great (590–604) becomes pope. During his pontificate, the Church becomes more independent from the Byzantine Empire and great efforts are made to evangelise the Anglo-Saxons and Lombards.

aa33b06c-4e59-5f3d-ac59-c14a054e3995.description: In November the Fatimids of Egypt take control of Jordan during the region of al-Mu’izz Li-Deenillah.

aa3c2868-4847-59d7-87f3-bd8e285faa75.description: The Council of Trent begins, to end in 1563. The Council marks the beginning of the Counter-Reformation.

aa61a318-80ba-5c6e-bd8a-438a2bc6039e.description: Christian victory over the Turkish navy at Lepanto.

aa7e4844-6a13-5adb-b193-250d1dd40105.name: Rustam Pasha
aa7e4844-6a13-5adb-b193-250d1dd40105.description: Ottomans appoint Rustam Pasha as *mutasarrif* (governor). He is an equally firm and economical administrator.

aa8ab80f-57d0-524a-9616-51d06dc89d4f.description: First French invasion. The Portuguese court takes refuge in Brazil.

aaf64bc4-1ee7-5fb0-a695-a01a3b346ed6.description: Friedrich III, Elector of Brandenburg, is crowned as Friedrich I, King of Prussia. Prussia is on its way to becoming a European power.

ab2086dd-5008-5695-870e-cee4f7734ffb.description: The Hafsid ruler of Tunis takes refuge in Egypt. The Sultan helped him to take back his throne and he became the deputy of the Egyptian Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad bin Qalawun. The death of Ibn Mandhur, the author of Lisan al-Arab (‘The Arab Tongue’).

ab871503-57a1-540b-b6b2-c7a124254271.description: The town of Blida founded by emigrants from Andalusia.

ab9f145d-ab63-598c-827f-553071bb33c2.description: War between France and the European monarchies. Proclamation of the French Republic.

ac405094-1617-53c9-b850-3eecd1e25865.description: St Columba and a small group of monks sail from Ireland to the west coast of Scotland. They establish a monastery that becomes the head of the Celtic church in Britain and a major political centre.

ac6b6933-5006-5764-b55a-7c04c8eb0008.name: Carinthia remains within Austria
ac6b6933-5006-5764-b55a-7c04c8eb0008.description: The population of Carinthia in southernmost Austria votes in favour of remaining within Austria.

ac7675fd-3117-5c7d-99de-6c9f534988ea.name: Foundation of ministries
ac7675fd-3117-5c7d-99de-6c9f534988ea.description: Founding of the Ministry of Finance and formation of Sublime Council for Judicial Ordinances. The title “grand vizier” becomes “prime minister".

acb5324e-6ee9-50df-953c-ef7ed145490a.description: The reign of the Lombards comes to an end. Charles King of the Franks takes Pavia and establishes Frankish rule in Northern Italy. The Duchy of Benevento and Venice remain independent.

accc96bc-6ab2-539a-b0df-e6cc0b3ec739.description: Erik Bloodaxe, the Scandinavian king of York, is defeated and killed; this allows Edred, King of England, to rule over a united kingdom for the first time.

accee007-730c-5f1a-af2a-50916530d925.description: Kenneth MacAlpin, regarded as the first king of Scotland, unites the Scots of Argyll and the Picts north of the Firth of Forth under his rule.

ad63b2ed-50f4-5781-a0b3-f43a0534252e.description: The border between Tunisia and Algeria is drawn.

ad7d3d4b-5c07-5f75-989a-9bda20539d44.description: Villagers (Fallahin) in Palestine revolt against the Abbasids’ taxation system. More than 10,000 people participate in this uprising.

addd7ffb-1d9e-5390-9ecf-d4bae80076f7.description: French expedition to Egypt, led by Napoleon, which continues for three years during which the first Arabic printing house was established in Egypt.

aebb39f0-0301-5f01-95fc-a5ba5020de14.description: Frederick of Aragon (1302–37) is proclaimed King of Sicily.

aed23dd2-da70-5f34-aef6-f6a964358c01.description: Emperor Franz Joseph I declares the February Patent and dismisses the Hungarian Diet. Ányos Jedlik invents the dynamo. Compulsory preventive injection against pox introduced in Szabolcs County by Dr Frigyes Korányi.

aedb2eeb-e5a0-59d2-947d-9d0e59dca69e.name: Reorganization of the bureaucracy
aedb2eeb-e5a0-59d2-947d-9d0e59dca69e.description: Reorganisation of the bureaucracy and introduction of a new system of rank.

aee55dcb-e64d-56d6-8d37-339110aa7cff.description: The Venetians install Krešimir III (1000–30) as king of Croatia; he ruled with his brother Gojislav. They attempted to restore rule over the Dalmatian cities that were under Venetian control.

af28fca7-bb8c-5944-b735-7537a932742b.name: Foundation of Jerusalem Bishopric
af28fca7-bb8c-5944-b735-7537a932742b.description: Evangelists in Britain and Germany found the Jerusalem Protestant bishopric. There is an idea of converting Jews – the first bishop is a converted Jew – and the bishopric establishes a British cultural and educational interest in the Levant. It also stimulates archaeological work.

af36b9c9-6f1e-5a17-981f-ad357810e44d.description: Great Mosque of Algiers built. Yusuf ibn Tashufin, having conquered Spain and Central Maghreb, promotes the emergence of Afro-Andalusian Moorish art: stalactite domes, poly-lobed arches and mosque orientation.

af92a6d2-d9c6-5177-992f-a62c4d3ddca0.name: Russo-Turco Treaty of St. Stefano
af92a6d2-d9c6-5177-992f-a62c4d3ddca0.description: 3 March: Russo-Turco Treaty of St Stefano defines Bulgaria, which includes present-day Bulgaria, present-day Macedonia and northern Greece.

afdb6c38-1876-5448-a684-99a1e014502c.description: Nikola Zrinski defeats the Pasha of Budim near Bobocsa. The fall of Kostajnica and the arrival of Ottomans in Turopolje.

afdf4a34-61cf-57cb-8a1a-f0c93d8cf7fb.description: Census: 3 million people in the Czech lands. Introduction of astandardised system of measures and weights. P. Diviš constructed the first lightning conductor. V. A. Kounic-Rietberg became court and state chancellor.

b00bece1-e9ef-51c4-a46d-2ca684955112.description: East India Company forces win the Battle of Plassey, placing control of Bengal in the hands of Great Britain; the victory achieves a significant presence in India for the British.

b0728687-0bba-5e7c-b532-bca6333bd220.description: The philosopher Immanuel Kant (1724–1804) publishes his book Kritik der praktischen Vernunft. He is considered a major philosopher of the Age of Enlightenment.

b0f65cad-ac36-5a16-9132-edb438476d9a.description: Ahmad Pasha al-Jazzar, replaces the rule of the family of Zahir ‘Umar, taking ‘Akka as the capital of his semi-independent state, fortifying the city and constructing its beautiful mosque, which still stands today.

b10de746-5b07-5d02-acce-b16eb208bec2.description: Muhammad Ali Pasha expels Ottoman governor and, achieving virtual independence from the Ottoman court, begins comprehensive efforts to modernise Egypt.

b16040fb-7fff-5e4d-9880-f8a9cd6aca41.description: Pico della Mirandola (1463–94) writes Oration on the Dignity of Man, an expression of the new Renaissance humanist culture that exalted man’s dignity and right to self-determination.

b186ce0e-da1f-5d1c-8fee-685d2d3a6538.description: ‘Abd al-Mu’min, who succeeds Al-Mahdi ibn Tumart, makes a ceremonious entrance in Marrakesh, announcing the triumph of the Almohad movement.

b1ce405d-02ce-57e6-b472-f5efa37d7128.description: The First Crusaders on their way to the Holy Lands arrive in Constantinople in December.

b20a151f-3e49-5055-a747-5fb897245e37.name: The Regicide in 1908 was fomented
b20a151f-3e49-5055-a747-5fb897245e37.description: 1 February: The assassination of King Carlos I and his heir-apparent Prince Royal Luis Filipe in Terreiro do Paço in central Lisbon, fomented by, among other things, the King’s appointment of João Franco as head of government in 1906; with the King’s consent he set up a dictatorship one year later. Queen Amelia and Prince Manuel escape and the prince is enthroned as King Manuel II.

b21a88ed-1bff-51d2-9572-59343ff27c02.description: Proclamation of the First Republic in Spain.

b22c9412-b81d-541c-ac67-550c7b3423fa.description: Treaty of Tordesillas: division of the lands discovered and to be discovered in the Eastern, Portuguese, hemisphere and the Western, Spanish, hemisphere.

b270bdbe-6be4-54c5-ada3-d9ad481b2a9f.name: Act of Union
b270bdbe-6be4-54c5-ada3-d9ad481b2a9f.description: The Irish Rebellion of 1798, which was intended to put an end to what Irish nationalists perceived as the subordination and dependency of Ireland on the British crown, instead contributes to the Irish parliament’s vote to join the union between the kingdoms of Great Britain and Ireland. On 1 January 1801, Britain, Scotland and Ireland sign the Act of Union and merge, to form the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland.

b28c9df7-14e9-5e9c-bf74-f08fcc4ae941.name: Treaty of Union
b28c9df7-14e9-5e9c-bf74-f08fcc4ae941.description: The Kingdom of Great Britain comes into being under the Treaty of Union of the kingdoms of England (which then included Wales) and Scotland on 1 May 1707. It lasts, controlled under a single parliament and government based at Westminster, up until 31 December 1800.

b335ab24-b315-5c09-960d-0f66de12da34.description: On 2 February King Otto I (r. 936–73) of the Ottonian Dynasty, later called Otto the Great, is crowned emperor in Rome.

b34d4400-42b8-5812-9665-4d46c62162cf.description:
The ‘Josephina’ road between Karlovac and Rijeka is constructed.  
The first stockmarket in Rijeka is established.

b3e72002-c909-5f0c-b8ce-2a1b2f9f4036.name: Egypt political status under Ottomans
b3e72002-c909-5f0c-b8ce-2a1b2f9f4036.description: During this time Egypt is a legally nominal Ottoman province governed by a *wali* on behalf of the Ottoman Sultan, although *de facto* it is virtually independent, with its *wali*s styling themselves as Khedives. Despite their legally subservient status, Egypt’s walis enjoy far more political power than their descendants, who, decades later, rule the country as nominally independent sultans and kings.

b3e9340f-746f-5f40-8598-469c96c12b25.description: The Golden Bull becomes the first constitution of the empire by which the German emperor is chosen by seven electors.

b4067dff-b620-5208-9c64-2fed65b17b3e.description: Philip V is proclaimed King of Spain. Start of the Spanish War of Succession, which lasts until 1714. Opening of the southern sea routes.

b408faee-eb68-5b03-92bc-1b638c1c30b8.description: Al-Ghazali, la principal figura religiosa del siglo XI, reside en Damasco. Sus obras representan un renacimiento de las ciencias religiosas.

b416af05-98cc-5124-a312-cb7cbfcdb093.description: A notary of King Béla III (Anonymus ‘Magister P.’) writes a chronicle of the Hungarian conquest and settlement (Gesta Hungarorum). The beginning of the rebuilding of the Kalocsa abbey (built in the 11th century).

b44afa8a-6fdd-5283-8e91-916b78e1be34.description: Reform of traditional teaching at the Zaytuna Mosque, which becomes official state-controlled teaching.

b48bd62b-fa7e-59b2-a51f-ae05444cce7d.description: Construction of the Zaytuna Mosque in Tunis.

b4d0e6d3-2101-5e35-aa03-dbfc992a7426.description: Displeased with the king’s rule noblemen force King András II to sign the Golden Bull that limits his power. In another order the king strengthens the privileges of the ecclesiastical order.

b4e565db-820f-5c5a-9daa-d2b536ddcd1d.description: Start of the Castilian War of the Communities.

b5117dae-7ecc-5e8d-8fba-fcfbda3221e9.description: Second siege of Constantinople by the Muslim Arabs.

b5185e44-a403-59df-aac5-72e0072cab29.description: The Portuguese Inquisition starts its work. Jesuits arrive in Portugal.

b529bd07-47c3-539d-9de7-789064fb5dfb.description: Sultan Sulayman I besieges Szigetvár defended by Count Miklós Zrínyi who getting no help and with heavy odds against him dies with his soldiers in a sortie. The Sultan had died two days earlier.

b544b3d8-93e2-507e-b42e-78206606849e.name: Egyptian navy sunk by the European Allied fleet
b544b3d8-93e2-507e-b42e-78206606849e.description: When under the command of an Ottoman representative the entire Egyptian navy is sunk by the European Allied fleet, Muhammad ‘Ali asks for the territory of Syria in compensation.

b5a7407b-9961-5d8b-a7e0-332975b142d3.description: Revolution ends the July Monarchy and the Second Republic is proclaimed. Slavery is abolished. Social movements lead to the June Insurrection, which is brutally put down. Algeria becomes a destination for deportees.

b625b9c3-b446-5b15-a72b-d1fcde8c6b1c.description: Bourgeois revolution demanding end of absolutism, equality of Czech with German, freedom of the press and religion. Abolition of serfdom and the corvée obligation. Slavic Assembly tries to found a Slavic association within the monarchy and turn it into a federal state.

b63c3d95-074d-5fb5-a748-3ee3b8172e4f.description: King Matyas II approves the new Statute of the Zagreb Gradec.

b64c70c6-7190-5fd3-91f8-d792e406301d.name: Revolution in Moldavia and Wallachia
b64c70c6-7190-5fd3-91f8-d792e406301d.description: January 1821–July 1822: revolution in Moldavia and Wallachia against the Phanariotes (Greek rulers imposed by the Ottoman Empire since the beginning of the 18th century) and for social and economic measures to improve the lives of the people. After the suppression of the revolution the Empire appoints Romanian rulers in Moldavia (Ioniţă Sandu Sturdza) and Walachia (Grigore Dimitrie Ghica).

b64dbe3a-8e3c-5a90-99b8-b1317c0f5e05.description: Orhan Gazi captures Bursa, which becomes the second Ottoman capital after Söğüt.

b6765682-4a1a-5ec4-9bd7-aeaabcaaf66b.description: On 10 June a great Arab revolt is launched by Husayn ibn ‘Ali, Sharif of Mecca and king of the Arabs, against the Ottomans to liberate Arab lands from Turkish occupation.

b742f38f-fcd3-5ba8-9605-1a54dd34a156.description: The Almoravids enter Fez and take control of the Maghreb.

b74eb8da-0d1f-50e5-afa9-b3165ba07882.name: Spain's neutrality in World War I
b74eb8da-0d1f-50e5-afa9-b3165ba07882.description: Spain's neutrality in World War I brings important economic upturn.

b76ca99e-e559-5fdf-9a8b-04dce8d4dd75.name: Berlin Conference was called by Portugal to regulate European colonization and convened by German Chancellor Otto von Bismarck
b76ca99e-e559-5fdf-9a8b-04dce8d4dd75.description: Berlin Conference called by Portugal to regulate European colonisation and convened by German Chancellor Otto von Bismarck. The Portuguese government presents the "Pink Map”, a project uniting the colonies of Angola and Mozambique through the corridor of land that separates them. The proposal is rejected by England although endorsed by the majority of countries.

b7a35988-6bae-5f8a-83fe-4a762ab7b7fd.description: Reorganisation of the Byzantine Empire and institution of the Exarchate of Carthage, consolidating the pre-eminence of the military.

b7cafd04-cfbc-5d2f-869c-b1244dba10e3.description: Restored administration. The highest Czech administrative institutions transferred to Vienna. German made equal with Czech, Catholicism became the only religion. Extensive confiscations and emigrations.

b866c80c-6101-513d-b43a-448219e41750.name: Al Qawasim attack British vessels
b866c80c-6101-513d-b43a-448219e41750.description: Between around 1790 and the early 1800s, threatened by increasing British inroads into traditional Gulf economies and politics, and supported by the Persians and Omanis, the Qawasim attack British vessels to defend their economic empire in the Lower Gulf.

b890b9a0-58fe-5006-9f93-59534db03cef.description: Idris II (son of Idris I) founds the town of al-Aliya in the Kairouan Quarter (Adwat al-Qayrawaniyyin) on the left bank of the Wadi Fez.

b8915690-0a5e-5709-a657-6a93c2f4cd39.description: Death of the scholar Ibn Khaldun in Egypt.

b8d722c9-0e0e-535a-9a57-a4dca583c9d5.description: Austria takes Milan and the Kingdom of Naples.

b8fe4d88-fe86-55cc-8116-70dc21138999.description: Restoration of independence under John IV and the start of the Bragança Dynasty.

b9453ddd-b1fa-5026-b5b4-80c48b1d90da.description: The caliphal court moves away from Syria and Baghdad, ‘City of Peace', is founded by the Abbasid Caliph al-Mansur, designed as a perfect circle.

b9624a6c-c148-5059-aa97-bb75b8d4815e.name: Liberation wars
b9624a6c-c148-5059-aa97-bb75b8d4815e.description: The Liberation Wars (and the decisive Battle of Leipzig in 1913) were between Napoleon Bonaparte’s French troops and Central Europe; Napoleon is overthrown.

b9cc4451-123b-507a-bae4-e230f5e04b15.description: Charlemagne, King of the Franks and the Lombards, is crowned emperor by Pope Leo III. He extends his power over part of the Germanic world and southwards beyond the Pyrenees in the ‘Hispanic March’. He establishes a relationship with the Caliph of Baghdad, Harun al-Rashid.

b9f3c4da-72a6-5963-a86e-8c41d7515200.name: Dreyfus Affair
b9f3c4da-72a6-5963-a86e-8c41d7515200.description: The Dreyfus Affair: Captain Dreyfus is unjustly accused of espionage, is militarily degraded, and then deported at the end of the trial. The writer Émile Zola denounces this situation in a pamphlet entitled *J’accuse*. The case divides France; it is recognised that Dreyfus is innocent.

ba088189-fc32-514c-92f5-dbb368c7cfb4.description: Fakhr al-Din al-Ma’ni II, a tribal ruler of Mount Lebanon and Western Syria, gains autonomy and attempts to by-pass Ottoman authority by signing a treaty with the Italian Tuscans.

bb041492-319e-5653-9660-c02e76c1dda1.name: Ibrahim Pasha expedition to Hijaz
bb041492-319e-5653-9660-c02e76c1dda1.description: Ibrahim Pasha leads Egypt’s expedition to Hijaz and crushes the Wahhabi Revolution.

bb06b73c-f591-5a2b-991b-6707ab102939.description: The authority of the Hungarian-Croatian parliament over Croatian internal legal questions is acknowledged at the joint council at Požun.

bb3fda76-0312-5e9a-a89e-1b9a45f32688.description: Foundation of the Kharijite cities of Mzab and start of the Hilalian invasions.

bb458b74-6213-5c57-bc33-ed788f6bcd7c.description: Hassan Pasha builds the Ketchaoua mosque.

bb4b1b57-1470-5bc6-a9fe-3412b633ab6b.description: Salah al-Din becomes sultan, extends Cairo’s fortifications and constructs the Citadel.

bb592ce6-edae-5d1a-a243-b1684f29fae9.description: Said Pasha grants concession to the French F. de Lesseps to construct the Suez Canal.

bb611188-8d8a-52d9-b54b-b22d3f63809a.name: King Abdulaziz ibn Abdulrahman startes unification of modern Saudi Arabia
bb611188-8d8a-52d9-b54b-b22d3f63809a.description: In 1902, age 19, King ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, along with a small army, returns to Riyad to reclaim his family legacy. Managing to take Riyad, ‘Abd al-Rahman then begins to unify modern Saudi Arabia.

bbd980f9-cebf-5faa-aa60-598d4144ac5b.description: Victory of the Kharijites at Tobna.

bbf9e8be-a84b-57dd-9985-b859352a0bbd.description: Cardinal Jules Mazarin becomes prime minister to the regent, Anne of Austria. He clashes with the ruling classes in the Frondes and emerges victorious.

bc0e4cd3-9761-5240-abd6-ea5558b08009.name: Formation of Young Ottoman opposition
bc0e4cd3-9761-5240-abd6-ea5558b08009.description: Formation of Young Ottoman opposition against the bureaucratic domination of Ali Paşa and Fuad Paşa.

bc39c11d-9f3f-5033-95ec-4c15448480ce.name: Partido Histórico and Partido Reformista merged into Progressist Partyin September
bc39c11d-9f3f-5033-95ec-4c15448480ce.description: Partido Histórico and Partido Reformista merge into the Partido Progressista in September. Power alternation with the Partido Regenerador framed rotativism. They were able to carry out some urgent reforms but in the end the system soon degenerated into political conformism.

bc9ad394-a1da-54aa-8d59-da7b490761ae.description: Sulayman I the Great occupies Buda. Hungary torn into three parts: Turkish *vilajet* (province); Upper Hungary under Ferdinand I; the rest under Queen Isabella and János II (János Zsigmond), son of the Queen and János I.

bcbb11ff-390a-518b-99f5-f2b734224056.description: The Great Nordic War breaks out, with Russia, Poland and Denmark against Sweden led by King Charles XII (Karl XII).

bdc520c0-d465-57f8-94ca-4cb5e75dd289.description: The Muslims begin the conquest of Spain under the leadership of Tarik ibn Ziyad.

bdd92207-0f4c-5503-baf6-bb04dce976f4.description:
Arrival of Jesuits in Zagreb. In 1607 they established the Classical Gymnasium, the first gymnasium (high school) that still exists today.  
Arrival of the first pharmacist J. Gasparini in Zagreb.

be037dae-57a2-56b8-82d6-1085352b1f7c.description: Muslims and Jews expelled from Castile, La Mancha and Extemadura, Andalusia, Catalonia and Murcia begin to settle in Morocco and other countries in the Maghreb.

be05c3dc-95d8-5943-a914-04c1689110f3.description: King Mátyás I dies and the all’ antica Renaissance presence in Hungary (see the Renaissance Buda castle, Mátyás I’s famous Corvina library) wanes. Struggle for the Hungarian throne.

be727f32-2d07-5474-95c2-145cf901fcb8.name: Reforms of Ahmad Pasha Bey
be727f32-2d07-5474-95c2-145cf901fcb8.description: Rule of Ahmad Pasha Bey, known as the “Great Reformer” of modern Tunisia. His greatest achievements include modernisation of the army and the abolition of slavery.

be990659-2366-541e-8272-7d59e40d54da.description: Peace of Utrecht: Spain loses its European territories.

bea24b3e-94e5-5465-8187-72544a565216.description: Pope Urban V affirms the Paulite order, founded by Hungarians c. 1250. King Lajos (Louis) I founds Pécs University and enriches Aachen Cathedral’s Hungarian Chapel with great artworks.

bf236d04-4009-51bb-ad6b-4483bda35b4a.description: Under the influence of Saint-Simonian Ismail Urban, Napoleon III applies his ‘Arab kingdom’ policy in Algeria.

bf2a3eee-32a7-59e6-a08f-d1f67a936713.description: Algiers founded by Buluggin ibn Ziri.

bfac147f-bfa2-5f5b-a074-cf774ea13e0e.name: Guerra de la Independencia
bfac147f-bfa2-5f5b-a074-cf774ea13e0e.description: Guerra de la Independencia (Peninsular War) during the French occupation of the Iberian Peninsula and the rule of King Joseph-Napoleon Bonaparte.

bfae2d2e-6b0a-5b1c-acf0-f9c9f030a8f7.description:
In Varaždin the first Jewish commune is established.  
Joseph II announces his ‘Patent on the abolishment of slavery’ for the territories of Hungary and Croatia.  
The first Real Gymnasium is opened in Senj.

bfd763d5-09d1-5db0-8408-5e1f7fba178e.description: On 3 September the Battle of ‘Ain Jalut takes place in Palestine between the Muslim Mamluks and the nomadic tribes of Mongols who defeated the Islamic world in the 13th century, destroying cities and killing citizens. The Mamluk victory in this battle stops the march of the Mongol army in Jordan and Palestine.

bff4327f-780e-50a1-b88c-190b4d016eaf.description: In this year the German missionary Ansgarius visits Birka, preaching Christianity to the Swedes, according to Vita Ansgarii by the monk Rimbert.

c00fe438-1fca-56ab-a07f-59e48b5ac90e.description: After the town is forcibly taken by the King of France in 1660, Colbert grants the Marseilles Chamber of Commerce a special statute, giving it the power to authorise French subjects to establish themselves in the Ports of the Levant, and he pays his ‘consuls’ by levying a 20% tax on goods carried by foreign ships.

c05c7d66-c994-5535-bf3d-f1dbb65a6028.name: War between Greece and the Ottoman Empire whereby the Greece attain their national indepence
c05c7d66-c994-5535-bf3d-f1dbb65a6028.description: The War between Greece and the Ottoman Empire concludes with Greece attaining its independence with the help of Russia and the Western nations.

c06fd0fe-9f1f-56a4-a4fe-eaa140c0ae59.description: Charles I fails to arrest five members of Parliament for treason and leaves London to raise an army; the First English Civil War begins between Cavaliers (royalists) and Roundheads (parliamentarians).

c0aba31a-80c6-5273-a220-b84597e0f473.description: On the 4th of July, the American Congress passes the Declaration of Independence, which formalises the 13 colonies’ independence from British rule.

c0d92fc5-643e-5316-bbd3-ecb8e503fb82.description: Ibrahim Pasha administers Syria on behalf of his father Muhammad Ali Pasha (in Cairo) following the process of Westernisation.

c0fd7a73-d8ef-54d3-acf7-1b95c60e99f0.name: Death of king Carol I
c0fd7a73-d8ef-54d3-acf7-1b95c60e99f0.description: Death of King Carol I. As he only had one daughter, who died at the age of three, Ferdinand, his fraternal nephew, had been designated heir to the Romanian throne in 1880.

c107a8ac-aa8d-5c26-b7e9-2acbaccec4fe.description: Amuri, King of Jerusalem and leader of the Crusader army, captures the city of Bilbis and slaughters every man, woman and child. The burning of Fustat is ordered by Shawar, minister of the Fatimid caliph, to prevent the Crusaders from reaching Cairo. Twenty thousand barrels of oil were used for this purpose and the fire continued for 54 days.

c1191510-fdd8-540b-b777-5815e1913a56.description: Wenceslas IV inherits Czech crown. Completion of the oldest Czech translation of the Bible. Klaret’s (Claretus) attempt to create Czech scholarly terminology. Discord among the king, his brothers and the aristocracy.

c11a8a08-9416-5eb8-b06a-3bb77699d825.description: Swedish missionaries are involved in Tamil Nadu (India) for the first time.

c12a3d56-3254-5e4a-bbe8-2633f4552dd2.name: First Serbian Uprising
c12a3d56-3254-5e4a-bbe8-2633f4552dd2.description: The First Serbian Uprising culminates in the first Serbian *Vožd* (Grand Leader), a progenitor of the Karađorđević Dynasty, Đorđe Petrović. He is elected, at a gathering of the Serbs at Orašac on the Feast of the Presentation, having won many famous victories against stronger and better-armed Turkish armies at Ivankovac, Mišar and Varvarin. Following the Treaty of Bucharest and the failure of the Uprising, Petrović flees to Austria in 1813, but soon after, eager to continue his efforts at expelling the Turks, he joins the Greek liberation movement. He secretly returns to Serbia in 1817 to discuss a joint plan of action with the Prince of Serbia Miloš Obrenović, but Miloš has him assassinated.

c1a052a1-d3df-5007-9fa2-ef15c7daad0f.description: The Muslim fleet is defeated by the Pisans at Palermo.

c23b6072-da45-5b41-93d3-84c3264c7d22.description: As a result of the revolution in November 1918 Germany becomes a republic. Emperor Wilhelm II abdicates.

c2ac4726-0fb6-51b3-8e4b-75d99c1ed6ec.name: Rebellion of reactionaries against constitutional system
c2ac4726-0fb6-51b3-8e4b-75d99c1ed6ec.description: The 31 March Incident (31 Mart Vakası/Olayı or Hadisesi) is a rebellion on 13 April (31 March in official Rumi calendar) in Constantinople against restoration of the constitutional system. It is the culmination of the Ottoman countercoup that attempted to end the Second Constitutional Era in the empire and the newly established influence of the Committee of Union and Progress in order to reaffirm Abdülhamid II as absolute monarch.

c2cfc86e-3d78-557f-b498-ae8f293a68ac.description: Beginning of the Muslim invasion of the peninsula following victory over the Visigoths at the Battle of Guadalete.

c300e0d4-21f2-5804-b91a-5e00d38022a5.description: According to Annales Cambriae, the Battle of Camlann is fought between the forces of King Arthur and Mordred; both leaders are killed in the battle.

c325c56a-f379-5525-a0bb-71fa220749a5.description: The Fourth Crusade, which will last until 1204, leaves from Venice.

c3385d5c-571e-559d-8bd4-9c5b2553d3d5.description: The marriage of the daughter of Khumarawayh, Qatr al-Nada, to the Abbasid Caliph al-Mu'tadid. The legendary wedding, including the trousseau, costs the Egyptian treasury over 1.2 million gold dinars.

c34053e8-373d-51c1-9459-84324ae6402b.description: On the death of Henry I of England, his nephew Stephen of Blois stages a coup and seizes the English throne in place of Henry’s daughter and designated successor, the Empress Matilda.

c34fbefc-cd49-5776-8bd7-bc1e1e4ccb08.description: The century is marked by trials and crises that shake the Hafsid kingdom: civil wars, foreign incursions and cholera epidemics.

c40011c6-a118-5cd6-852d-ecb3cffbf6bc.description: Palestine in general and Jerusalem in particular celebrate the Ottoman conquest of Constantinople.

c450cd75-fa24-561e-a4cd-2ac9f99cdd45.description: The powerful As‘ad Pasha al-‘Azm governs Damascus and comes down heavily on the local janissaries who were rising in power. He builds the ‘Azm palaces in Hama and in Damascus, as well as his famous caravanserai.

c471d86e-177b-59c8-bbc1-f86d92947636.description: Sidi Muhammad ibn ‘Abdallah founds the port town of Essaouira and begin the economic reorganisation of the kingdom.

c495b5a1-d33e-5830-8f73-2b4173b274eb.description: Ya‘qub al-Mansur founds the town of Rabat (Ribat al-Fath – the field of victory).
