c49acc6e-15c5-51b5-a7c9-07fac2322ced.description: First edition of The Lusiads by Luís de Camões.

c6035d9a-14a2-5e29-8236-99c2ed96bd1a.description: Charles IV elected Roman king. The period of his rule embraced the greatest flourishing of the Czech lands. Origination of the Czech crown jewels. Cult of St Wenceslas disseminated.

c61a5b3a-b12b-5c2b-a169-6feb08ed2c4b.name: Bashir II breaks away from the Ottoman Empire
c61a5b3a-b12b-5c2b-a169-6feb08ed2c4b.description: Bashir II breaks away from the Ottoman Empire, allies with Muhammad ‘Ali Pasha of Egypt and assists his son Ibrahim Pasha in a siege of Acre. This siege lasts seven months before the fall of the city on 27 May 1832. They also conquer Damascus on 14 June 1832.

c66f6fba-6819-5196-9c17-35fb4891c439.description: The socio-cultural movement in Ifriqiya flourishes with individuals such as Sidi Bou Saïd and Sidi Mehrez venerated as patron saints.

c7156df8-c0a2-5be7-b62f-c2ea87445ef9.description: Sultan al-Nasir Muhammad bin Qalawun defeats Ghazan, King of Tartars, in the Levant.

c71bc23e-42c8-5156-858d-a7641dd585a9.description: Master Simon Kézai, a cleric of King László (Kun) IV, starts to compile the Gesta Hungarorum, a chronicle of Hungary (completed in 1285) that contains the theory of the Hun-Hungarian identity.

c75815d0-8188-52cd-83f8-d9af69f1a938.description: The Fatimid restore the city walls of Jerusalem.

c75a9819-4fac-5fb8-b9ea-f60b264d5c5d.name: Demonstrations and riots against high bread price
c75a9819-4fac-5fb8-b9ea-f60b264d5c5d.description: Widespread demonstrations and riots against high bread price. The government uses the army to repress protests: in Milan 85 demonstrators are killed.

c79a75fb-768d-524b-b8d4-01aa62350453.description: Elizabeth I accedes to the throne of England and Ireland and rules for 45 years; she is the daughter of Henry VIII and Anne Boleyn and the final monarch of the Tudor dynasty.

c7ae992c-e206-51a0-b860-847bb3d2ab40.description: Army conscription is introduced in the Ottoman empire; there is evidence of the contribution of Ajlun inhabitants to army life.

c7affa80-67ee-523c-9282-f78edebeb07c.name: Austria had to cede the Venetian province
c7affa80-67ee-523c-9282-f78edebeb07c.description: Following defeat at the Battle of Königgrätz (3 October), at the Peace of Vienna, Austria is forced to cede the Venetian province to Italy.

c7e39669-756d-5628-a85e-5f6e63e52e37.description: A treaty is made between the Roman Empire and the Ghassanids, a Christian Arab tribe settled in southern Syria and Damascus, in order to defend the eastern frontiers against the Persians.

c7f4290b-1cb7-515d-a3bb-a56997bc66da.description: Gustav Vasa is elected King at Strängnäs, freeing Sweden from Danish sovereignty.

c81b6084-c7e0-5ee6-9d42-2ebe66c13390.description: Battle of Salado. Decisive victory over the Marinids of North Africa, who had led the final Muslim offensive in the Peninsula.

c8237ae8-0e29-5625-bcad-e1a782a53f93.name: The beginning of the Greek Revolution
c8237ae8-0e29-5625-bcad-e1a782a53f93.description: The Greek Revolution against the Ottoman Empire begins.

c824d709-d2ba-5633-ad39-4ee07e7b96ca.description: Isabel II ascends to the throne and start of a period of regency. Process of building a liberal Spanish state begins. Start of the first Carlist War (1833–40) against Isabel’s coronation, claiming the dynastic right of her uncle, Carlos María Isidro.

c82b56d8-1f36-56eb-9d96-985565899101.description:
Lund University is founded in Scania, the southernmost part of the country, which had then recently become part of Sweden.  
In the same year a series of witch trials and executions begins in Dalarna. It spreads over large parts of Sweden in the following nine years. Many innocent women are accused of witchcraft and burned at the stake.

c8403923-cc76-54ee-ad2b-f2c59506b3b4.description: Tarik ibn Ziyad crosses the Straits of Gibraltar, defeats King Roderick of Spain and takes Córdoba and Toledo.

c8535c0d-6a38-5567-8f06-e61e10b00a66.description: Jesuit Stjepa Glavač, a professor of the Zagreb Academy, publishes the first domestic geographic map of Croatia, which meets the high standards of cartography of that time in Europe.

c87a811f-3fcb-5dcb-a5f5-0343b00e651b.description: The start of the Thirty Years’ War (1618–48) between Protestants and Catholics; the war has disastruous results, including death, poverty and serious economic stagnation.

c87ad466-47cd-5bbc-8931-fde4642d0bd1.description: Hammad ibn Buluggin ibn Ziri founds the Qal’at Bani Hammad. His mosque and palaces were to inspire the architects of the Giralda in Seville and the Cuba in Palermo.

c97e8963-bfc2-5a43-b2bf-c81b0ecc5b58.description: The Hafsids take several town in Central Maghreb: Constantine (1233) and Béjaia (1235).

c9bba37d-a0bf-5fc3-a408-e9a5dab9da60.description: Sultan al-Ghawri is killed in battle against the Ottomans. His successor Tuman Bay, the last Mamluk sultan, was captured a few months later and hung on Bab Zuweila by Selim I, the Ottoman sultan. Khayrbek, governor of Aleppo, who betrayed the Mamluks was appointed first Ottoman governor of Egypt.

ca13f3c3-9178-595b-a98d-ba165ecdfeae.description: Liberal victory in the civil war. Establishment of a constitutional monarchy.

ca23cae6-e740-535b-ba20-c9ca85b8f263.description: Charles IV is the first Czech sovereign to be crowned Holy Roman Emperor. In 1356 he issued the Golden Bull confirming the autonomous Czech state and making the Czech king foremost among the electors.

ca28c751-c4e6-57ae-9c23-329e3402cafe.description: ‘Alawid Sharif Mulay Ali al-Sharif is proclaimed Sultan of Morocco.

ca350f1e-6708-5ae1-93ac-c94410b0097a.description: The great geographer Ibn Battuta, born in Tangiers, begins a 25-year journey that would take him to China in Asia and Timbuktu in Africa.

ca4dab82-c037-5e7d-9cc9-f142bc8064f3.description: Galileo Galilei finishes his telescope and publishes Starry Messenger, prompting scientific reflection that plunges the Church’s thinking on the universe into crisis for the first time.

ca9db0f2-bfab-57f5-9bb0-418ad0d229da.description: Amedeo, Duke of Aosta, is elected King of Spain by the Spanish Parliament; he rules with the name of Amadeo I.

cada2b2a-5077-51db-b8bd-293193a7a1c8.description: Joseph II abolishes all male and female religious orders except those which take care of the sick and helpless or are engaged in education.

cae30c3c-1b20-553e-8959-9c14f0cec485.description: Death of Paracelsus (1493–1541), physician, philosopher and writer of medical treatments, who was a defender of empirical medicine and rejected Gnostic traditions.

caf5e20d-1898-53d0-ac57-1bb917b199ec.description: Death of al-Maqrizi, the great Egyptian historian.

cafcedd7-d08c-58c0-88a0-9afe6f78d930.name: Ibrahim Pasha was forced to retreat to Egypt
cafcedd7-d08c-58c0-88a0-9afe6f78d930.description: Bilad al-Sham (Greater Syria, including Jordan) is under Ibrahim Pasha who is ruling on behalf of his father, Muhammad 'Ali of Egypt. Ibrahim Pasha is forced to retreat to Egypt through Transjordan where the Egyptian army suffers severe casualties on its way back to Egypt.

cb033485-0266-5359-af4e-d3c570e6095b.description: Aragon incorporates the Kingdom of Naples.

cb1217ce-60de-563d-a0ab-97790f36d7a0.description: Christopher Columbus discovers America. Lorenzo de’Medici dies.

cb81d3bf-ba06-5fd6-bead-e6de159d3027.description: First expedition of Muslim Arabs in Ifriqiya. Victory at Sufetula (Sbeitla).

cb9b4b59-170b-5014-b533-c938a5423c1a.description: Completion of Karlštejn Castle: Emperor’s residence housing the Czech and imperial crown jewels, the archive and relics of saints. The construction of the Stone (now Charles) Bridge, Prague.

cbd2db7e-72ef-5012-a5f3-845860281f0e.description: To suppress the Ahmad Orabi rising the British Fleet bombards Alexandria. The beginning of the British occupation of Egypt, which will continue for 72 years.

cc06deec-2f3e-5bd9-a760-ea299e41ce57.description: The Marinids enter Marrakesh, ousting the Almohads.

cca6a898-27a6-5c20-abde-316a4c04542f.description: Renewal of the Capitulations by Louis XIV. The galleys run by each power ‘must not cause any damage’ to the other.

cccc2bda-a276-59ef-83e1-5fd09865f622.name: Northern Ireland
cccc2bda-a276-59ef-83e1-5fd09865f622.description: Following Ireland’s decision to secede from the United Kingdom, Northern Ireland immediately exercises its right to opt out of the new dominion and remain one of the four countries of the United Kingdom.

cd30deaf-8bf6-5320-b0ae-ecdc9ca88c01.description: The beatification of St. John of Nepomuk, drowned in the Vltava (Prague) in 1393. The most popular saint in the Czech lands, Lower Austria and southern Germany.

cd59198c-6c78-50bf-a618-10e0a1bd1dc1.description: Treaty of Alcanises, which fixes the Portuguese border.

cd6e3fcb-a2b9-556f-9ecf-aa89e48b9b94.description: A madrasa for teaching Shafi’i rites (one of four Sunni rites in Islam) is established at Karak; King Muhammad ibn Qalawun sent his sons to study at this madrasa.

cd81a354-8325-5bdf-a706-90372cee8350.description: Reign of Barsbay marks the beginning of a period of peace, cultural vitality and increased trade.

cd82c248-d129-5e7e-8dad-52f6b3518d9d.name: Second French Revolution of July
cd82c248-d129-5e7e-8dad-52f6b3518d9d.description: 27–29 July: the Second French Revolution of July 1830 results in the fall of Charles X, who is succeeded by his cousin Louis-Philippe.

cdb44628-286e-58a4-a172-35be0c6e4cef.description: The fez is introduced, along with judicial, military and administrative reforms on more Western models in the Ottoman Empire.

cde4a42a-7836-5f60-bcf4-af77253199ed.description: Beginning of the Rif War. Tragic Week in Barcelona, with protests against the sending of Catalan reservists to the war in Africa.

cdf9940a-81ce-5846-840d-f1fc8b0691b1.name: Anarchist Gaetano Bresci kills the King Umberto I
cdf9940a-81ce-5846-840d-f1fc8b0691b1.description: Anarchist Gaetano Bresci kills the King Umberto I, in revenge for the protesters killed in Milan in 1898. Victor Emanuel III becomes King of Italy.

ce1bd9f9-0d3d-5f64-bbc1-ec2be2dc878e.description: War breaks out in Europe following Germany’s invasion of Belgium; World War I kills more than 16 million people between 1914 and the Armistice in November 1918.

ce5a2b73-bf3c-5d8e-8ead-a7760392a485.description: Work starts on the palace-convent of Mafra, commissioned by John V (r. 1705–50).

ce5ab688-36af-5c17-bf70-1f1c3171bc86.description: Adherents of Martin Luther, the German religious reformer, appear in Prague. Outbreak of conflicts among Catholics, Utraquists and Lutherans. Anabaptists in Moravia.

ce5ef438-a99b-58e9-91d3-868e95d90512.description: Abbasid campaigns in the south. Conquest of Lisbon and Mértola.

cea62768-a82e-516b-8739-68da41e5739c.description: A Portuguese column infiltrates Moroccan lands and begin work on the Graciosa fortress on the Loukkos River.

ceb082e2-41c6-5247-9b6d-5f2c151c9212.description: The personal union between Sweden and Norway is dissolved.

cece3c05-9623-5ee2-bb38-05d397db175e.description: The beginning of the compilation of the Pray codex (contains the first continuous Hungarian texts) and the oldest Hungarian chronicle, the Annals of Pozsony (Pressburg, today: Bratislava, Slovakia).

cf41c193-d7d7-55eb-ba75-fef5a91fe51c.description: End of the monarchy (revolution of 5 October).

cf7629ca-daa6-5361-abca-22273c761e10.name: British declare the independence of Egypt
cf7629ca-daa6-5361-abca-22273c761e10.description: Britain declares Egyptian independence, but retains control of Egyptian foreign policy and the basic administration of the country. On 15 March of this year, Fuad I issues a decree changing his title from Sultan of Egypt to King of Egypt.

cfff96d7-be4e-591d-83a2-bf64ce44e84a.description: ‘Abd al- Mu’min rebuilds the mosque of Tinmel, birthplace of the Almohad dynasty and the prototype of its mosques.

d0055e62-03e6-5062-b550-94e01bccb816.description: Conversion of Oghuz Turks to Islam.

d0682c4b-7e25-541d-9c53-2d7c70c06280.description: Plague attacks cities and villages, taking many lives.

d084e8e7-42cc-5ea4-a428-d0fdca31f841.description: Division of the Carolingian Empire. Charles the Bald’s West Francia is attacked from the north by the Normans and the south by the Saracens (after 838). Royal authority is limited by the growth of large regional principalities.

d09c6663-d561-54e2-990c-7f950c4e0c9f.name: Proclamation of the Republic of Turkey
d09c6663-d561-54e2-990c-7f950c4e0c9f.description: 29 October: Proclamation of the Republic of Turkey. Mustafa Kemal Atatürk becomes the first president of Turkey.

d0a1821f-6553-5881-8654-dca4b4851c0b.description: Adrian IV grants a papal bull, Laudabiliter, which recognises Henry II of England as lord of Ireland and licenses English colonisation of Ireland; the process begins with Henry’s arrival in 1171.

d0d5cca8-455e-57b4-a64e-4df10dda0bf3.name: Second Serbian Uprising
d0d5cca8-455e-57b4-a64e-4df10dda0bf3.description: The Second Serbian Uprising – the Takovo Uprising – represents the second stage of the Serbian revolt against the Ottoman Empire, which breaks out soon after. The revolt leads to recognition of Serbian autonomy within the Ottoman Empire and establishment of the *Kneževina* (Principality) of Serbia, which obtained its own Assembly, Constitution and ruling dynasty.

d0ebefd8-0ffb-57eb-bf50-f6d8700012eb.description: Badi' al-Zaman al-Jazari (from al-Jazira) is commissioned by the Atabeg Artuqid court to write his brilliant illustrated manuscript on mechanical engineering, a milestone in technology history.

d11003b4-e777-5ecb-b0eb-805d3ec485fe.description: Battle of Mohacs. Ludwig Jagellon defeated by the Turks, the dynasty died out. According to a contract from 1515, the Czech throne passes to the Habsburg dynasty. Anti-Habsburg movement of the Czech Estates.

d192615b-1534-5d7d-adf1-b637a02711eb.description: Execution of the leaders of the Wesselényi revolt against the Habsburgs. All needs of the Austrian armies based in Hungary paid for by Hungary causing paupery. Continuing oppression of Protestants.

d1cbecff-0106-5906-b954-c1f48fa72143.description: Fakhr al-Din al-Ma’ni (1590–1635) expands his control of Lebanon to major parts of Palestine.

d1d1554b-3362-5368-9218-36949157048f.description: The start of the new army Nizam-ı Cedid (New Order) by Selim III.

d1d28ea9-863c-574b-8177-58ec73feafc1.description: Vasco da Gama leaves for India.

d24acba2-dc90-58c7-8d82-7ac4a6eaf1ed.name: Battle of Omdurman
d24acba2-dc90-58c7-8d82-7ac4a6eaf1ed.description: Sudan is in possession of the Egyptians until a Sudanese revolt under the Mahdi severs the connection. It is brought back to Anglo-Egyptian rule with a military conquest led by an Egyptian army officered by the British. Control of Sudan facilitated British colonial expansion in Sub-Saharan Africa.

d26cc83d-0def-5c56-817e-635316052e2c.description: Tankaz, the Mamluk governor of Syria begins a comprehensive construction project in Jerusalem including Madrasa Tankaziyya, Suq al-Qattanin, Khan Tankaz, two bathhouses and a minaret.

d27c91d8-b51a-5f96-9b4f-43602e02ce25.description: The birth at Mecca on 2 July of Prophet Muhammad, the messenger of God who introduced Islam to the whole world.

d2d232be-77e5-5589-b163-5011502463c4.description: The Hafsid Kingdom of Tunis exerts a remarkable influence in politics, economics and culture.

d30aeb41-22eb-5171-b465-98b2ac76c327.description: Death of the historian Ibn Khaldun.

d327227e-c522-5553-af40-86f52c894373.description: On 20 August a local government is formalised in Salt city after the decline of the Arab Kingdom at Damascus; its council of state was headed by Mazhar Rislan and its membership was made up of deputies from Amman, Madaba and ‘Udawn tribe.

d36604ba-45ea-57e0-adbc-56e7b6d707aa.description: In this, or the following, year, King Magnus grants freedom of taxes for those who serve him in his wars as equestrians. This was important step in the development of privileged nobility.

d42b5254-a078-5f1d-8da7-98560fa6908c.description: Establishment of the independent Czechoslovak state after the end of the First World War. President T. G. Masaryk elected (1920) (d. 1937). Origins of the theory of art and art history institutions.

d42e6053-1207-5eac-9c32-ba07f5996c9c.description: Foundation of the town of Raqqada a few kilometres outside Kairouan.

d441d9d9-9d79-5a5d-b9e5-0730eba6dce7.description: Charles of Anjou, brother of the King of France, marries Beatrice, heir to the Count of Provence. Sailors from Marseilles become special allies of the Angevins in southern Italy.

d448e324-dea8-57ed-b5a0-3c7e59d063ad.description: Pope Boniface VIII (1295–1303), in conflict with the French for political reasons, is arrested by the French, but immediately released following a popular uprising.

d4860780-9509-5d8d-b6f9-352b581af192.name: The Straits Convention
d4860780-9509-5d8d-b6f9-352b581af192.description: 13 July: The Straits Convention, signed by the Ottoman Empire and the great powers, prohibits foreign warships from entering the Bosphorus or the Dardanelles.

d4bbbe9d-548a-5705-8eb8-4cfc5b9910c1.description: Work starts on the Hieronymites Monastery.

d50438da-0cee-5e33-978d-cb233a2697f2.description: At the Battle of Marj Dabiq, north of Aleppo, the Ottoman Empire defeats the Mamluks and takes over Syria.

d5152fda-76e7-5dae-a0d9-1d2f36e55fc6.description: The King of France, Charles VI, is afflicted by madness. France falls into civil war, and the Treaty of Troyes recognises Henry V of England as the heir to the French throne.

d57ef1fd-9b93-512c-adf0-5ac932aba9b0.description: Return of Ferdinand VII and restoration of autocracy.

d5aa0473-92b6-535a-9451-3e271c580839.description: Construction of the Sidi Bel Hassan Mosque in Tlemcen.

d5ee18bf-fa6d-5978-a139-5ebdd84668d9.name: In consequence of the Prussian-Danish war
d5ee18bf-fa6d-5978-a139-5ebdd84668d9.description: As a consequence of the Prussian–Danish war, Denmark retracts its demand for Schleswig and Holstein.

d62eb47e-c4d2-58b2-87b6-1d7f30fce072.description: Austro-Hungarian monarchy ends. Charles IV agrees to the form of state chosen by the Hungarian nation but does not abdicate. Count Mihály Károlyi is Prime Minister of the People’s Republic of Hungary, which lays down arms and starts armistice talks.

d63d9614-3dc4-5914-bca6-562df6c9cf5a.name: Defeat of the Greek army duting the Greek -Turkish war
d63d9614-3dc4-5914-bca6-562df6c9cf5a.description: Defeat of the Greek Army during the Greek–Turkish War.

d680b239-defd-5fb4-824d-123331d240d3.description: ‘Uqba (Okba) ibn Nafi reaches Sebta, Tangiers then Walili (Ancient Volubilis) before going on to the town of Nfis in the Haouz and Igli in the Souss.

d6a1262e-96c2-576c-aaf1-286b2b02a307.description: Further Capitulations allow subjects of Western Christian nations (particularly Spanish, Portuguese and Neapolitan) to trade within the Ottoman Empire ‘with the consent and protection of the banner of France’. The alliance with the ‘Grand Seigneur’ is renewed in 1597.

d6d22b87-4333-572c-9d32-824cfd38f3cb.name: Creation of the Emirate of Transjordan
d6d22b87-4333-572c-9d32-824cfd38f3cb.description: By August 1921 this British policy has been changed and it is decided to establish the Emirate of Transjordan under the leadership of Husayn ibn ’Ali’s son, Prince ‘Abdallah, who will become King of Jordan in 1946.

d7184f37-632b-550e-8191-79287a888a15.description: Death of Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz (1646–1716), last universal genius in Germany and founder of the Prussian Academy of Science, who made major contributions in philosophy and mathemathics.

d7a5e47d-dffb-5324-99c0-ea5f93794b2f.description: Achir founded by Ziri ibn Manad.

d7bbafec-4995-54c2-9b69-d9f7a93f9e10.description: The ‘Triumph of Orthodoxy’ that marks the end of the second Iconoclastic Period (814–42) in the Byzantine Empire. Theodora, the regent for her son Michael III, orders the restoration of the icons.

d7c0ba86-2670-50a8-a0e9-229880d1cff3.description: Around this time the portcullis gate in the Eketorp ring-fort on Öland falls for the last time. As far as we know, this gate, built around AD 400, was the first of its kind outside the Roman Empire.

d8178e1b-75fb-5950-86bb-9b794229a34b.name: Giuseppe Mazzini founds the Giovine Italia
d8178e1b-75fb-5950-86bb-9b794229a34b.description: Giuseppe Mazzini founds the republican movement for national unification, Giovine Italia (Young Italy).

d8898867-5089-58c8-b7a6-cc7af47bbef9.description: Vienna was surrounded by Turkish armies and Moravia was plundered before the Turks were forced back to the Balkans. The last Turkish war in Europe.

d8bb351d-decf-56fc-824c-191e0f0f9636.name: By the end of July 1916 the ports of Jiddah, Yanbu and Rabegh were in Arab hands
d8bb351d-decf-56fc-824c-191e0f0f9636.description: By the end of July 1916, the seaports of Jeddah, Yanbu and Rabigh are in Arab hands. This allows the British to increase their supply of arms and equipment to the Arab forces fighting in the Hijaz.

d8d9d642-a711-5136-bdad-fe9e9688f1da.description: Deposition and exile of the last sultan, Mehmed Vahiduddin.

d8eb5131-93d9-5553-a4e8-12d1f3bb75b5.description: Battle of Muhi: Mongolian troops led by Khan Batu defeat the army of King Béla IV. At the end of the Mongol invasion in 1242 Austrian and Styrian forces also attacked Hungary, which was rebuilt by King Béla IV.

d8ecdf6b-5b33-5360-b5d3-32068d0ed13e.description: Abolition of the Caliphate of Cordova.

d8faf424-dbf7-5084-8268-7865f0071002.description: Brief reign of Shajar al-Durr, widow of al-Salih Ayyub, as Sultana for 80 days.

d92743d5-0fb0-5c9a-8f0f-d125f43c5a5f.description: Amir Ziri ibn Atiya of the Maghrawa founds the town of Oujda in Eastern Morocco.

d9284d5a-fbf9-5b26-9f54-b06fcf1fb2fc.description: Coronation of (St) István who affirms his authority over the Hungarian leaders (e.g. in 1003 over Gyula in Transylvania) and establishes Hungary’s legal, administrative and ecclesiastical system.

d9938d03-6f40-5f32-9ebe-47a56c3e1c1b.description: F. Křižík invents the self-acting regulator of the arc lamp, the first electrical lighting. His invention was received to great worldwide acclaim. The first telephone network introduced (1882).

da43fca1-5998-517d-be0a-aa3e6869443a.description: Musa ibn Nossayr becomes the first governor of Ifriqiya.

da9f2411-7c61-5ded-bc8d-bbddf1185af5.name: Third Republic
da9f2411-7c61-5ded-bc8d-bbddf1185af5.description: The Third Republic had a difficult start: the Treaty of Versailles with Prussia granting Alsace and Lorraine to the German Empire, and repression of the Commune. After a period known as the “Moral Order”, the Opportunist (1879–98) or Radical Republic (1898–1914) set up a large number of reforms in all areas, which include among others: a law on primary education (1881–2); a law on freedom of the press (1881); the restoration of the law on divorce (1884); a law allowing Trades Unions (1884); and a law on the separation of Church and State (1905).

daa73a72-f069-50c3-abbc-df5a38d392b0.description: Mazagán (al-Jadida), the last Portuguese town in Morocco, is abandoned.

db3cf6a9-5343-5856-9f86-57ba82b813a3.description: The siege of Siget. Nikola Šubić Zrinski holds out against the army of the Sultan Sulayman I and falls during the last attack.

dbdc55cf-cbdc-57f4-92f4-24bcbfdb2f84.description: Anders Celsius presents his thermometer, which shows the temperature on a scale of 100 degrees.

dbe59a55-2cd7-53ec-b4b2-afb589fe96bd.description: Jesuit mathematician Ruđer Bošković publishes his work *De natura et usu infinitorum et infinite parvorum* in Rome.

dbfb208e-9ef7-5de2-80cf-cbb2915bc41d.description: The Fatimid Caliph al-Hakim bi-Amrillah (r. 996–1021) orders the destruction of the Holy Sepulchre Church. Ten years later he would order its rebuilding.

dc118738-02b5-525d-888b-545b10c9c60f.description: Political stability under the reign of the Hafsid princes.

dc5090aa-a461-51b6-a23d-7087c1e20e77.description: Battle of Austerlitz (Battle of Three Emperors). Austria, Prussia and Russia defeated by Napoleon.

dc8a4daa-7306-5da4-b957-b12cbfd3a082.description: In pursuit of a South Slav cultural union bishop Josip Strossmayer founds the Yugoslav Academy of Arts and Sciences.

dc9368d3-fea8-55cb-9f02-8e9c8be66205.description: Decree of Kutná Hora adjusts the university voting rights between the Czechs and other nationalities. Jan Hus appointed university chancellor. Origins of the Hussite reformation movement, critical of church rule.

dce2677e-94dc-5b49-bd57-0a7cea6fe4b2.description: End of the civil war in Castile and start of the Trastámara dynasty.

dd13de0c-ab78-5a7d-b509-d34b51f10b4d.description: Battle of Hattin in which Salah al-Din defeats the Crusader army and liberates Jerusalem.

dd25461e-de8f-5476-85c3-6c77ed048053.description: The Almohads lose the Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa in Andalusia.

dd26d7b2-753d-5c64-a874-8775f4efc0cb.description: At the Battle of Yarmuk on 15 August the Muslim army defeats the Byzantine forces. Damascus is definitively occupied and the Islamic conquest of Syria begins.

dd5c065d-477f-5ea9-8e11-662a99b5b09c.description:
According to some, the Croatian kingdom was established and Duke Tomislav became its first king.  
The first Church Synod is held in Split.

de28ed00-1d01-5505-a1e9-e174ff172b66.description: Decisive encounter between the armies of ‘Abd al-Mu’min and Tashufin ibn Ali near Oran. Death throes of the Almoravid dynasty.

de2f000c-cfaa-5bfa-b2e4-3ec80a893998.name: The first Tunisian political party
de2f000c-cfaa-5bfa-b2e4-3ec80a893998.description: The first Tunisian political party is established as the Constitutional Liberal Party of Tunisia: “Le destour’’. In a pamphlet published anonymously in Paris, one of its founders, Abdelaziz al-Thalibi, specified the party’s demands.

de69d57f-9181-57df-a130-8edc2aaa1536.description: The building of the Aswan Dam to control the Nile water and the entire irrigation system.

de762d60-c903-57cf-bc84-0eeb2eadec27.description: Civil war, known as the Wars of the Roses, breaks out between the rival royal houses of Lancaster and York, marked by the First Battle of St Albans.

de8565a1-ea85-51ca-9f3e-c1bff5e6320a.name: Madrid Convention
de8565a1-ea85-51ca-9f3e-c1bff5e6320a.description: In November 1912 the Madrid Convention makes northern Morocco a Spanish protectorate.

de958d36-f511-5186-ad55-a694e77e7543.description: English and Scottish Protestant colonists settle at the Plantation of Ulster in the north of Ireland on land confiscated from Irish Catholic landowners.

deb262b8-eae7-5330-a52e-db83f321553d.name: First World War
deb262b8-eae7-5330-a52e-db83f321553d.description: The duration of World War I.

debccaa7-c112-539c-9761-c664285d1e7e.description: Anti-Habsburg revolution and freedom fight (from March 15) led by Lajos Kossuth. Independent Hungarian government (Prime Minister: Count Lajos Batthyány). Hungarian victory in the battle of Pákozd.

dec2255f-859a-5ea4-b21c-046b469c315e.description: Umberto I (1878–1900) is assassinated by the anarchist Gaetano Bresci. He is succeeded by his son Victor Emanuel III (1900–46).

dec494c3-1b67-5083-9f8f-22fe01a9c778.name: USA declaration of war on the German Empire
dec494c3-1b67-5083-9f8f-22fe01a9c778.description: The United States declares war on the German Empire.

ded926c2-f3e7-596b-bc2f-c6569f079b40.name: Bab-i Ali coup
ded926c2-f3e7-596b-bc2f-c6569f079b40.description: 23 January: Bab-ı Ali coup d'état in the empire (Turkish: Bâb-ı Âlî Baskını) results in Grand Vizier Kamil Paşa being driven from power and replacement of Minister of War Nazım Paşa by İsmail Enver. Effectively ending the London Peace Conference, it marks a significant point in the Ottoman government's progress towards centralisation, giving de facto power to the triumvirate known as the Three Pashas.

df10ab15-72a2-575f-aaea-0e1c635a99fd.description: Peace of Augsburg: failure of the imperial policies of Charles V.

df480296-e505-5591-b42e-51a9b97477e7.description: The completion of the Great Mosque of Ahmad ibn Tulun, which features many innovative elements in Islamic architecture. Annexed to it was a bimaristan (hospital) to treat the poor and it also served as a shelter for the disabled.

df91e41a-78ac-53b4-93f5-9d311ce78485.description: The Battle of Varna: Sultan Murad II defeats the Hungarian army. King Ulaslo I dies but commander-in-chief János Hunyadi survives. Stripes and a double cross first appear together in Hungary’s coat of arms.

df995303-878c-5e40-99d7-ef78b6593a65.description: Around this time the emporium Birka is founded. This community or small town was situated on a small island in the Lake Mälaren, not far from today’s Stockholm.

dfe631ee-5cdf-519b-9900-189432eb9818.description: The victory of the Byzantine army over the Persian army in the Battle of Nineveh on 12 December, which breaks the power of the Sassanid dynasty.

dff5d537-8122-5251-9a1f-7c0a00f69ebb.description: Founding of the Ottoman governing unit in Middle Slavonia with the centre in Požega. For more than 40 years the governor was Hadži Mehmed-aga who supported Sulayman during the siege of Siget.

e0420d62-68b7-59e0-aa3f-306dd2f7c607.description: First of series of retaliatory raids lead by al-Mansur against the Christian kingdoms of the north, lasting until 1002.

e046f0a4-6fdf-5c32-aff1-fb445b485ba3.description: A trade treaty is signed between Anatolian Seljuqs and the Venetians.

e05c0958-d738-51d3-acad-0a0cf634dd7b.description: Jacques Cœur, based in the south of France, begins profitable trading with countries in the Near East, particularly Egypt.

e1b83e18-7a70-583e-9f1a-ab5c213c38da.description: Frederick Barbarossa (1123–90) arrives in Italy to side with the Pope against the Commune of Rome and the Normans. In the same year, Barbarossa is crowned King of Italy in Pavia.

e205bea0-1c2b-5928-8567-a7336452f9c5.description: Birth of Saint Fructuosus of Braga.

e21b4827-ea94-5fb0-8cf5-de9a45f8e87b.description: Merchants from Amalfi (Italy) construct a huge social institution including a hospital in Jerusalem.

e26c8990-cb4c-5264-a88c-9d3bcba1d94c.description: Olof Rudbeck the Elder publishes his Nova exercitatio anatomica, a pioneering work on the lymphatic vascular systems.

e2787654-cd49-577d-8bc9-13e2b3bd8ef4.description: Sultan Sulyman the Magnificent (r. 1520-66) orders the construction of Jerusalem’s city wall, the citadel and the restoration of the Haram al-Sharif and the water system. His wife establishes a famous foundation

e2946e30-19c8-53fb-8154-96405aa99d19.description: Law separating the Church and the State.

e2a693dd-d5c5-5158-870a-fd111cd2e0a5.name: British support of Greek independence
e2a693dd-d5c5-5158-870a-fd111cd2e0a5.description: The poet Lord Byron epitomises Romantic support for Greek independence from the Ottoman Empire. Over the next century, British opinion wavers between seeing the Ottoman Empire as a force for stability or one oppressing Christian populations – the Armenians and Balkan Christians.

e2ae8c52-993f-523b-8536-a6032f1dfc1d.description: The Marinids annex the Kingdom of Tlemcen, and renovate Mansurah and the Sidi Boumediene mausoleum.

e2c660af-cf37-5e43-bdf9-58206070e022.description: A great famine strikes the country due to the low Nile flood, during the rule of Amir Yazid ibn Hakim al-Mahdi, ruler of the Abbasids.

e2c6e0ff-23b6-51fa-ada1-bc426edb793d.description: Entry of Miklós Horthy (governor of Hungary from 1920) to Budapest as head of the national army ends the 133 days’ rule of a communist regime (Tanácsköztársaság) led by Béla Kun.

e3639455-9b9f-5abe-95de-b7e69fe3fc26.description: On 20 August the Muslim armies overrun the Transjordan highlands. They go on to win a decisive battle against the Byzantines on the banks of the Yarmouk River, which opens the way to the conquest of Syria.

e38eb7bb-c5e8-5f3d-99ac-8bd7b8098123.description: Süleyman Bey, conquering Iznik, declares it the capital of the Anatolian Seljuqs.

e3a06506-4e7a-5b7d-b91d-26b97ef9dd36.description: Charlemagne (r. 768–814) inherits the Frankish crown and becomes king of a large part of Europe and the founder of a Roman, Christian and Germanic empire.

e3a13cad-baca-54cf-8177-5f05cdb89109.description: Several Umayyad palaces are built in Jordan, notably Mushatta Palace with its fantastic façade.

e3a9688d-05ef-5df2-ae69-f916aefdc9f9.name: The Congress of Vienna decides the restoration of pre-Napoleonic monarchies
e3a9688d-05ef-5df2-ae69-f916aefdc9f9.description: The Congress of Vienna decides the restoration of pre-Napoleonic monarchies: Kingdom of Sardinia (Piedmont, Genoa, Sardinia); Kingdom of Two Sicilies (Southern Italy and Sicily), the Papal States (part of Central Italy), Grand Duchy of Tuscany and other smaller states. Much of northern Italy (Milan, Venice, Trieste etc.) is under the Austrian empire.

e41722a0-a639-58a4-abf5-46e09f85eb27.description: Ottoman Empire enters World War I on the German side.

e41e5dce-6445-59c9-bb41-416730136680.description: In February mediation between ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib and Mu’awiya is held at Udhruh in southern Jordan after the battle of Siffin to decide who will be the caliph of Muslims. Mu’awiya wins by trickery.

e450d568-2f2e-5dca-b923-c611fabdfc18.description: In January the inhabitants of Pella sign a covenant with the new Muslim rulers after the battle of Fihl (Pella) agreeing to pay poll and land taxes; the transition from Byzantine to Islamic rule at Pella was peaceful and uninterrupted.

e46b969c-0f8a-501d-a790-8a27a09b62ee.description: The end of Ahmad al-Jazzar, who is succeeded by Sulayman Pasha (1804–19) and then with ‘Abdallah Pasha (1819–31).

e47cdabf-08c6-59c7-ba21-0ad6dba27cc6.description: Szatmár Peace Treaty ends the unsuccessful freedom fight of Prince Ferenc Rákóczi II. Publication of *Harmonia Coelestis* composed by Prince Pál Esterházy, Palatine of Hungary.

e4b020eb-e1db-5203-bd29-56d67c4a279f.name: Freedom of commerce
e4b020eb-e1db-5203-bd29-56d67c4a279f.description: The intention of the trade treaty signed with France in August 1863 is to curb the damaging effects of protectionism and to limit the extent of European penetration but, subverted from its original purpose, it becomes one of the causes of the protectionism problem. The *Dahir* of June 1864 then proclaimed freedom of trade throughout the Sharifian Empire. The conventions of 1856, 1860–1 and 1863 established the legal bases for relations between Morocco and Europe. Europe’s influence then began to grow.

e4df6026-d90b-5d19-9f62-9e85843131a4.description: Publication of El Quijote, by Miguel de Cervantes.

e5124ae0-a507-5d8b-b230-3b31d8a62c50.description: The Scottish Wars of Independence begin following annexation of Scotland (and seizure of the symbolic stone of Scone) by England. Scottish victory at Stirling Bridge is led by William Wallace.

e51306f9-7ebc-5fb3-a8bf-4084a48f8bf0.name: pre-March Revolution
e51306f9-7ebc-5fb3-a8bf-4084a48f8bf0.description: The Pre-March Revolution involves a series of protests, gatherings and disturbances, but by July 1849 the Bundes troops are victorious and the revolution fails.

e52dc1da-d1a9-58d1-bbb9-c3306a1ddfe4.description: Abbasid Caliph al-Mu’tazz appoints Bakbak as governor to Egypt, but Bakbak sends Ahmad Ibn Tulun instead.

e582ada5-0a13-5c75-993f-a679ea3bdad8.name: Uprisings in different parts of Italy for constitutional rule and national unification
e582ada5-0a13-5c75-993f-a679ea3bdad8.description: Uprisings in different parts of Italy demand constitutional rule and national unification. In Rome and Venice, short-lived republics are proclaimed. King Carlo Alberto (Kingdom of Sardinia) grants a constitution and wages war against the Austrian Empire, but he is defeated.

e59d2a50-6c31-57a5-9d6d-2c1277d26e98.description: Treaty of Almizra by means of which Castile and Aragon divided al-Andalus.

e5e3cc5c-5c18-54c0-8aa7-b65207704ff5.description: Queen Christina abdicates at Uppsala castle.

e5ec69f1-3f2a-58a8-9d89-34296fd7ca61.description: Rumour has it that in this year King Hugleikr, possibly from what is Sweden today, was slain with all his men in Friesland by the Frankish, i.e. Merovingian, Prince Theodebert.

e61f57cc-61e7-58bc-afa0-1987b218d783.description: Jordan and Syria submit to the Ikhshidids under Muhammad bin Tughj, the founder of this dynasty in Egypt.

e628c68b-7d57-5eae-8bd7-d5c088e26ac0.description: Foundation of the kingdom of al-Mu‘izz ibn Badis, which splits from the Fatimid Caliphate of Cairo.

e63aeb47-1ac7-53bc-8730-89d528ec45ae.name: The Cent Jours
e63aeb47-1ac7-53bc-8730-89d528ec45ae.description: March–July, the *Cent Jours* (Hundred Days) between which Napoleon I returns to power and then finally abdicates after defeat at Waterloo.

e68564b0-bee0-50d6-9a4d-a76ce24c91d1.name: Kingdom of Sardinia, backed by France, wages war against Austrian Empire and annexes Milan
e68564b0-bee0-50d6-9a4d-a76ce24c91d1.description: The Kingdom of Sardinia, backed by France, wages war against the Austrian Empire and annexes Milan. Pro-unification insurrections in central Italy; Garibaldi leads an  expedition of 1,000 volunteers in Southern Italy. Italy is unified under King Victor Emanuel II (formerly King of Sardinia) as a constitutional monarchy.

e69b3932-a14b-593e-a264-9dfa6ce7d609.description: The monk Stefan becomes the first Swedish Archbishop. The ceremony was in Lund, which was then Danish but is now a town in southern Sweden. Stefan was ordained by the Danish archbishop Eskil on 5 August and Pope Alexander III was among the participants. Stefan’s see was in Uppsala. He went to work immediately and one of his letters from 1165 still exists. This is the oldest preserved letter in Sweden. It is written in Latin.

e6a20dd3-2812-51b6-b796-4a720035fc27.description: The Highland Clearances, where tenants are evicted to make way for sheep farming, result in thousands of Scots emigrating to America, Australia, New Zealand and Canada between 1763 and 1775.

e6d2aa53-98d4-5f8c-a7e3-143688535526.name: Urabi Revolution
e6d2aa53-98d4-5f8c-a7e3-143688535526.description: The ’Urabi Revolution, led by Colonel Ahmed ’Urabi, erupts in February 1879 and continues until 1882. It is the first revolution of the modern age in Egypt.

e6ec5d5c-d3cc-5cec-ac30-bbc47b0c3908.description: The French government supports the Pasha of Egypt Mohamed Ali and helps him to succeed to the pashalik.

e6feeb0d-01bf-59bb-8069-390c3a62f0d3.description: Ajlun becomes the centre of an administrative district (Niabah) extending from the Zarqa river in the south to the Yarmouk river in the north and from the Jordan valley in the west to Badiya in the east.

e72f3a22-2b6d-5269-8bd4-6f8656211e9c.description: The Fatimids restore the Dome of the Rock.

e744318c-cf49-5f17-9561-66e10cc83c25.description: The Abbasids conquer Palestine, which loses its former centrality of rule and investment.

e75d379a-83bf-5514-b8ff-b882a8a1cfce.description: Foundation of the town of Taghrart on the site of modern-day Tlemcen.

e7a0564c-2fde-525e-beda-c6a62ccba83a.description: The Goths attempt to occupy the town of Sebta.

e7db9b2c-691b-5da5-b210-f7ebed29dc84.description: Tanzimat (reformation) period: local Syrian governors are removed from their positions as the Ottoman Empire enforces tighter administration in its efforts towards Westernization.

e7ddb571-6ebb-51ae-a0a7-952796b9090d.name: Revolution in the Romanian space
e7ddb571-6ebb-51ae-a0a7-952796b9090d.description: Revolution in the Romanian countries: in Wallachia and Moldavia revolutionaries demand their countries’ right to self-determination, while in Transylvania Romanians want equal rights to those of the Hungarians and Germans.

e8286945-4b4e-5742-8d29-67d38200b404.description: Prince Géza is succeeded by his son István who continues the Hungarian conversion to Christianity. Following nomadic tradition Prince Koppány claims the rulership but is defeated and killed.

e8443181-9b2b-5076-bbb2-bb68474dcfcd.description: An Umayyad town is established on the citadel of Amman comprising a palace complex, congregational mosque, residential units, a reservoir and a bath.

e86b7e94-46ed-53ef-a3ac-d1cba55b1cf2.name: End of first Saudi State
e86b7e94-46ed-53ef-a3ac-d1cba55b1cf2.description: The third Imam, Saud ibn ‘Abd al-‘Aziz, faces a hostile reaction from the Ottoman Empire through its powerful viceroy in Egypt Muhammad ‘Ali Pasha. After ‘Abd al-‘Aziz’s death in 1814, his son, Abdallah, battles with the Egyptian army in many regions of the state. Finally Dir‘iyya is surrendered, and Imam Abdallah is then taken to Turkey, where he is executed.

e87499ba-1b26-5ebb-a5a6-10553c4b6652.description: Muhammad Ibn Ahmad al-Maqdisi (al-Muqaddasi), the famous geographer is born in Jerusalem.

e8a92eb7-b493-55d1-8d0c-28c26221d3f8.description: Period of internal power struggles in the bey families. The reigning princes manage to ensure the dynastic succession.

e8abfaa9-54c8-5120-85d8-e917550305c1.description: Foundation of the Qal’at Bani Hammad (Algeria).

e8c1dc29-ee34-5f24-a0e2-af9d9bf7af11.description: The Congress of Vienna restores the pre-Napoleonic fragmentation of Italian lands, and the hegemony of the Austrian Empire over the peninsula is sanctioned.

e8d8e9c8-0b8c-505f-9f0e-9f8cd8dbab43.name: Treaty of Kutahya
e8d8e9c8-0b8c-505f-9f0e-9f8cd8dbab43.description: 8 April: Treaty of Kütahya with Egypt. The Ottomans recognise Syria, Palestine and Lebanon as within the sphere of the Egyptian control.

e8e5c1de-5a72-513d-8780-6bd0f9d01843.description: The Muslim armies expand in southern Palestine, and then begin to move towards the north. In the Battle of Yarmuk the Byzantine army is defeated and Greater Syria gradually falls under the control of the Muslim army.

e91e593e-0e93-5e78-9d5a-8ed442a901a4.description: With the decisive help of the Hungarian-Kun army Habsburg Rudolf I defeats the Czech army in the Battle of Dürnkrut (Morvamező). The beginning of the rise of the Habsburgs.

e93c2f30-ccf5-5960-a67a-3e6992627c4d.description: Napoleon Bonaparte’s forces enter Syria. Era of Westernisation begins, which later leads to the collapse of local craftsmanship and local economics in the face of Western industrialism.

e97d88c7-20a2-5221-81bb-69777ec45799.description: Consolidation of Almoravid power in the southwest of the peninsula. Attack on Coimbra.

e9acdfb4-fa2b-5954-8588-5aad2a2cfd48.name: Incorporation of the Ionian Islands to Greece
e9acdfb4-fa2b-5954-8588-5aad2a2cfd48.description: The Ionian islands are incorporated within the newly established Greek State.

e9e2d41f-f69c-5f10-ba54-2a75e470fc69.description: Çelebi Mehmed goes to France as ambassador.

ea03b14b-4d46-52b3-9829-7c5d67ea667d.description: Draught and famine in Egypt because of the low Nile flood and more than 17,500 persons die that year.

ea659014-2186-58a5-8ced-5cd030253cdc.description: Mulay Hafid signs the treaty for the French protectorate in Morocco

ea76b19d-d318-510e-b037-2c49fe133c7e.name: Union of Moldavia and Wallachia
ea76b19d-d318-510e-b037-2c49fe133c7e.description: Union of Moldavia and Wallachia. In January 1859 Alexandru Ioan Cuza is elected ruler of both Moldavia and Wallachia, the double election being recognised by the Great Powers and the Ottoman Empire. In November 1861 the sultan issues a ferman approving the political and administrative union of Moldavia and Wallachia during Cuza’s reign. The United Principalities could now have a single government and parliament.

eb4c1b6e-c0de-56e2-9986-9d964c16dba5.description: Fakhr al-Din II Ma‘n, the powerful Amir of Lebanon, sends his deputy to Constantinople asking the Ottoman Sultan to give him the governorate of Irbid and Ajlun to strengthen his emirate.

eb78e52c-1a04-55f3-8bfd-9c8b44dc2542.name: Capture of Algiers
eb78e52c-1a04-55f3-8bfd-9c8b44dc2542.description: With the capture of Algiers, France ousts the Ottoman Empire and asserts its claim to the western Mediterranean. The beys and the regency’s elite then become aware of the dangers posed by the Europeans.

eb8e4233-bf9c-543b-a7ae-0bf1fd6ca558.description: Sayf al-Dawla al-Hamdani rules Aleppo as an independent Hamdanid emirate. His court poets, Abu Firas and al-Mutannabi, glorify his many raids on the Byzantine frontier.

ebaf3d20-b569-5c17-901d-66c26b5cdce8.name: Bosnia crisis
ebaf3d20-b569-5c17-901d-66c26b5cdce8.description: Austria-Hungary annexes the Ottoman provinces of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Following international protests, Germany shows solidarity with Austria.

ebbd957d-2247-5a2c-a0ca-239a804b4a25.name: Colonial rivalries: the Moroccan crisis
ebbd957d-2247-5a2c-a0ca-239a804b4a25.description: Colonial rivalries: the Moroccan crisis brings about a new raft of trade agreements between the English and the French, with the participation of the Spanish, sharing out Morocco and Egypt, which is greeted with dismay by Moroccans.

ebfeed41-a5b2-5e36-819b-8c972b3aa95b.name: War
ebfeed41-a5b2-5e36-819b-8c972b3aa95b.description: War catches the people by surprise: British troops are fighting the Ottomans on three fronts. They are repelled at Gallipoli, pushed back in Southern Arabia, and British forces are captured in Iraq. By the end of the war these setbacks are reversed and Britain and her allies occupy Constantinople, Egypt, Iraq and the Levant.

ec698fe7-4144-5e90-a847-26e3e1fbe964.description: Establishment of towns. German colonisation. Invasion of the Mongolians (1241). Introduction of mining law (1249), the provincial court (1253) and provincial statutes. The Inquisition introduced (1257).

eca05a52-fc8e-5b80-b48c-17d51aa468e7.description: Pope Kliment XIV issues a bull abolishing the Jesuit order. Establishment of learned societies; compulsory school attendance introduced (1774). Peasant uprisings. Origins of the Czech National Enlightenment. The first history of Moravian art published.

ecde9fa3-39ac-5cad-8542-8c81a363ddf5.description: Ottoman Empire declares bankruptcy. Balkan uprisings.

ed1587b0-9a1e-5ac6-b48e-8198dae5dee7.name: The first French-language newspaper Le Tunisien
ed1587b0-9a1e-5ac6-b48e-8198dae5dee7.description: The Young Tunisians found the first French-language newspaper *Le Tunisien*. Echoes of their militant action are seen in the riots of Djellaz on 11 November 2011 and the tramway accident on 8 February 1912.

ed170053-eb91-5c65-ac00-3c8cea2efc9c.description: Birth of Nikolaus von Kues (1401–64). His De docta ignorantia is notable for his mystical beliefs. He suggested the earth was a nearly spherical shape that revolved around the Sun.

ed3443e2-ad25-5fe5-9e41-af9913c072da.description: Timur-i-Lang (Tamerlane) sacks Damascus and the economy deteriorates; plague and famine are rife.

ed37556c-6a5f-54a0-a270-11ea7b5a1e44.description: The first permanent army, consisting of Swedish peasants, is created.

ed3b30cd-5cda-50bc-887f-5bf8435c4119.description: Preaching of the Third Crusade, which is joined by the King of France Philip Augustus and Richard the Lionheart. Having returned to France Philip Augustus defeats the troops of Emperor Otto at Bouvines and greatly extends his kingdom.

ed6800c0-3445-5557-a755-7876a32b6c4b.description: The decline of the Almohads is deepened by the victory of the Sanhadja tribe from Bani Ghania at Béjaia.

ed825c92-debf-58b2-8d13-a0228b632940.description: Preaching of the Second Crusade, in particular by Saint Bernard. King Louis VII returns defeated to France, and Jerusalem is taken back by the Muslims in 1187.

ed9398cd-7bbd-55a8-8d39-00c64c1b5ccb.name: Coronation of King Carlos I on 10 October
ed9398cd-7bbd-55a8-8d39-00c64c1b5ccb.description: 10 October: Coronation of King Carlos I (28 September 1863 – 1 February 1908) Despite the King’s attempt to reform the political system, the growing urban influence of the Republican Party and the people´s discontent were fostered by cash payments made to the Royal House.

ed94200b-ec0d-532a-bae6-046ab22f6779.description: Dante Alighieri begins his masterpiece of universal literature, the Divine Comedy, completed in 1313.

ee1529ff-b7df-5539-a5a7-a7ac6bfcf20c.description: ‘Abd al-Rahman III lays siege to Beja and Faro. Establishment of the Caliphate of Córdoba.

ee2176b7-39b8-5042-8b19-2e3784ec3be2.description: Edict of the Byzantine Emperor Leon III by which he excluded western Balkan lands, the entire Illyrics, from the authority of the Roman Pope and submitted them to the Byzantine patriarch.

eede12ef-3df3-5d4e-83ac-3847e6efc9f0.description: Ottoman Sultan Murad III ibn Salim Khan orders the renovation of Aqaba Castle; his name is inscribed on a medallion above the inscription which bears the name of the Mamluk Sultan Qansawh al-Ghawri.

ef2ebfed-06be-5790-887c-90f9f186d001.name: The Tétouan war
ef2ebfed-06be-5790-887c-90f9f186d001.description: The Tétouan war of 6 February 1860: the Spanish, seeking to extend the borders of Ceuta and Melilla, exploit a raid by a neighbouring tribe against a redoubt built outside the walls of Ceuta to launch a major military action and occupy Tétouan. To end the occupation of Tétouan, the Moroccan state was obliged to pay a significant sum (20 million douros), which it was unable to do. As a result, it was forced to seek a foreign loan that it was able to pay back using customs revenues.

efc21828-9124-5e11-9771-508147e2ab25.name: Death of King Alfonso XII
efc21828-9124-5e11-9771-508147e2ab25.description: Death of King Alfonso XII. Alfonso XIII born posthumously. Pacto de El Pardo: agreement between liberals and conservatives to rule the country by turns. Regency of Queen María Cristina until 1902 when King Alfonso XIII comes of age.

efddb048-fe19-5c4d-92af-28eb7b156ac6.description: Fire causes great damage to the Holy Sepulchre Church.

efec963a-5aea-52ab-a72c-094cdb7eac97.name: Crimean War
efec963a-5aea-52ab-a72c-094cdb7eac97.description: Russia’s expansion to the Black Sea and the Caucasus encroach on, seize and annex Ottoman possessions. Britain and France support Ottoman resistance, targeting the Russian naval base in Crimea. Britain provides military and naval support to the Ottoman armed force.

f015da88-e24f-5276-a062-4dd49d86cc3e.description: The Almohads take Algiers and Constantine, overcoming the last heir of the Bani Hammad, Yahia ibn ‘Abd al-Aziz (515–47/1121–52) and unifying Morocco and the Central Maghreb.

f0378c93-047e-5f8a-bb0e-8b8246245a72.name: Austrians were defeated by a French and Sardinian Army
f0378c93-047e-5f8a-bb0e-8b8246245a72.description: Defeat of the Austrians by a French and Sardinian Army at the Battle of Solferino on 24 June sees terrible losses on both sides.

f09fa1bf-bd44-53e8-8b1f-61e8de9ab1d1.name: Peace congress of Paris
f09fa1bf-bd44-53e8-8b1f-61e8de9ab1d1.description: At the Congress of Paris peace conference, Wallachia and Moldavia are put under the collective guarantee of the Great Powers (Austria, Russia, Prussia, Piedmont, the UK and France), while remaining under Ottoman sovereignty. The Russian protectorate over the Romanian countries is ended. Moldavia receives the southeast of Bessarabia.

f15b3998-59b7-5b52-a7ce-1a2847f2d9d3.description: Parliament passes the Act of Supremacy declaring the monarch (Henry VIII) the supreme head of the Church of England, and outlawing any act of allegiance to the Pope.

f165063a-aa20-5646-b298-4a2c2325198e.description: The entire Umayyad court is massacred by the ‘Abbasids, except for ‘Abd al-Rahman bin Mu‘awiya who escapes from Syria to al-Andalus (Spain) and founds there a line continuing the Umayyad dynasty.

f195491d-369a-5107-b22f-925f5752f876.description: Construction of the Djama’a al-Djedid mosque in Algiers, the first Hanafite mosque, inspired by Byzantine architecture.

f1bf9f5a-062f-5064-8b4b-e29fcdbc77ad.description: Turks occupy several Hungarian fortresses in the new Turkish wars. At the siege of Eger fewer than 2,000 Hungarians led by István Dobó triumph over the attacking 60–70,000 Turks.

f1eef633-b025-530e-9f24-58caef33da93.description: Establishment of the Czech Academy of Science. K. V. Klíč invents photogravure. The first automobile with a combustion engine in the monarchy (1897); first Czech motorbike and cinema (1898). Widespread emigration to the USA due to the economic depression.

f209ded8-b80a-51ad-ba20-d1c2ab088ec1.description: The Damascene theologian ‘Abd al-Ghani al-Nabulsi, from Sufi order called al-Naqshabandiyya, influenced by Ibn al-Arabi, writes many works on religion and mystical philosophy.

f258c162-5afa-53dc-97a2-1a65f298faba.name: Austria declared war against Serbia
f258c162-5afa-53dc-97a2-1a65f298faba.description: Austria declares war on Serbia in July: she is supported by Russia, France and Britain. Turkey and Bulgaria enter the war on the side of the German–Austrian Alliance.

f2a72779-7feb-5a74-a2f5-dc6daf7807fb.name: The Arab Revolt
f2a72779-7feb-5a74-a2f5-dc6daf7807fb.description: The Arab Revolt begins on 10 June 1916 led by the Governor of Mecca (Makkah), Sharif Husayn ibn ‘Ali, and his sons, the amirs ‘Ali and Faisal. His forces seize the city of Riyad and force the small Ottoman garrison to seek refuge in the local fortress. Another of Husayn’s sons, Amir Abdallah, manages to surround and then take the town of Ta’if.

f2bb5e9a-aa69-5950-869b-6a56797e20ae.description:
Last Mongol invasion of Damascus, by Timur i-Lang (Tamerlane).  
Ibn Khaldun, Tunisian historian in Damascus at the time, pleads with Tamerlane on behalf of the city, but the Citadel is breached and the city sacked.

f2dbfd4a-2937-5639-9f38-c6e1fa8367c4.name: War and status of Mount Lebanon
f2dbfd4a-2937-5639-9f38-c6e1fa8367c4.description: The privileged position enjoyed by Lebanon is ended by the Ottomans in World War I: Lebanon’s semi-automous status is abolished and Mount Lebanon, an important territory at the international level, is put under martial law by the Ottomans. The Turkish commander Jamal Pasha occupies Lebanon militarily.

f2e97bee-ecc2-5dd8-9315-3224384abab6.name: The Austrian republic is founded in Vienna
f2e97bee-ecc2-5dd8-9315-3224384abab6.description: Emperor Charles I renounces his participation to the government of Germany-Austria (Deutsch Österreich). The Austrian republic is founded in Vienna.

f2ea8421-d374-5b7a-8b01-218f5ed21b02.name: Transilvania integrated into the Hungarian kingdom
f2ea8421-d374-5b7a-8b01-218f5ed21b02.description: The centre of present-day Transylvania is integrated into the Hungarian kingdom after the creation of the Austro-Hungarian monarchy. Partium and Banat had already been included in Hungary.

f2eece35-36f2-5ec7-953c-7b250d1a46de.description: Following the Oran earthquake, the Spanish restore the ruined town, which becomes the capital of the beylik of Western Algeria.

f308d5db-d4d9-5f21-bcf6-ac477b078299.description: The architectural features of a new capital founded in Samarra have a strong impact on the decorative repertoire all across the Islamic empire and particularly in Egypt and Syria, as seen in Kharab al-Sayyar and al-Raqqa.

f3489c6a-6edf-534e-9008-63e90c67aa09.description: The old castle Tre Kronor (Three Crowns) in Stockholm burns down.

f36b3e3b-8c78-5b05-b1df-4601084030aa.description: The Treaties of Westfalia end the wars between the King of France and the Emperor of Germany waged since 1636.

f3a4f4dc-7de1-542e-9814-56c1610cb575.description: The English fleet under Lord Howard of Effingham, Sir Francis Drake and Sir John Hawkins defeats the Spanish Armada; war between Spain and England continues until 1603.

f436f770-aaad-5d98-b58f-8a0d4fe080ae.description: On the death of King András III the Árpád house dies out in the male line. Fights for the Hungarian throne ensue. The coronation of Károly I Róbert of Anjou (Caroberto), descended from the Árpád female line.

f44c9645-723a-5045-86ba-4f19c1d7284a.name: Ottoman and Egyptian navy destroyed at Navarino
f44c9645-723a-5045-86ba-4f19c1d7284a.description: 20 October: A joint British, French and Russian fleet destroys the Ottoman and Egyptian navy at Navarino as the Sublime Porte did not accept the declaration of the UK, France and Russia for an autonomous Greece (in the Protocol of London, 6 July 1827).

f4651af3-bcb4-5c95-994b-774c069af48e.description: Roger I of Hautville (1072–1101) begins the conquest of Sicily against the Arabs, which is completed in 1091.

f51633b9-d8de-5098-8516-badfbf827e61.name: Uprisings in different parts of Italy in favour of national unification
f51633b9-d8de-5098-8516-badfbf827e61.description: In 1820–21 and 1830–31, uprisings in different parts of Italy in favour of national unification and constitutional rule. They meet harsh repression.

f562c18f-4d48-50be-8456-fd2d224e24b7.name: The second Saudi state
f562c18f-4d48-50be-8456-fd2d224e24b7.description: Following the events of 1818, the Hijaz returns to Ottoman rule. Then in 1824 the Second Saudi State emerges, led by Imam Turki bin Abdullah, and with its capital now in Riyad following the destruction of Dir‘iyya. Imam Turki is then succeeded by the sons Imam Abdallah and ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Faisal. In ‘Abd al-Rahman’s reign, in 1891, the Second Saudi State falls into the hands of his enemy al-Rashid. This prompts the king to leave Riyad for Kuwait with his family.

f578c08f-29f1-55c0-8c87-480553f9ab97.description: Scotland’s National Covenant is signed; a protestant manifesto, it rejects King Charles I’s attempts to impose an Anglican prayer book as well as other constitutional changes on Scotland.

f596be10-32f7-5725-a5c7-7516ddd7c5c0.description:
Arab nationalists are executed in May by Ottoman governor Jamal Pasha in Marjeh Square, Damascus.  
Sykes-Picot Treaty signed by the French and British imperial forces, dividing the Arab lands.

f5f1cfee-6e24-5a3f-b06b-da4f762dacb5.description: The Mamluk Sultan Qaytbay goes on an inspection tour of the Syrian provinces and strengthens  urban development as Syria is contested by the rising power of the Ottomans in Turkey.

f621f014-fec0-513d-8397-7210af9eceac.description: The first Islamic gold coin devoid of iconographic representation is struck in Damascus by Umayyad Caliph ‘Abd al-Malik, with Arabic declaration of faith. Arabisation of the administration.

f6486cbf-833b-5a9a-b1e5-b99bdf7b38d6.name: The Government of British India administers the Trucial Coast
f6486cbf-833b-5a9a-b1e5-b99bdf7b38d6.description: The government of British India administers the Trucial Coast.

f66036f1-4e15-58e2-b837-641dd3ec6f7e.description: Salah al-Din dies and the Ayyubid empire is fragmented.

f716d2e1-962f-5ff8-ba44-fea6ab9ca023.description: Ibn Askar, author of the hagiographic dictionary *Dawhat al-Nachir*. is born in Chefchaouen.

f71ab877-43a7-52d5-b530-155d15d061fa.description: Battle at Krbavsko Polje after which Ottoman armies overran most of Croatia and Islamisation followed, particularly in the so-called ‘Turkish Croatia’ between the Una and Vrbas rivers.

f726c72d-feb1-51eb-a3f1-4b2046178dc7.description: Emperor Franz Joseph enters the Dual Monarchy with Hungary. Conflicting interests prevent Austria-Hungary from uniting the South Slavs: Croatia and Slavonia fall under Hungarian control, while Austria retains Dalmatia.

f765b2af-f1fc-560b-b967-c8a80d2cefb9.description: The first wave of Eastern European Jewish immigrants settles in Palestine; this is the beginning of several waves of European Jewish immigration to Palestine.

f7817e08-dae7-5dce-a040-441d69b15f83.description: Justinian, the Byzantine Emperor, begins constructing many castles along the main caravan routes, and several churches in Jerusalem, Bethlehem, Gaza and Nabatian Negev.

f79e6586-b41d-5804-8d78-c3f4b0b49da0.description: French expedition and start of the colonisation of Algeria.

f7ed8b5c-10ba-56ca-b0eb-710e579bebb2.description: The Spanish built the fortress at Gibraltar after a failed attempt to take Algiers.

f812d16c-326f-503a-8a09-b382b5cc0904.description: The Dome of the Rock is built as the framework of a large construction programme on the plazas of the Haram al-Sharif, including the Dome of the Chain, the gates of the Plaza and the Aqsa Mosque.

f81f60e8-4b8c-5d37-af44-829a47dc02fb.name: First Republican Constitution enacted in April
f81f60e8-4b8c-5d37-af44-829a47dc02fb.description: April: First Republican Constitution enacted. Manuel de Arriaga is elected as the first President. It is believed that the Republic will address the economic crisis and promote progress. Though bringing together political forces, the regime is too vague to achieve the necessary economic and social reforms and soon ends up in political fragmentation and infighting.

f825be5e-2187-5142-a098-b4609fb91d10.name: Electoral reform
f825be5e-2187-5142-a098-b4609fb91d10.description: Electoral reform: the right to vote is extended to 7 per cent of the Italian population, by lowering the age limit (from 25 to 21) and the level of income required.

f82dac15-a8ae-54bf-b092-872543fb1559.description: Damascene Ibn al-Shatir, a great Muslim astronomer, craftsman and instrument designer, composes important new planetary theories that predate Copernicus by two centuries.

f8996915-8dc8-59b7-9c61-2f9e5f25f5b6.name: Major Sidónio Pais takes power on 5 December and is elected President on 21 April 1918
f8996915-8dc8-59b7-9c61-2f9e5f25f5b6.description: Major Sidónio Pais takes power on 5 December and is elected President on 21 April 1918. Continuous unrest leads to a military coup by General Gomes da Costa in 1926 followed by a dictatorship. António de Oliveira Salazar become Finance Minister (1928–32) and then Prime Minister until 1968. The Estado Novo dictatorship lasted for 48 years.

f8ab46ce-bcc2-511a-850d-f38946c479f9.description: On 5 July Salah al-Din (Saladin) wins a great victory at Hittin over the Christian Frankish troops; he went on to destroy the power of the Crusaders in Palestine and Jordan.

f8e67d66-41cf-5e60-a8c6-7bd5eaf44324.description: John Wyclif, an Oxford scholar, translates the Bible into English from Latin, allowing ordinary people to read it for the first time and inspiring the Lollard political movement.

f94e413e-27b6-5b84-837f-d12f8e7d849a.description: In March several post offices between Cairo and Karak and between Karak and Damascus are erected during the Mamluk sultanate of Barquq.

f95ef00d-5881-5f23-a0a7-97d8a4b0ea0d.description: The Fatimids of Cairo take control of Damascus, causing great turbulence. The Byzantines control northwestern Syria (999–1001). Thus Syria is pressured by expansionists on both sides.

f966e949-77bb-5cdd-8109-8790777c61f7.description: Beginning of the Reformation. Luther nails his 95 theses against the abuse of indulgences to a church door in Wittenberg. His translation of the Bible established the basis of the modern German language.

f9b7ced4-fc8e-58c0-8c65-3d4abb460248.description: Zagreb and a major part of Croatia are stricken by plague of epidemic proportions.

f9c9412a-9326-54c1-ac37-5ba1dcfdded8.description: The National Constituent Assembly gives France the unity it needs. The 1791 Constitution establishes a constitutional monarchy, which ends the following year after the events of 10 August and the deposition of Louis XVI.

f9d06f35-e6e9-591b-bfb0-b9bebea912d2.name: The Palestinian Mandate
f9d06f35-e6e9-591b-bfb0-b9bebea912d2.description: The letter from the British Foreign Secretary, Arthur Balfour, to Lord Rothschild in November 1917 offers British support to Zionist aspirations for Palestine to be a national home for Jews. This is internationally confirmed by the League of Nations handing over Palestine to Britain as a Mandate.

fa146fb6-5a64-5ce2-a03a-bcd8beeda8a5.description: The failure of the second siege of Vienna of the Ottoman Army.

fa3f1f07-d3b6-5a96-9e8f-4bcbc686594f.description: A cast of Turkish soldiers (deys) from Istanbul govern the Regency of Tunis.

fa9e3a30-f855-5391-954a-d0a6594bc53e.description: Election of Gábor Bethlen (Protestant Transylvanian prince) as King of Hungary. He leads a freedom fight against the Habsburgs and brings cultural and economic prosperity to Transylvania.

fadb650a-3f77-5e92-8fbf-11335af1ebec.description: First siege of Vienna by the Ottoman Army.

fadf814c-a30e-52d2-8a58-e68572477477.description: Mongol troops return to Central Asia after sending the scholars and artisans of Damascus to Samarqand and massacring the rest of the population. Mamluk leadership is weakly restored. Internal dissent and militias are rife.

fb4279cc-2a2e-5097-8bb9-f0b9e415b75a.name: The right to vote is reserved to a small elite of men
fb4279cc-2a2e-5097-8bb9-f0b9e415b75a.description: The right to vote is reserved for a small elite of men who have certain levels of income and education: only 2.2% of the Italians can vote.

fb446172-097e-5137-9d15-1e91ba397877.description: The Fatimid caliphate defeats the alliance army of Bilad al-Sham, whose ambition was to establish a state for themselves, and dominates southern Bilad al-Sham again.

fb485c98-2fef-5d95-9979-b4759442a502.description: The Almoravids found the town of Marrakesh, heralding the start of a new era in Maghreb and al-Andalus.

fb4893db-de69-5c2c-acb9-9f0032da2e9f.description: Reign of the reformist prince Ahmad Pasha Bey.

fb5706a8-c5d5-59fd-9e3d-856bfba165bb.description: Francisco Pizarro competes the conquest of the Inca Empire (Peru).

fb93aeda-ffde-52d7-a9a2-5207439fd8be.description: March on Rome: the event confirms the rise to power of Benito Mussolini’s National Fascist Party and the beginning of the Fascist regime (1922–43).

fbe2c0cb-c555-56b0-921f-ba012da34ea8.description: Second war of independence: Austria declares war on the Kingdom of Sardinia. The war is initially fought in Northern Italy.

fbea5e27-1a9d-5d68-b467-1d18b4d4ee21.description: Tunisia becomes an Ottoman province administered by a pasha appointed by the sultan in Istanbul and assisted by political-military leaders.

fc0145f9-4901-5066-af76-09df98b21db9.description: Belvoir citadel (Kawkab al-Hawa) is built in a wave of citadel-building all over Palestine.

fc28a94e-ec36-535b-af73-640343430467.description: Bobastro taken and the rebel ‘Umar ibn Hafsun defeated.

fc7da7f1-b6bf-500a-8a58-2f899e4344d5.description: The geographer al-Sharif al-Idrissi is born in Sebta. Half a century later he writes a geography book entitled *Kitab nuzhat al-Mouchtaq* at the request of the Norman King Roger II.

fc9476ee-fd24-5794-8618-07c87f363c41.description: The first Anglican school is established in the city of Salt by Metropolitan Samuel Gobat who established 37 schools in the villages and cities of the region.

fcaa4990-56bd-58ef-9e83-96246178abfd.description: Abbasid Caliph al-Mahdi (r. 775–85) visits Palestine and Jerusalem, ordering restoration of damage caused by an earthquake in 775.

fcc50734-42e9-5c36-b3b6-59ef8a5e7f8e.description: The most devastating plague hits Damascus, handicapping the city and killing 2,000 people a day, as recorded in the chronicles of the Moroccan voyager Ibn Battuta.

fcf06ed2-f35a-5b2a-b4d6-b03e8c7621d3.description: The Saracens establish a base in Fraxinetum, Provence, in the mountains now known as the Maures, staying for more than two generations.

fde54950-5fd5-5b9b-9601-8073f41c898c.description: The Treaty of Northampton officially acknowledges Scottish independence, which in 1320 had been recognised by the papacy following the Declaration of Arbroath.

fe206d6b-72a1-563f-a90c-6f64acd94d31.description: The first printed work issued in the Czech lands: Statutes for the Prague Diocese (Pilsen printing works).

fe23bf96-3929-5f22-88f9-80c3800efe11.name: The German Empire
fe23bf96-3929-5f22-88f9-80c3800efe11.description: The German Empire, a union of sovereign states and free cities, is established under Prussian leadership.

fe3499d5-b4ca-50ce-a116-199c95627bef.description: Death of Emperor Justinian I soon after his construction of the Ibn Wardan fortress in the Syrian desert. The long and intermittent Byzantine–Persian war is refuelled.

fe5f683c-10ed-5a91-b8f4-3f9d2a88fafb.description: Varangians attack Constantinople, the Byzantine capital.

fe803dfc-b069-516e-a06c-06714e3116d8.description: Reorganisation of the Suebian Church by Saint Martin of Dumes.

fed1cb3f-f671-5994-be2b-f4a920bd0e4a.description: During the rule of the Merovingian Dynasty (c. 500–751) Germanic tribes become subjects of the Merovingian Dynasty.

ff240b80-84a8-553d-b0d4-03478e5bfb99.description: Benito Mussolini Fasci Italiani di Combattimento (Italian Combat Groups) in Milan.

ff2f7b63-df5b-5738-8a4e-4afa91239df1.description: Maria Theresa ascends throne (d. 1780). Invasion of the Prussian army leads to inheritance wars over the Czech crown. Unifying style known as ’Pragmatic Sanction in art’.

ff513241-e32b-5b81-a894-322b95dc3362.name: Cuza is forced to abdicate
ff513241-e32b-5b81-a894-322b95dc3362.description: February: because of his authoritative regime, Cuza is forced to abdicate by a coalition of conservative and liberal-radical politicians.

ffe284d1-ac86-5274-8902-0f9ec6a435f3.description: After the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand and his wife Emperor Franz Joseph I leads the Austro-Hungarian monarchy into World War I on the sides of the Central Powers. Beginning of Hungarian aircraft industry.
